chapters.title: Chapter 201 -201-The Survival and Future of Humanity
paragraphs: Daniel stared blankly at that figure gradually disappearing into the distance. It felt as though something had lodged itself in his chest, leaving him so stifled that he could barely breathe.
He suddenly remembered what the Godkin prodigy Kahn had once said back in Heavenscar.
The human race had fled here from the Endless Starfield.
If the Godkin had not granted the human race a place to settle, humanity would still be homeless remnants adrift in the star sea!
Could it be...
Was this the truth?
Was that man with the greatsword the first leader of the human race?
He had walked out from the void, crossed the Time River, and led countless human beings into this universe.
Then...
For the continuation of his race, he had resolutely gone back to face death!
But that greatsword man had been so powerful. Who exactly could have forced him into such a desperate state?
Who was humanity’s true enemy?
Within Daniel’s vision, the scene continued.
The human sages led those human powerhouses through the starry sky, wandering from place to place with no true home.
They suffered countless contemptuous looks and mockery, and endured innumerable attacks and insults.

Some were cheated out of their last remaining resources during trades. Some were seized as hostages while borrowing a passage. Some had not even had time to step out of a portal before they were casually erased by local powerhouses.
Yet the human sages endured all humiliation and swallowed every indignity.
Because behind them were tens of millions of human lives.
At last, they arrived at the God Realm.
It was a golden continent suspended at the center of the star sea, shrouded in holy light and worshiped by all races!
The God King sat upon a Supreme-grade throne, looking down from above at this group of ragged wanderers.
Daniel stood within the residual shadow of that starry sky, watching as the Godkin emperor slowly spoke.
"You exiles wandering between the star seas are stained with the dust of slaughter. You are destined to bear bitter fruit."
The God King’s voice was indifferent, carrying not a trace of warmth.
"The gates of the God Realm will not open for you."
When the human sage heard this, his hands—weathered and covered in scars—trembled as he carefully took out that gemstone from his robes.

Its light was gentle, yet unstoppable, like tens of thousands of golden threads piercing through layer after layer of palace domes before finally falling upon the God King’s face, illuminating his eyes!
The God King’s gaze narrowed slightly.
He saw the surging Strength within the depths of that gemstone.
It was a vast and majestic power like the collapse of a nebula, an ancient remnant settled within the long river of time.
An uncontrollable greed surfaced from the depths of his pupils, like a serpent that had slept for a thousand years suddenly opening its eyes.
That was a supreme treasure left behind by a High Oracle-grade existence!
He thought to himself that if he could absorb it, perhaps the threshold of High Oracle-grade would no longer be so far beyond reach.
This gemstone—he was determined to have it!
However, when his gaze moved away from the gemstone and once again landed on those ragged human sages, that greed instantly turned into deep wariness.
Although these humans were currently weak, they were ultimately a non-human race.
He absolutely could not bury any seed that might one day explode beneath the foundation of the God Realm.
The God King pondered for a moment, then slowly spoke.
"My race holds a World Fragment known as Aetheria."
He paused, looking down at them like a judge overlooking prisoners.
"However, your race is not lacking in strength. That fragment of land may not be able to bear too heavy a burden."
His gaze swept across every human powerhouse present like a blade.
"The Godkin can offer protection—on one condition. You must be willing to have... no more Divine-grade powerhouses!"
The meaning could not have been clearer.
I can take you in.
But your strength keeps me awake at night!
That world cannot contain so many of you—unless you personally break your own spines.
The human sages looked at one another, silent as mountains.
After a long while, the old man at the head of the group took a deep breath.
"Your Majesty the God King, we need to return and discuss this. Please grant us a little time."
A faint, almost imperceptible smile appeared at the corner of the God King’s mouth.
"Very well."
The human sages bowed and withdrew.
The moment their figures disappeared into the light of the portal, the God King suddenly rose and summoned all the Godkin powerhouses.
The candlelight in the hall flickered, casting half of the God King’s face in brightness and the other half in shadow, making him look like an ancient statue.
"If they come again tomorrow..."
His voice was bone-chillingly cold.
"If they refuse to bow their heads, kill them immediately and seize that gemstone."
"As you command!"
The human sages left the God Realm and gathered in a barren star region.
Within the cracks of the void, chaotic winds whipped their robes until they snapped loudly.
"The God King is wary of our strength."
One powerhouse spoke in a low voice, his tone filled with bitterness.
"He controls so many worlds, yet he insists on forcing us into that tiny fragment world..."
"Why don’t we simply seize territory under the God Realm’s rule?"
A young voice rang out, full of anger.
"We cannot."
The old man shook his head, his gaze as deep as an ancient well.
"We are an outsider race. Every inch of land in this universe has an owner, and their roots are intertwined like a web. If we seize land by force, we will surely be attacked by all sides."
"This concerns the survival of our race. We cannot afford that risk."
"His Majesty entrusted the race to us. We must not fail his expectations."
Another person clenched his fists so tightly that his knuckles cracked.
"His Majesty was willing to go to his death for the continuation of our human race. Are we... afraid of death?"
"It is only death."
The old man raised his head, his gaze sweeping over every face present.
There was no tragic grandeur in his eyes, only a nearly indifferent calm.
"Death at this moment is for the continuation and survival of our race."
His voice lowered, like an echo drifting from a deep valley.
The result of their discussion was decided.
Soon, a group of human powerhouses was summoned.
"Take our Divine Souls, along with His Majesty’s gemstone, and go meet the God King."
"After we die, the human race will no longer be a threat to the God King. He will definitely agree."
"What?"
The human powerhouses were filled with terror and confusion.
"No! Without your guidance, the human race will have no direction forward!"
"That’s right! If there really is no other choice, you sages can temporarily leave this universe first..."
"Say no more. Even if we leave this universe, the God King will still be unable to eat or sleep in peace. It is better to make a clean break and completely remove the thorn in his heart."
"Only..."
"We must guard against him going back on his word."
"We need to settle our people separately. If he turns hostile, at least we will not all be wiped out in one stroke."
After the sages finished giving their instructions, they summoned the newly appointed leader.
The old man placed the gemstone into his hands.
His calloused hands lingered for a moment on the new leader’s palm, as though passing on something that could not be put into words.
It was entrustment.
It was trust.
And it was a weight heavier than mountains!
Then, he turned around.
A cold flash of light.
Blood sprayed!
Golden blood froze in the starry sky, turning into cold crystals one after another...
The newly appointed leader knelt in the void. Tears blurred his eyes, but he clenched his teeth tightly and did not make a single sound.
Only the wind howled past his ears.

chapters.title: Chapter 202 -202-Forging a Supreme-Grade Throne with the Flesh and Blood of His Own Race
paragraphs: God Realm.
The God King sat high upon the Throne, looking down at the human leader who had come alone.
The human leader carried the vessels containing the Divine Souls of the sages and held that gemstone in his hands as he knelt in the center of the cold hall.
His head was lowered.
No one could see his expression.
The God King nodded with satisfaction.
"A group of clever people... Only when the human race has no powerhouses left can I finally rest easy!"
He could not help sighing in admiration. The human race was actually willing to sacrifice their own lives without hesitation, all for the sake of securing a chance of survival for their people.
The smile at the corner of his mouth grew deeper.
Only if the human race was weak enough could he sleep without worry!
Even if those human powerhouses left this universe, he would still be restless.
"However, those Supreme-grade powerhouses... are still a hidden danger."
A cold light flashed in his eyes.
"I must find a way to remove the Supreme-grades of the human race and eliminate all future troubles forever."
Daniel stood blankly within that residual shadow.
So this was how the humans of Aetheria had come to be.
The human race’s place of shelter had not been some benevolent gift from the Godkin.
It had been bought with the lives of the human sages.
This was the origin of the humans in the world of Aetheria!
Daniel stood in silence.
Within this residual image of the starry sky, he suddenly understood the true weight behind the words "Flame of Heritage."
Flame of Heritage.
It was not combat technique.
It was not the accumulation of knowledge.
It was the spiritual inheritance of willingly casting oneself into the fire for the continuation of one’s race.
The heritage flame of humanity was the willingness to sacrifice oneself for righteousness.
This was what the new version wanted to tell him.
Daniel was deeply shaken.
He had witnessed that first human leader who bore the greatsword moving forward under unbearable weight, resolutely walking toward death for the continuation of his race.
He had seen those human sages take their own lives as an offering, all so their people could have a place to live.
There were always some things in this world more important than one’s own life!
And to those human ancestors, that thing was called the race!
Daniel’s vision suddenly changed.
If what he had seen before was the opening prologue, then now, he had truly stepped into the world of the instance!
The world of one hundred thousand years ago.
[Notice: The instance has officially begun.]
Daniel hovered in midair, identifying the direction.
He vaguely remembered the location of Luminara City.
Queen Kelly had ascended the throne in that city.
There would definitely be clues there.
He spread his wings and flew toward Luminara City.
However, before he could reach that legendary royal city, he saw a scene that made his fury surge.
Before him stood a human city.
A faint black fog enveloped the entire city like a coiled venomous serpent, strangling it until it could barely breathe.
Countless miserable screams rang out from within the black fog, tearing at the heart.
With a single glance, Daniel could see countless evil spirits slaughtering the entire city inside the mist.
Fragile humans had no strength to resist beneath the claws of the evil spirits. Women and children collapsed into pools of blood before they could even let out a scream.
The human powerhouses were surrounded and attacked by evil spirits dozens of times their number, falling one after another. Blood gathered into streams along the streets.
At this moment, the city had already become hell.
And the perpetrator of all this was hovering above the city.
It was a mage dressed in black robes. His face was as pale as paper, and his eye sockets were sunken, making him look like a skeleton draped in human skin.
He stared excitedly at the human tragedy below, his eyes filled with crazed fanaticism.
"Your deaths are perfectly appropriate."
His voice was hoarse, like a cold wind scraped from a tomb.
"Your blood shall become the steps by which I ascend the Supreme-grade throne!"
"As long as I step into the realm above Legendary-grade, I shall become the first Supreme-grade powerhouse in the history of the human race!"
"When that time comes, the entire human race shall prostrate itself beneath my scepter!"
Whoosh—!
Just as he sank into madness, a figure tore through the black fog and descended into the human world.
Daniel hovered before him, his gaze icy cold.
The black-robed mage abruptly retreated half a step, his pupils shrinking.
"You... Who are you?!"
Daniel did not answer.
He merely stared at him in silence, his gaze unlike that of someone looking at a living creature.
"Why slaughter your own race?"
Hearing this, the black-robed mage showed not the slightest trace of guilt. Instead, he spread his arms, threw his head back, and laughed wildly.
"For Strength!"
"For Supreme-grade!"
"I, Robael, the greatest necromancer in history, am destined to become the first Supreme-grade powerhouse of the human race!"
His laughter echoed through the black fog.
"Those foolish Legendary-grade powerhouses overestimated themselves and challenged Divine Wrath one after another. And in the end?"
"One by one, their souls scattered, their spirits perished, and not even ashes remained!"
He abruptly stopped laughing, his eyes burning with crazed flames.
"Because they never understood what true Strength is!"
"And I—the great Robael—shall use living souls as tinder and dead blood as firewood, forging the wails of countless lives into my crown!"
"Divine Wrath? Heh. That is nothing more than a threshold I must cross before reaching the summit!"
He stretched out a withered finger, his voice suddenly rising, trembling like a curse.
"I shall be crowned the first Supreme-grade of the human race!"
"And you—no matter who you are—are nothing more than another silent skeleton on this glorious path!"
Daniel listened expressionlessly until the end.
Divine Wrath.
What exactly was that?
From the sound of it, it seemed to be a shackle the Godkin had locked around the neck of the human race, specifically to block the path for Legendary-grade powerhouses to step into Supreme-grade.
But why had there not been even the slightest mention of it in the records from his previous life?
He shook his head.
These questions could be understood later.
For now—
He only wanted to send the madman before him to where he belonged!
"You crossed the line."
His voice was as calm as still water.
"You should never have slaughtered your own people."
"No matter the time, anyone who turns their blade against their own race is unworthy of being called human!"
The moment his words fell, a gust of wind suddenly blew over.
It was a kind of Strength that could not be seen or touched, yet truly existed.
Wind.
The omnipresent wind!
Robael’s body suddenly stiffened, and the wild laughter on his face froze into terror.
Because he discovered that he could no longer move!
He could not even turn his eyeballs.
He could not control the Strength within his body that he had been so proud of.
He was like a puppet pulled by invisible strings, and the other end of those strings was held in the hands of that indifferent man.
No!
He roared inwardly, unwillingness and fear completely engulfing him!
Boom—!
A thunderous explosion rang out.
Robael’s body exploded in midair, turning into a blood mist that filled the sky.
He had self-destructed.
But it was not a self-destruction of his own will.
It was a forced self-destruction caused by being controlled.
That arrogant, unparalleled necromancer did not even have time to scream before he was reduced to dust beneath Daniel’s Strength.
Epic-grade Forbidden Spell: Puppet of the Wind!
With Robael dead, the black fog enveloping the entire city instantly dispersed.
Those evil spirits roared unwillingly, but under the sunlight, they melted like snow and ice, vanishing without a trace in the blink of an eye.
Daniel looked at the devastated city and sighed, shaking his head.
He still had to continue forward.

chapters.title: Chapter 203 -203-The Backbone of Humanity, Divine Wrath Descends from the Heavens
paragraphs: Before long, he saw two human experts.
A man and a woman.
Their features bore a faint resemblance to each other. They seemed to be father and daughter.
Daniel did not disturb them. He merely hid in the distance and watched with curiosity.
"Bella, I still remember when you were little. You mischievously lifted a short sword, pointed it straight at me, and asked..."
He paused. A bitter smile surfaced at the corner of his mouth, as though half a lifetime of guilt had been hidden within that smile.
"Everyone else has a mother. Why don’t I?"
"Now, I will tell you the answer. I dedicated my entire life to the altar of Strength, lost myself in the pursuit of that illusory peak."
"Your mother could not endure a man who would forever turn his back on his family. So after you were born, she turned and left, never looking back again."
Bella remained silent.
Her eyes reddened, tears surging in them.
Her father continued speaking, his voice calm as still water.
"Do you know, my child?"
"I once thought that climbing to the peak of Strength was the most difficult trial in this world."
"But I was wrong."
"It turns out there are things far more difficult than that."
He laughed softly. In that smile, there was only the relief of a man who had weathered endless hardship.
"When you were hungry, I did not know. When you were cold, I did not know. When you fell ill, I still did not know."

"In order to let you live a little better, I lowered my head and sought advice from the women I had never once looked at properly before. I learned how to hold you, how to feed you, how to mend your clothes."
"And in the blink of an eye, you have already reached the peak of legendary-grade."
He looked at his daughter, his eyes filled with pride.
That pride was like an old blacksmith gazing upon a sword he had exhausted his entire life’s effort to forge.
"I, your father, have clung to life for many long years. Those of my generation were reduced to dust and scattered souls beneath Divine Wrath long ago. Even their names were never remembered."
"Even those who came after us, those younger than me, challenged Divine Wrath one after another—yet all of them died."
The man suddenly rose to his feet. In those cloudy eyes, a scorching light suddenly ignited.
"I once thought only fools would attempt to break through the threshold of supreme-grade."
"Supreme-grade... what is there to yearn for?"
He looked at Bella with reluctance, a bitter smile etched across his face.
"But now, it is your turn."
"I have lived a cowardly life. Whether toward you or toward the human race, I have never made the slightest contribution."
He straightened his back.
"Today, your father will block the edge of Divine Wrath for you."
"And help you fulfill your dream."
Bella’s entire body trembled. Her tears finally burst from her eyes.
She shook her head desperately, but she was choking too hard to utter a single word.
"My child."
Her father smiled brilliantly, his smile like the final ray of sunlight in the dusk.
"When you were young, you complained that everyone else’s father was a hero, and only I was the exception..."
"Now... please give me one chance to be a hero. Even if I am only your hero!"
Bella could no longer hold herself back. She cried out hoarsely.
"No!"
"I don’t want to advance to supreme-grade anymore!"
"Father, I only want you to live!"
But the man shook his head firmly, his gaze as hard as iron.
"You must become supreme-grade."
"Your dream is to become the first supreme-grade of the human race."
"You said you wanted to follow Queen Kelly’s example and light a torch for humanity."
"You said you wanted to protect this race, to protect those who are still struggling in the darkness."
His voice echoed in the wind.
Boom—!
His aura suddenly surged upward like a flood bursting through a broken dam, pouring forth without restraint.
Buzz, buzz, buzz—!
The wind and clouds changed color.
That was the sign of breaking through to supreme-grade.
That was the horn of mortals declaring war against gods.
"Father!!!"
Bella roared hoarsely. In that voice, there was despair, and also love and pain beyond words.
The man turned around and looked up at the firmament.
"My child, you protect the human race."
"And I..."
He stretched out his hand. His thin, withered fingers were like the tip of a spear thrusting toward a divine throne.
"Only need to protect you!"
"Divine Wrath, come!"
At this moment, Bella’s aura also climbed to its peak.
Tears blurred her vision, but she saw it.
The father she had once thought was never tall enough was, at this moment, taller than mountains and brighter than stars.
Boom!
Boom!
Rumble...!
The sky exploded apart.
A long sword glowing with golden light pierced through the heavens.
That sword tore through space, dragging countless spatial fragments behind it. It was like a falling sun suddenly descending!
Every hair on Daniel’s body stood on end.
An indescribable pressure made his heart pound violently.
That aura was stronger than supreme-grade.
It was...
The aura of a Divine-grade expert!
That sword was actually the Strength of Divine-grade!
Was this the truth of Divine Wrath?
Were those human experts who dared to break through to supreme-grade challenging this kind of Strength?
The sword light was like a blade of judgment, sweeping straight toward the father and daughter.
The father straightened his hunched spine, gripped his weapon tightly, and glared furiously at the golden radiance descending from the sky.
"Shatter for me—!"
Shatter!
Boom!!
Crack—!!!
He ignited every Immortal Singularity within his body, as if he had pressed an entire star into his chest.
Flames burst out from the gaps between his bones, transforming his entire body into a meteor burning with golden fire.
He shot into the sky.
The sword light pierced through his body without the slightest hesitation.
There was no collision. No stalemate.
Only a dull sound of penetration, like the echo of an ancient bell being struck upon a desolate plain.
Golden blood exploded from his wound, blooming into one fleeting flower after another in the void.
The sword light did not stop.
It passed through the father, then swept mercilessly over Bella.
"Father..."
A bleak smile appeared on Bella’s face.
There was no fear in that smile, only an indescribable sense of release.
Her voice was very soft.
Her gaze followed her father’s figure.
That figure was disintegrating within the sword light, turning into countless tiny points of radiance that drifted away.
And her own body also began to vanish at that very moment.
Starting from her fingertips, bit by bit, she turned into nothingness.
The two of them were slain one after the other.
It took no more than a single breath.
That sword was like judgment itself, appearing and vanishing in an instant.
Divine Wrath dissipated.
The human race still had no supreme-grade!
Daniel stood frozen in place, staring blankly at that empty stretch of sky.
Wind blew from afar, passing through the void that had been plowed open by the sword light, as though seeing off the father and daughter who had vanished.
He suddenly understood.
What the God realm had locked away was not merely humanity’s path to supreme-grade.
What they had locked away was all of humanity’s hope, dignity, and future!
They...
They had actually stooped to such despicable depths!
They had treated a group of exiles, who sought nothing more than a place to survive, in such a way!
Daniel’s eyes were cold as ice.
He slowly clenched his fists. His knuckles let out crisp cracking sounds.
At this moment, he said nothing.
But within those eyes, an oath had already been written.
That golden colossal sword descending from the firmament hung mercilessly above the throat of humanity’s fate, cold and ruthless.
Whenever a human expert sought to rise to supreme-grade, Divine Wrath would descend, severing all hope with a single strike.
That sword was a sacred artifact.
Slaying human experts was all too simple for it, without the slightest trace of mercy.
Yet the flames in Daniel’s chest burned ever fiercer.
He did not stop. He continued flying in the direction of Luminara City.

chapters.title: Chapter 204 -204-The Second Heaven-Sundering War
paragraphs: Luminara City.
Within Daniel’s field of vision, the outline of that city gradually became clear.
Although it was far from the majestic grandeur it would possess a hundred thousand years later, it was still much larger than he had imagined. Faintly, it already carried the shadow of a mighty city.
Its city walls towered high. Watchtowers stood like forests. People flowed through the streets in endless streams.
He descended into the city, only to happen upon a grand event.
At this moment, within Luminara City, a towering platform rose from the earth.
It stood ten thousand meters tall, piercing straight into the clouds, as though it sought to stab through the firmament itself.
Hundreds of figures were flying in from every direction, gathering toward that high platform.
Those people all wore solemn expressions. Even when they saw one another, they merely nodded slightly, as if they had long since reached some indescribable tacit understanding.
Daniel silently blended among them and landed in a corner.
He glanced sideways at a powerful figure who had just taken a seat beside him and asked in a low voice, "What are you all doing here?"
That expert looked at him in surprise and sized him up from head to toe.
"We were all invited here to participate in the second Heaven-Sundering. Don’t tell me Your Excellency does not even know about such a major event?"
Heaven-Sundering!
Daniel’s heart trembled.
What tremendous boldness!
He suppressed the waves in his heart and deliberately asked in confusion, "Invited? Invited by whom?"
"Why sundering the heavens? And why is this the second time?"
That string of questions stunned the expert somewhat. He once again examined Daniel seriously.
"Your Excellency... are you truly a human expert? You are not someone from the non-human races in disguise, are you?"
Daniel smiled and shook his head. "I have been in secluded cultivation for many years. I truly do not know the current state of the human race."
The man came to a sudden realization, and most of the vigilance in his expression faded.
Legendary-grade experts possessed long lifespans. It was common for them to enter secluded cultivation for hundreds or even thousands of years at a time.
Thinking of this, he felt relieved.
The expert slowly began to speak, his tone carrying a hint of age and hardship.
"Ever since Queen Kelly appeared out of nowhere ten thousand years ago, our human race rapidly rose on Aetheria and became a powerful force."
"Queen Kelly is one of the Three Human Monarchs, yet the territory she alone controls is broader than the domains of the other two monarchs combined!"
A look of pride appeared on his face, but his tone abruptly shifted.
"However, standing behind those other two monarchs are the Godkin—the true rulers of this continent."
"The God realm wanted to drive those two monarchs into a decisive battle against Queen Kelly."
Hearing this, Daniel’s brows furrowed tightly.
The Godkin wanted to provoke a civil war among humans?!
No matter who won or lost, it would be human blood that was shed.
As for the God realm, they would not lose a single soldier. They only needed to watch coldly from the sidelines.
What a sinister scheme.
The expert gave a cold laugh. "But the Godkin underestimated the unity of us humans!"

"How could those two monarchs slaughter their own kind for the private interests of the Godkin? They complied outwardly while defying them in secret, maneuvering openly and covertly, always refusing to truly raise their blades."
"But because of that, they provoked the wrath of the God realm."
"And so, the God realm sent down Divine Wrath."
Divine Wrath.
Daniel instantly understood.
So this was how Divine Wrath had come about.
It was the impotent rage of the God realm, and also the shackle they had placed upon humanity.
As long as the human race had no supreme-grade experts, they would never be able to stir up a true storm.
The expert sighed and continued, "Once Divine Wrath appeared, our human race had no more supreme-grade experts."
"Five years ago, Queen Kelly launched the First Heaven-Sundering War!"
Daniel’s heart shook.
Kelly...
She actually had such courage?!
To use such meager strength to resist the gods.
But how could she not know? If the human race could not even withstand Divine Wrath, how could they possibly fight the entire God realm?
That was almost no different from a moth flying into a flame.
Yet that fierce and unyielding courage was enough to shake the past and illuminate the present.
No matter how powerful the enemy was, she had never once thought of retreating.
Daniel shook his head and asked in a low voice, "What happened afterward?"
"The First Heaven-Sundering was personally led by Queen Kelly."
The expert’s voice grew heavy. "I still remember the grandeur of that day."
"Almost every powerful expert of the human race came. There were more than five hundred of them."
"But Queen Kelly dismissed everyone. She said she wanted to leave seeds behind for the human race."
"In the end, she only brought a handful of old subordinates and charged into the God realm."
Only a handful of people?!
Daniel clenched his fists.
She had clearly known that there would be no return from that journey.
So from the very beginning, she had never planned to come back alive?
"And after that?" Daniel pressed.
The expert smiled bitterly. "After that... Queen Kelly vanished without a trace. Some say she died in battle. Others say she was imprisoned by the God realm."
"In short, the First Heaven-Sundering War ended just like that."
So this was how Kelly had disappeared.
Daniel took a deep breath, suppressed the emotions surging inside him, and asked, "Then what is this Heaven-Sundering about?"
"This Heaven-Sundering was initiated by the new leader of the human race, Natasha."
The expert said slowly, "She is the child Queen Kelly adopted. Among the legendary-grade experts of the human race, she enjoys considerable prestige."
"The path Natasha seeks is not the same as Queen Kelly’s."
"Her Majesty the Queen sought to tear apart the ancient shackle between gods and humans. Natasha, however... only wants to shatter the Sword of Divine Wrath hanging over the heads of the human race."
Daniel nodded slightly. "She wants to destroy Divine Wrath?"
"That’s right."
A faint smile appeared on the expert’s lips.
Daniel shook his head. "Divine Wrath is probably not so easy to break."
"Of course."

The expert smiled. "Precisely because of that, Natasha has decided to borrow the Strength of a magic formation, gathering the will and Strength of hundreds of legendary-grade experts. United as one, we will resist that Divine Wrath together."
A magic formation?!
Daniel’s gaze flickered slightly.
That was indeed a path worth trying.
If one faced that holy sword alone, then no matter how powerful one was, it would be nothing more than flying into the flames.
But if hundreds of people united their hearts and wove their Strength together into a shield, perhaps...
Perhaps they truly could seize a sliver of hope beneath the edge of that sword of divine punishment.
However, whether that magic formation could truly bear such a heavy responsibility remained unknown.
While Daniel was deep in thought, several hundred more figures tore through the air from the horizon, landing one after another upon the high platform.
A moment later, a woman clad in azure robes appeared in the air.
She was Natasha.
However, the instant Daniel saw her face clearly, his entire body froze on the spot.
He knew this woman!
Before he had discovered the special instance known as the [Flame of Heritage], he had once encountered a young girl by chance beneath the night sky.
That young girl had been within arm’s reach of him, yet it had been as if an invisible fog separated them, as though she stood within the crack of another time and space.
In the end, that girl had removed the bracelet from her wrist and tossed it at his feet.
And it was because of that bracelet that he had been able to enter the [Flame of Heritage] instance.
The Natasha before his eyes was astonishingly that very same young girl!
Daniel quickly recovered from his shock.
He seemed to have faintly touched the outline of some kind of fate.
The shuttle of destiny wove back and forth, forming a net no one could unravel.
Back then, Kelly had been nothing more than a sacrifice waiting to die in Soul Devouring Vale. It was because of his appearance that she had climbed step by step to the throne and become Queen Kelly.
Yet Natasha, the orphan Queen Kelly had adopted, was precisely the one who guided him to meet Kelly.
All of this seemed like a cycle!
Daniel shook his head and pressed those chaotic thoughts deep into his heart.
The matter before him was the true priority.
Queen Kelly’s First Heaven-Sundering War had ended with her disappearance.
And now, Natasha was about to launch the second—
No one could predict how this would end.
Daniel silently clenched his fists.
It was time to act.
He wanted to see with his own eyes just how terrifying that so-called Sword of Divine Wrath truly was!

However, the instant Daniel saw her face clearly, his entire body froze on the spot.
He knew this woman!
Before he had discovered the special instance known as the [Flame of Heritage], he had once encountered a young girl by chance beneath the night sky.
That young girl had been within arm’s reach of him, yet it had been as if an invisible fog separated them, as though she stood within the crack of another time and space.
In the end, that girl had removed the bracelet from her wrist and tossed it at his feet.
And it was because of that bracelet that he had been able to enter the [Flame of Heritage] instance.
The Natasha before his eyes was astonishingly that very same young girl!
Daniel quickly recovered from his shock.
He seemed to have faintly touched the outline of some kind of fate.
The shuttle of destiny wove back and forth, forming a net no one could unravel.
Back then, Kelly had been nothing more than a sacrifice waiting to die in Soul Devouring Vale.
It was because of his appearance that she had climbed step by step to the throne and become Queen Kelly.
Yet Natasha, the orphan Queen Kelly had adopted, was precisely the one who guided him to meet Kelly.
All of this seemed like a cycle!
Daniel shook his head and pressed those chaotic thoughts deep into his heart.
The matter before him was the true priority.
Queen Kelly’s First Heaven-Sundering War had ended with her disappearance.
And now, Natasha was about to launch the second—
No one could predict how this would end.
Daniel silently clenched his fists.
It was time to act.
He wanted to see with his own eyes just how terrifying that so-called Sword of Divine Wrath truly was!

chapters.title: Chapter 205 -205-The Predecessors Plant the Trees, the Descendants Enjoy the Shade
paragraphs: Upon the high platform.
Natasha stood before the crowd, her gaze sweeping across the hundreds of powerful experts present.
She looked over each face one by one. Her gaze paused on Daniel for an instant, then calmly moved away.
Daniel’s eyes shifted slightly.
It seemed Natasha did not recognize him.
Most likely, the Natasha he had encountered that night had belonged to another time and space, not the Natasha of this timeline.
After figuring this out, Daniel waited quietly, wanting to see exactly what Natasha intended to do.
Natasha withdrew her gaze and slowly drew the long sword at her waist.
Clang!
The tip of the sword pointed toward the firmament.
Her voice was cold and clear, yet carried an unquestionable determination.
"I have summoned all of you here today for one purpose only—to destroy Divine Wrath!"
"Until that goal is achieved, we will not stop!"
She paused, then said loudly, "Although Divine Wrath is powerful, after studying it for a long time, I have finally found a way to break it."
"And that is—the Energy-Gathering Magic Formation."
A faint smile appeared on Natasha’s lips, her gaze burning bright.
"We only need to gather three hundred legendary-grade experts and use divine energy to combine our Strength. By burning our Immortal Singularities, we can condense a Divine Domain!"
The moment her words fell, the high platform erupted into commotion.
Divine Domain!
That was the symbol possessed only by supreme-grade experts.
The human race had once had supreme-grade experts before, and the ancient records stated it clearly—supreme-grade experts possessed Divine Domains.
If they truly could condense the power of three hundred legendary-grade experts and forge a Divine Domain, then perhaps they really could contend against Divine Wrath!
Immediately, an expert asked loudly, "Lady Natasha, that Divine Domain... what level can it reach?"
Divine Domains were also divided into different grades.
If it was only slightly stronger than a legendary-grade expert, then what use would it be?
Natasha’s gaze was like a torch as she spoke each word with absolute clarity.
"High supreme-grade."
Hiss—!
Sounds of people sucking in cold breaths rose one after another.
High supreme-grade!
That was already terrifyingly powerful.
The faces of the gathered experts revealed excitement and anticipation.
But immediately after, someone else asked, "How many Immortal Singularities need to be burned?"
Immortal Singularities were the foundation of legendary-grade experts.
Their quantity and quality determined everything.
Natasha fell silent for a moment, then slowly spoke.
"Once the Energy-Gathering Magic Formation I have studied is activated, it cannot be stopped. The burning of Immortal Singularities will continue... until death."
Boom—!
The high platform instantly burst into an uproar.
This—this was sacrifice!
The sacrifice of three hundred legendary-grade experts’ lives!
No wonder it could condense a high-grade supreme-grade Divine Domain. So it was fueled by life itself.
The experts looked at one another, hesitation and fear flashing through their eyes.
Natasha clenched her teeth. Her voice trembled, but it remained firm.
"For the sake of this magic formation, for the sake of shattering the sharp sword hanging over humanity’s head, I am willing to offer up my own life."
Her voice was not loud, yet it struck a crack into the heart of every person present.
"All I ask—is that we destroy Divine Wrath!"
Her gaze was as firm as a boulder.
"In war, there must always be those who bleed. There must always be those who sacrifice. Then let it begin with me."
The instant her words fell, a bold and heroic voice exploded like thunder.
"Good! Count me in, Meller!"
A burly man suddenly rose to his feet.
His gaze swept across everyone present. His voice was like a great bell, shaking even the runes on the high platform until they trembled slightly.
"Perhaps some of you have not yet reached the peak. Perhaps for now, you have no intention of breaking through, and you still have a way out—I understand."
He sneered, and his voice abruptly rose.
"But one day, you will come to that threshold!"
"Even if it is not you yourself, it may be your own flesh and blood, your closest friend who has gone through life and death with you, or the student you poured your heart into teaching!"
"When they break through their shackles and are slain by a single strike from Divine Wrath, how will you face the blood scattering across the sky?"
His voice echoed in the wind.
"The God realm thinks that with a mere Sword of Divine Wrath, they can force our human race to crawl on the ground forever? Dream on!"
"Do not let the God realm look down on us, and do not let our descendants point at our tombstones and mock us!"
He glanced at Natasha and said loudly,
"Do not let future generations say that we grown men were not even as brave and fierce as a woman!"
Those words were like boiling oil poured into raging flames, instantly igniting the fire in the chest of everyone present.
"Count me in!"
Another expert stepped forward, his eyes reddened. "Our deaths today are so countless human descendants in the future can step onto the stairs of supreme-grade!"
"If we retreat in this battle, then in the future, those slain by Divine Wrath will be our children and grandchildren!"
"The sages once said—the people of today plant trees so the people of tomorrow may enjoy the shade. Are we going to disgrace the sacrifices of our ancestors?"
One expert after another stood up.
"Count me in! It’s only death!"
"I have lived long enough. If, at the very end, I can contribute a portion of Strength for the future of humanity, then this life has not been in vain."
"Count me in as well."
They knew that the moment they stood up, they were stepping onto a road of no return.
Their Immortal Singularities would be drained dry. Their flesh and blood would be devoured by the magic formation. Perhaps not even ashes would remain.
But they still stood up.
In this world, who did not fear death?
Of course they were afraid.
But there were always certain things more important than one’s own heartbeat, one’s own breathing, one’s own life.
Some lived for resources. Some lived for authority. Some lived for family.
And today, they chose their race!
To die for their race, to die for countless human descendants who had yet to be born...
It was worth it!
Upon the high platform, more than two-thirds of the experts suddenly rose to their feet.
Far more than three hundred.
The blood and spirit of humanity had never been extinguished!
As long as that spirit remained, the human race would never perish.
Natasha selected three hundred experts from among them and personally arranged the magic formation that carried all their hopes.
Runes lit up one after another beneath her fingertips, like stars being ignited one by one in the night sky.
All that remained was to wait for Divine Wrath to descend.

Then they would ignite the Immortal Singularities of three hundred legendary-grade experts, condense the legendary Divine Domain, and fight a decisive battle against the sharp sword that had hung above humanity’s head for countless years.
Daniel witnessed all of this, silently clenching his fists.
This world was so unfair, so dark!
The strong ruled everything, arbitrarily judging and toying with the weak!
Strength was the only language that could travel freely through this world.
He had long since understood this truth, and so he had never stopped pursuing Strength.
To defeat everything—that was the deepest long-cherished wish buried in his heart.
He continued watching the situation on the platform.
Natasha nodded slightly toward a peak legendary-grade expert.
That expert wore a look of grim determination and released all of his aura with a boom.
His momentum climbed higher and higher, like an ancient sword slowly being drawn from its sheath, until it reached its peak.
At that very moment—
Buzz, buzz—
A low hum suddenly echoed between heaven and earth, like the growl of an ancient beast awakening in the abyss.
Whoosh!
A long sword shining with brilliant golden light suddenly descended, wrapped in an overwhelming, unmatched might!
Divine Wrath had arrived.
Natasha was just about to give the order to ignite their Immortal Singularities.
Suddenly, a figure appeared out of thin air before the long sword.
The aura radiating from that person was unparalleled, like an peerless blade being unsheathed.
Daniel had made his move!

chapters.title: Chapter 206 -206-Clashing Head-On with Divine Wrath and Coming Out Unscathed?
paragraphs: Facing that Sacred Artifact–grade Sword of Divine Wrath, Daniel’s expression did not ripple in the slightest.
It was as if what approached him was nothing more than a breeze brushing past his face.
Hiss—
Wherever the divine sword passed, space shattered inch by inch, like a parchment scroll being torn apart.
If he were struck by it, he would inevitably be ground into dust by those fractured spatial rifts.
Boom—
Daniel resolutely burned his Immortal Singularity.
Golden flames rose from his body, as though he had draped himself in a cloak woven from blazing fire, snapping and roaring in the air.
When Natasha saw this, she cried out in alarm, "Wait!"
The hundreds of powerful figures also stared at that silhouette in astonishment.
The expert who had spoken with Daniel earlier was especially stunned. His mouth hung open, and he could not utter a single word.
Daniel slowly clenched his fist.
His voice was low, yet it seemed to carry some irresistible decree.
"Light."
On his fist, light began to shine.
That light was so blazing that it could not be looked at directly, as though a scorching sun had been grasped in his palm.
In that instant, he stacked tens of millions of skills upon one another. His MP was drained in a flash, only to be fully restored in the next breath by [Eternal Sacred Heart].
The light around his fist grew brighter and brighter, fiercer and fiercer.
In the end, it transformed into a black sun!
The radiance was far too intense. Even the surrounding space could not bear it and collapsed with a thunderous crash, forming an abyss that devoured everything.
"Be destroyed!!!"
Buzz!
Rumble—!
Daniel charged forward of his own accord.
His fist collided violently with that holy sword.
The instant the two clashed...
Bang!
Rumble—!!!
Two terrifying forces crashed into each other. The resulting shockwave sent the hundreds of legendary-grade experts on the high platform flying.
Crack!
Kacha—
A fissure appeared on the enormous golden sword!
Immediately afterward, the cracks spread wildly like a spiderweb, dense and countless!
Finally—
Bang!
The divine sword shattered with a deafening explosion!
Divine Wrath had been destroyed!
Sword light scattered in every direction, and fragments fell like rain.
Daniel remained in the posture of throwing a punch, like a frozen statue.
But as the sword light dissipated, his body suddenly began to crumble like sand, disintegrating bit by bit into ash.
Mutual destruction?
No.
In the next moment, Daniel’s figure appeared once again on the high platform, completely unharmed.
He raised his head and stared coldly at the sky.
Above the heavens, clouds surged and rolled.
A semi-transparent face emerged within the clouds, staring down at him just as coldly.
Those eyes were filled with fury and disbelief.
After a moment, the face slowly vanished.
A faint smile appeared at the corner of Daniel’s mouth.
He had done it after all!
As expected of a Sacred Artifact, this Sword of Divine Wrath was no ordinary weapon.
It had to be the natal Sacred Artifact of a sage, containing an immense amount of sacred power.
Let alone a high-grade supreme-grade expert—even a peak supreme-grade powerhouse might not necessarily be able to withstand a single strike from it.
Yet Daniel had not only blocked it, he had forcefully destroyed it, provoking that sage from the God realm into personally descending to spy on him.
"Good thing I had the Immortal Revival buff."
Daniel smiled.
In that instant just now, he had first shattered Divine Wrath with absolute Strength. Immediately afterward, he had been erased by an overwhelmingly terrifying force.
Through that, he knew what it was.
The Strength of a sage.
Sage rank!
That was a level above the Divine Domain!
With his current power, if he faced a sage directly, he would only be crushed to death.
He could not resist it.
He did not even know how he was supposed to resist it.
But so what?
He had long since prepared a backup plan. Even if he died here, it would not matter.
That was why he had not died.
With his own brute force, he had forcibly destroyed a Sacred Artifact!
Divine Wrath?
A sage?
They did not seem to amount to much after all.
This was his first time exchanging blows with a sage. Though it had only been a strike from afar, it had already given him a countermeasure.
At the very least, he would not be erased so easily again.
That counted as quite a valuable gain.
The hundreds of human experts who had been blasted away by the shockwave hurriedly flew back.
Their hearts were filled with shock.
That had been Divine Wrath!
The sharp sword that had hung above the human race’s head for countless years.
The murderous weapon that had slaughtered who knew how many peerless geniuses.
Today, they had personally witnessed a powerful figure withstand Divine Wrath with his own strength and shatter it.
Moreover, the aftermath of his clash with Divine Wrath had been enough to send hundreds of legendary-grade experts flying.
What kind of terrifying strength was that?
Could he be a supreme-grade expert?
But were there still supreme-grade experts left in this world?
Could he be an ancestor who had secluded himself for countless years?
Their minds were filled with questions. Unable to wait any longer, they rushed back to the high platform, eager to see what had happened.
Then, they froze.
Divine Wrath had disappeared!
And that unknown powerhouse was standing there completely unharmed.
Divine Wrath...
Was gone!?
On the spot, some human experts’ eyes reddened, tears streaming down their faces.
One after another, they bowed to Daniel, their voices trembling yet sincere.
"Thank you, Your Excellency, for breaking the shackles of the human race!"
"Your righteous deed is as noble as the stars!"
"Thank you for saving us. The descendants of humanity will never forget this."
"The merit you have rendered for the human race is enough to be written into an epic-grade record and passed down forever, never to fade!"
They had come here prepared to die.
They had been ready to sacrifice themselves, leaving not even intact corpses behind.
Now, they no longer needed to die.
Divine Wrath had been destroyed.
There was no better outcome in the world than this.
Natasha, in particular, bowed solemnly at a perfect ninety-degree angle. Her voice was choked with emotion as she spoke word by word.
"Natasha thanks Your Excellency for stepping forward on behalf of the human race!"
Daniel calmly swept his gaze over everyone.
"I am also human. I merely did what little I ought to do."
When the experts saw that this mysterious human powerhouse was so modest, their admiration deepened even further. They thanked him again and again.
Daniel smiled.
He thought of Kelly.
After the Heaven-Sundering War, Kelly had vanished without a trace. It was undoubtedly connected to the God realm.
Therefore, he had to make a trip to the God realm!
Emotionally speaking, Kelly was the human leader he had personally nurtured. Their relationship was not shallow.
Moreover, his class change quest was to search for clues about Kelly.
Whether for personal reasons or practical ones, he had to go to the God realm!
At this thought, he could not help but recall the face that had appeared in the sky just now.
That sage from the God realm.
Once he set foot in the God realm, he would definitely come into conflict with the Godkin.
The God realm not only had supreme-grade beings, but also sages—and perhaps even existences more powerful than sages!
But Daniel was not afraid.
With the bug-level ability of Immortal Revival on him, there was nothing for him to fear.
"When the time comes, I may not be the one who suffers."
A plan had already formed in his mind.
The only remaining question was this:
How was he supposed to reach the God realm?
Daniel looked at the experts before him.
"I want to find Queen Kelly, but I don’t know where the gate to the God realm is. Does anyone here know?"
Everyone exchanged glances, their expressions somewhat strange.
Five years ago, after Queen Kelly went to the God realm, she had never returned. There had not even been the slightest news of her.
And now, this Excellency actually wanted to go as well?
This would be the second Heaven-Sundering.
The true kind.
Natasha said softly, "Your Excellency, I know how to get there."
She hesitated for a moment, but still spoke.
"However, if you intend to go to the God realm, then you should also understand just how dangerous that place is."
"After Her Majesty Kelly went there, she never came back... I’m worried..."
Before she could finish speaking, the surrounding people began to persuade him one after another.
"Your Excellency, you absolutely must not go!"
"That is the Godkin’s lair! Divine-grade experts are everywhere there, and the security is extremely tight. If you go there like this, how is it any different from walking straight into a trap?"

"Exactly! Just that one Sword of Divine Wrath alone suppressed our human race for so many years. Who knows how many even more terrifying things they still have in their hands? Your Excellency, please think it over carefully!"

Today, they had personally witnessed a powerful figure withstand Divine Wrath with his own strength and shatter it.
Moreover, the aftermath of his clash with Divine Wrath had been enough to send hundreds of legendary-grade experts flying.
What kind of terrifying strength was that?
Could he be a supreme-grade expert?
But were there still supreme-grade experts left in this world?
Could he be an ancestor who had secluded himself for countless years?
Their minds were filled with questions.
Unable to wait any longer, they rushed back to the high platform, eager to see what had happened.
Then, they froze.
Divine Wrath had disappeared!
And that unknown powerhouse was standing there completely unharmed.
Divine Wrath...
Was gone!?
On the spot, some human experts’ eyes reddened, tears streaming down their faces.
One after another, they bowed to Daniel, their voices trembling yet sincere.
"Thank you, Your Excellency, for breaking the shackles of the human race!"
"Your righteous deed is as noble as the stars!"
"Thank you for saving us.
The descendants of humanity will never forget this."
"The merit you have rendered for the human race is enough to be written into an epic-grade record and passed down forever, never to fade!"
They had come here prepared to die.
They had been ready to sacrifice themselves, leaving not even intact corpses behind.
Now, they no longer needed to die.
Divine Wrath had been destroyed.
There was no better outcome in the world than this.
Natasha, in particular, bowed solemnly at a perfect ninety-degree angle.
Her voice was choked with emotion as she spoke word by word.
"Natasha thanks Your Excellency for stepping forward on behalf of the human race!"
Daniel calmly swept his gaze over everyone.
"I am also human.
I merely did what little I ought to do."
When the experts saw that this mysterious human powerhouse was so modest, their admiration deepened even further.
They thanked him again and again.
Daniel smiled.
He thought of Kelly.
After the Heaven-Sundering War, Kelly had vanished without a trace.
It was undoubtedly connected to the God realm.
Therefore, he had to make a trip to the God realm!
Emotionally speaking, Kelly was the human leader he had personally nurtured.
Their relationship was not shallow.
Moreover, his class change quest was to search for clues about Kelly.
Whether for personal reasons or practical ones, he had to go to the God realm!
At this thought, he could not help but recall the face that had appeared in the sky just now.
That sage from the God realm.
Once he set foot in the God realm, he would definitely come into conflict with the Godkin.
The God realm not only had supreme-grade beings, but also sages—and perhaps even existences more powerful than sages!
But Daniel was not afraid.
With the bug-level ability of Immortal Revival on him, there was nothing for him to fear.
"When the time comes, I may not be the one who suffers."
A plan had already formed in his mind.
The only remaining question was this:
How was he supposed to reach the God realm?
Daniel looked at the experts before him.
"I want to find Queen Kelly, but I don’t know where the gate to the God realm is.
Does anyone here know?"
Everyone exchanged glances, their expressions somewhat strange.
Five years ago, after Queen Kelly went to the God realm, she had never returned.
There had not even been the slightest news of her.
And now, this Excellency actually wanted to go as well?
This would be the second Heaven-Sundering.
The true kind.
Natasha said softly, "Your Excellency, I know how to get there."
She hesitated for a moment, but still spoke.
"However, if you intend to go to the God realm, then you should also understand just how dangerous that place is."
"After Her Majesty Kelly went there, she never came back...
I’m worried..."
Before she could finish speaking, the surrounding people began to persuade him one after another.
"Your Excellency, you absolutely must not go!"
"That is the Godkin’s lair!
Divine-grade experts are everywhere there, and the security is extremely tight.
If you go there like this, how is it any different from walking straight into a trap?"
"Exactly!
Just that one Sword of Divine Wrath alone suppressed our human race for so many years.
Who knows how many even more terrifying things they still have in their hands?
Your Excellency, please think it over carefully!"

chapters.title: Chapter 207 -207-Slaying a God? The God of Light Laughs in Anger
paragraphs: Daniel shook his head, his gaze falling on Natasha.
"Back then, how exactly did Queen Kelly ascend to the God realm?"
Natasha knew this mysterious powerhouse had already made up his mind to go. She gritted her teeth and answered truthfully.

"Back then, Queen Kelly used the temples of the various races of Aetheria as leverage. She threatened to sever the Godkin’s faith system and forced them to open a passage. That was how she ascended to the God realm."
Using the temples to threaten the Godkin?
Daniel’s eyes lit up.
Good method!
The reason the God realm could rule over Aetheria was precisely because of the Godkin’s religious orthodoxy.
That was the foundation of their rule.
Severing that orthodoxy was the same as cutting off the roots of the God realm.
As expected of Kelly!
He smiled and said, "In that case, I’ll learn from her this once. I just don’t know where the God realm’s temple is."
Natasha quickly replied, "Your Excellency, every race in Aetheria has its own temple. The beastfolk worship the Temple of the War God, while we humans worship the Temple of the God of Light!"
Daniel understood immediately.
He nodded. "Thank you."
Luminara City stood beneath the twilight, its stone-paved streets glowing with a cold grayish-blue sheen under the fading afterglow.
Daniel flew straight above this enormous city, his gaze landing on the building that had stood there for who knew how many ages—
The Temple of the God of Light!
He remembered that every player who first arrived in the main city could enter the temple and pray before the divine statue in exchange for a temporary blessing buff.
It was just that throughout his journey, his strength had risen far too quickly. He had never taken that insignificant blessing seriously.
But today, what he was looking for was precisely this temple.
Relying on his memory, he soon found its location.
The temple was majestic. Stone pillars towered into the clouds, and on both sides of the main gate stood two statues with wings spread wide, guarding this land shrouded in holy light.
Inside the temple, candle flames burned eternally.
Golden light poured down from the stained glass of the dome, dyeing the entire hall into an ancient painting.
With a slight movement of Daniel’s will, his figure vanished into the void.
In the next moment, he was already standing before the statue of the God of Light.
He glanced calmly at the divine statue that stood a hundred zhang tall.
Its face had been carved in meticulous detail.
Its eyes seemed capable of piercing through all things.
Its right hand looked as though it was about to bestow a blessing, yet also as though it was about to deliver judgment.
Then, Daniel released his aura.
Boom—!
In an instant, all the candle flames in the temple trembled at once.
The eyes of the God of Light’s statue suddenly lit up.
The entire hall began to tremble faintly under that pressure. An ancient and icy will spread through the air.
A voice rang out from deep within the statue.
Deep.
Majestic.
Like thunder falling from the highest heavens.
"You have come."
"You ant who destroyed my sword."
Daniel was slightly stunned.
Then, he understood.
So the Sword of Divine Wrath that had hung above the human race’s head for countless years was actually the God of Light’s own sword?
Divine Wrath was the murderous weapon personally forged by this god.
The corners of Daniel’s mouth lifted slightly, and he gave a cold laugh.
"I want to ascend to the God realm."
A trace of obvious surprise appeared in that voice.
"What do you want to do?"
"Ascend to the God realm."
"Why?"
"To slay a god!"
There was a moment of silence.
Then, the God of Light laughed.
His laughter echoed through the empty temple, shaking the candle flames until they swayed.
It was as though he had heard the most absurd and ridiculous joke in the world.
When the laughter gradually faded, his voice suddenly sank.
"Good!"
"I will wait for you in the God realm."
"Since you insist on seeking death, I do not mind fulfilling your final wish."
The smile on Daniel’s lips deepened.
So ascending to the God realm was actually this simple!
Buzz—!
Space suddenly trembled.
Layer upon layer of ripples spread out before Daniel, circle after circle, shimmering with dark and ancient golden light.
A door slowly emerged from the void!
Dense runes were carved across the doorframe, every line flowing slowly with power.
Behind the door was a bottomless river of stars!
Daniel stared at it for a moment.
He did not hesitate.
He raised his hand and pushed the door open.
Whoosh—!
Light swallowed everything.
[Prompt: You have discovered [God realm]. Contribution Points +10,000,000!]
He stood behind the door and swept his gaze over his surroundings.
"So this is the God realm?"
As far as the eye could see, there were only barren mountains and wilderness.
Yet even though this was merely a remote borderland of the God realm, it still carried an extraordinary presence.
The mountains possessed spiritual charm. The trees and grass were lush and flourishing. Even the wind carried some ancient, vast aura.
The God realm was a true great world.
Its world rank far surpassed the Aerial Realm.
But in Daniel’s eyes, it was still nothing special.
His figure flickered continuously through the void. In just a short while, he had already crossed more than half of the God realm.
Along the way, he quietly left behind hidden measures.
Near every divine city, he hid strands of his hair and left his marks.
The cities of the Godkin did broaden his horizons.

A single divine city was more than a hundred times vaster than the human race’s Imperial City. Countless living beings, numbering in the hundreds of millions, dwelled within. Towers and pavilions rose into the clouds.
What was even more astonishing was that countless non-human races actually lived inside those cities.
They were strange and varied, with all kinds of appearances. There were many races even Daniel could not name.
"As expected of the Godkin who rule over more than a dozen planes."
Daniel could not help but sigh.
However, he had not come to the God realm for sightseeing.
He had come for a "friendly exchange"!
Daniel’s figure hovered in the air, his robes snapping loudly in the wind.
He knew it would not be long before powerful beings came looking for him.
Sure enough.
A moment later, a group of Godkin powerhouses rapidly flew over.
They stopped not far from Daniel and cast appraising gazes at him one after another.
"So this is a human from Aetheria?"
"He looks like nothing more than legendary-grade to me. We’re all supreme-grade. Wouldn’t it be a little too much for us to attack together?"
"The Divine Mentor said this person’s strength is extraordinary. He even destroyed that one’s holy sword!"
"Hiss... That was a sage’s personal sword!"
"Looks like this fellow really isn’t simple. We can’t judge him by ordinary standards!"
"Exactly. We were ordered to come here and kill him. Don’t get careless."
"Then let Vakado, whose strength is around the middle among us, fight him."
Daniel listened expressionlessly to the discussion among these Godkin powerhouses.
These Godkin were all rather young. They wore identical robes, and on their chests was embroidered an emblem shaped like a divine sword.
At that moment, a young Godkin stepped forward from the group.
He looked Daniel up and down twice, then arrogantly raised his chin.
"Godkin, Skyvault Corridor—Vakado!"
Boom—!
A supreme-grade aura suddenly erupted from his body, sweeping outward like a raging gale.
A supreme-grade powerhouse!
Daniel’s expression remained calm as he said indifferently, "Human race, Faustus."
He did not know what exactly the God of Light meant by this.
Could it be that the god thought he was too weak and not worthy of his personal intervention?
The Godkin were indeed arrogant to the extreme.
"Divine Domain!"
Vakado gave a low shout.
In the void, an enormous golden pearl suddenly appeared. Light flowed across its surface, releasing a suffocating pressure.
When the group of young Godkin saw this, they immediately began discussing among themselves.
"Now that Vakado has made a move, this human is dead for sure!"
"It seems Vakado isn’t underestimating the enemy. Not bad. The Divine Mentor said that even when facing an ant, one must crush it with the force of thunder!"
"Of course! You have to remember, our Skyvault Corridor is a supreme-grade academy that has been passed down in the God realm to this day. We don’t have that many arrogant fools."
"Even Vakado, whose ranking is only average, would be enough to dominate an entire region if he stepped outside the God realm."

chapters.title: Chapter 208 -208-The Instantly Slain Genius, Harris
paragraphs: Daniel glanced at Vakado’s Divine Domain, and a relaxed smile appeared at the corner of his mouth.
The aura of this Divine Domain...
It was still far from enough!
"Arrogant fool. You’re courting death!"
When Vakado saw Daniel’s calm and unbothered expression, fury surged in his heart.
Boom—!
The divine pearl carried an unparalleled force as it smashed toward Daniel like a falling meteor.
"Oh?"
Daniel frowned slightly.
He discovered that the surrounding space seemed to have become sluggish.
The wind slowed.
The air froze.
It was as though an invisible hand had seized this entire stretch of heaven and earth.
"Interesting."
A sharp glint flashed through Daniel’s eyes.
The next moment—
"Thunder Abyss!"
Rumble—!
A thunderclap suddenly exploded in the clear sky, as though the heavens had been torn open.
Daniel stacked tens of thousands of skills together, condensing the thunder elements that filled the sky into a colossal palm that blotted out the sun.
Within that massive palm, golden Immortal Singularity faintly flowed.
"Crush it!"
Daniel shouted.
The giant thunder-element palm collided violently with the Divine Domain pearl.
Boom—!
Crack—!
The divine pearl shattered instantly.
Pfft—!
Vakado’s Divine Domain was destroyed, and he immediately spat out a mouthful of golden blood.
However, it was not over yet.
After smashing the divine pearl apart, the giant thunder-element palm was actually completely undamaged. It continued descending toward Vakado with overwhelming force.
Boom—!
Vakado wanted to dodge, but then he saw the giant palm suddenly accelerate.
It was like a mountain descending from the sky, completely covering him beneath it.
Crackle, crackle—!
"Ah—no!"
Lightning raged wildly.
Thunderfire scattered in every direction.
By the time the giant palm dispersed...
Vakado’s figure was already gone!
[Ding! You have killed the Godkin powerhouse [Vakado]. You have obtained [Divine Blood] ×1, [Divine Soul] ×1, [Divine Bone] ×1, [Primal Spirit] ×1 point, gold coins +6.42 million...]
Daniel’s eyes lit up. He immediately began operating the system.
[Ding! You have sold [Divine Blood] ×1, [Divine Soul] ×1, [Divine Bone] ×1, and [Primal Spirit] ×1 to Doom Guild for 1 copper coin, triggering Millionfold Boost!]
[The sold items are special materials. Please choose quality boost / quantity boost!]
"Quantity boost!"
Listening to the system prompt, Daniel chose quantity boost for everything.
Divine Blood, Divine Soul, Divine Bone—
These were all precious materials used to fill the [Reincarnation Sacred Spring].
As for Primal Spirit, that was an even more important resource!
He was still counting on gathering ten billion points of Primal Spirit to deduce that legendary forbidden technique!
[Ding! Congratulations, you have obtained 1 gold coin! You have obtained [Divine Blood] ×1,000,000!]
[Ding! Congratulations, you have obtained 1 gold coin! You have obtained [Divine Soul] ×1,000,000!]
[Ding! Congratulations, you have obtained 1 gold coin! You have obtained [Divine Bone] ×1,000,000!]
[Ding! Congratulations, you have obtained 1 gold coin! You have obtained [Primal Spirit] ×1,000,000 points!]
The moment Vakado died, the young Godkin were all shocked.
Instant kill!
"This human guy really isn’t simple!"
What made them feel even more uneasy was that this person was only legendary-grade!
If he were allowed to break through to the supreme-grade realm in the future...
Wouldn’t that be terrifying?
For a moment, the expressions of all the young Godkin present darkened.
"In the entire Skyvault Corridor, there are probably no more than five people who can instantly kill Vakado in one move."
"Vakado died way too miserably... That human was clearly hiding something."
"Who’s going next?"
"My strength is about the same as Vakado’s, so I won’t go up there and throw my life away."
"Same here. Besides, I still have to control the Void Eye and broadcast the battle details back to Skyvault Corridor in real time. It’s not convenient for me to fight."
"Hmph. All excuses. You’re simply embarrassing the Godkin! I’ll do it!"
Skyvault Corridor.
This was the most prestigious academy in the God realm, with a heritage that had been passed down for countless years.

At this moment, all the instructors and students inside Skyvault Corridor had gathered together, observing the live situation of this duel through the divine artifact held by the young man at the front.
When they saw Vakado get killed instantly in a single move, all the Godkin were stunned. Their expressions looked as if they had seen a ghost.
An instant kill—
Just how powerful did one have to be to do that?
After pondering for a moment, one instructor slowly said, "This human powerhouse is highly skilled at controlling elements. That move just now was a lightning-type ability."
A student raised a question.
"If he controls elements, shouldn’t he be a mage? But why didn’t we see him holding a staff?"
As soon as those words came out, the instructor was directly stumped. For a while, he could not answer.
"Ahem..."
Another instructor hurriedly stepped forward to smooth things over.
"The Endless Starfield is vast. There are all kinds of strange and unusual abilities out there."

"Just because we don’t understand something doesn’t mean it doesn’t exist. In my opinion, although this person is only legendary-grade, he must have used some ancient secret technique to raise the power of his skills to this level."
Only then did the students feel that this explanation made sense.
"Most secret techniques have side effects or limitations."
"Exactly. Then can we infer that this person is good at explosive bursts of power, but not good at prolonged battles?"
"That should be the case. MP will always run out eventually. As long as we can stall him and drain his MP, we’ll have a chance to win."
When the instructors heard the students’ analysis, they were rather gratified.
This was precisely the meaning behind conducting this real-time battlefield observation!
"Let Harris take the next match. He’s quick-witted and strong. He should be able to see through this human’s weakness."
"As long as Harris lasts until his MP is exhausted, he’ll be able to counterkill him."
"In this match, our odds of victory are above fifty percent."
On the battlefield, another young Godkin stepped forward.
His entire body exuded a shrewd aura. His eyes sized Daniel up again and again, like a hunting hawk locking onto a rabbit.
"Godkin, Skyvault Corridor—Harris!"
Daniel did not speak.
Inwardly, he was already starting to feel annoyed.
These Godkin were so tedious, coming one after another. How long were they planning to keep fighting like this?
It would be better to make things simple and settle them all at once.
Thinking of this, Daniel shook his head and said indifferently,
"Too troublesome. All of you can come at me together."
As soon as these words came out, all the young Godkin froze.
This...
Wasn’t this far too arrogant?
He wanted a group of supreme-grade powerhouses to attack him together?
Wasn’t this the same as completely looking down on Skyvault Corridor and all of them, the Godkin geniuses?
"Impudent!"
Harris felt that he had been deeply humiliated. He was so angry that he actually laughed.
"Get past me first before you say that!"
"Divine Domain—rise!"
Boom—!
A rift suddenly tore open in the void, and an enormous island flew out from within the crack with a thunderous rumble.
The island was absurdly huge, almost as large as one of the human race’s main cities.
The aura it released was far stronger than that of the previous Godkin youth by an unknown amount!
Harris had been thoroughly enraged by Daniel. After summoning his Divine Domain island, he charged fiercely toward Daniel together with the island.
For a moment, the entire space began to shake.
It was like the sea in the midst of a storm, as though it might collapse at any second.
Behind him, the young Godkin cried out in surprise one after another.
"Harris was actually hiding this much strength!"
"So he never used his full power in those sparring matches inside the Corridor!"
"What a Harris... This time, he might really be able to win!"
