chapters.title: Chapter 216 -216-Flipping the Table — Advancing to Level 240!
paragraphs: Daniel looked at her, and for some reason, he thought of Kelly.
Compared with Natasha, Kelly had seemed ordinary and plain.
She was like an innocent, bright-eyed young girl. She looked fragile, yet her heart was firmer than anyone’s.
Toward everything in this world, she carried a childlike curiosity and imagination.
But Natasha?
She was like someone who had already walked through frost and hardship for far too long. The sharpness about her had long since been worn smooth, turning into steadiness and restraint.
Daniel had seen far too many powerful people.
On the contrary, someone like Kelly was what truly made him feel she was extraordinary.
An ordinary person, relying on nothing but a mortal heart, had built a foundation that even gods did not dare look down upon.
That was not something just anyone could do.
Whoosh—!
Natasha sensed Daniel’s aura and flew over at once.
"Your Excellency, you’re back!"
Her face was filled with shock.
Queen Kelly had gone to the God Realm, and even now, no one knew whether she was alive or dead.
Yet this Excellency had also gone to the God Realm, but he had returned alive. How could she not be shocked?
But what she wanted to know even more was: where was Queen Kelly? Why could she not come back?
Daniel looked at Natasha, nodded, then suddenly asked, "You’ve been here this whole time?"
Natasha answered, "Yes."
"This Soul Devouring Vale is my home. I am Mother Kelly’s only daughter. This place was extremely important to her, so before she left, she specifically told me to stay here and not go anywhere."
Daniel fell silent for a while.
He handed Kelly’s letter over to her, his tone calm.
"This is the letter Kelly left for you."
He took out the bracelet as well and handed it over with the letter.
"This is also from Kelly."
Daniel lied.
The true owner of that bracelet was actually Natasha herself. It was just that he did not know which space-time that Natasha came from.
In any case, the tangled fate between the three of them could never be separated from this bracelet.
The moment Natasha heard that it had something to do with Queen Kelly, she immediately took the letter and bracelet.
After reading the letter, her eyes instantly turned red.
Even someone as strong as her could not stop her tears from falling.
"Mother Kelly... was such a fool."
Natasha said through her tears, "Only she would be foolish enough to go looking for some homeland."
Daniel fell silent again.
Natasha looked at him with a complicated gaze and slowly spoke.
"Your Excellency, you’re the person Mother Kelly mentioned, aren’t you?"
Daniel did not speak.
Natasha gave a bitter smile. "I should have guessed long ago."
"Other than you, who could be so powerful?"
"Other than you, who would risk their life to go to the God Realm to find her?"
"Other than you, who could find Soul Devouring Vale and deliver this letter into my hands?"
She suddenly raised her hand and pointed toward the two statues that had stood in the valley for tens of thousands of years.
One man, one woman.
The man was Daniel. The woman was Kelly.
"I should have thought of it sooner. After all, you look so much like that statue!"
Daniel glanced at the two statues.
After so many years, they were still there.
Moreover, they had been preserved as if they were brand new, without the slightest change.
No wonder Natasha could recognize him.
Daniel did not deny it.
He said calmly, "Kelly’s choice was not wrong."
"In the Aetheria that came afterward, humanity would indeed experience calamity after calamity."
"Humans were ants. Fish on a chopping board!"
He thought of what had happened in his previous lives.
The game and reality fused together, and countless invaders threw Aetheria and Earth into chaos.
Humanity clung to life by a thread, forced to the edge of extinction.

Humans were like the lowest-ranked gladiators in an arena, covered in wounds, fighting desperately with their lives on the line. Yet in the end, it was merely to entertain the lords sitting in the stands.
How pathetic!
However, Kelly’s vision had ultimately been limited.
She saw the crisis facing humanity and wanted to break the situation, so she chose the path of "Tracing Origins."
But Daniel had personally experienced humanity’s darkest days.
He knew how to break the situation.
The only way was to flip the entire table.
Humanity would not be gladiators, nor spectators.
Only by becoming the ruler who could make the rules could they truly break this game.
The two of them had chosen different paths, but what they carried in their hearts was the same.
One had stepped into the stars alone a hundred thousand years ago.
The other would overthrow everything pressing down on humanity a hundred thousand years later.
Thinking of this, Daniel looked at Natasha and said, "Goodbye."
Back then, it was because of that pair of bracelets that he had met Kelly and helped her ascend step by step to the throne.
Kelly had adopted Natasha.
Natasha had then given that pair of bracelets to Daniel.
Was this not something that had been destined long ago?
This was the cycle of fate!
Natasha opened her mouth, wanting to say something.
But Daniel’s figure had already scattered like the wind.
Natasha stood there, pressing her lips together, her eyes red.
"Mother Kelly didn’t manage to wait for you..."
"Then will you go and find her?"
"Your Excellency..."
Daniel returned to the main world.
This instance had brought him far too many gains.
The laws of fate and karma were the greatest reward.
Next was his battle with the sage of the God Realm, which had allowed him to figure out the depths of a low Divine-grade powerhouse.
Although a sage’s sage rank was like an invincible domain, and although a sage could use Thoughtstep, Daniel possessed an undying and indestructible ability. The sage could do nothing to him either.
He thought of Kelly’s whereabouts.
"The Endless Starfield, huh..."
Daniel took a deep breath.
The Endless Starfield was vast and boundless, with countless star domains gathered within it.
The star sea was endless. Even the God Realm was nothing more than a speck of dust within it.
Yet Kelly had dared to charge into the Endless Starfield alone.
That courage...
He wondered, one hundred thousand years later, was she still alive, or had she already died?
Daniel shook his head.
When he had the chance to go to the Endless Starfield in the future, he would ask around for news about her.
For now, increasing his strength was the most important thing.
After seeing the foundation of the Godkin, his sense of crisis toward humanity had grown even heavier.
Compared with the Godkin, players who had not yet grown up were simply far too weak!
He took out the Class Awakening Scroll.
Rip—!
The system notification immediately rang out.
[Prompt: The seal on your experience bar has been lifted. You may continue leveling up.]
Daniel had never needed to worry about experience. He directly chose to level up.
[Ding! Your level has increased! Current Level: 221. You have gained 20 attribute points.]
[Ding! Your level has increased! Current Level: 235. You have gained 20 attribute points.]
[Ding! Your level has increased! Current Level: 240. You have gained 20 attribute points.]

[Prompt: You have not yet completed your class change. Your level cap has been sealed again. Excess experience will be temporarily stored in the EXP Pool. Please complete your class change as soon as possible to remove the cap.]
Level 240.
The gap between Daniel and ordinary players was growing wider and wider!
Right now, the top players were still around level 160. Mainstream players were at level 140, while ordinary players were only a little over level 110.
In other words, Daniel’s level was nearly twice that of ordinary players.
Just then, the prompt for the next class change mission also rang out.
[Ding! You have received the Forbidden Curse Mage class change mission. Do you wish to accept?]
"Accept!"
[Ding! You have accepted the class change mission [Command a Pocket World]!]
[Prompt: Your quest log has been updated. Please check the details.]

chapters.title: Chapter 217 -217-Godkin War City, Arcane Machinery
paragraphs: Daniel opened his quest log.
[Command a Pocket World]
[Forbidden Curse Mage Class Change Mission]
Restriction: Forbidden Curse Mage
Mission Difficulty: Exalted-grade
Mission Objective:
Obtain a pocket world.
Mission Introduction:

You have already stepped onto the path of one of the world’s most supreme classes, wielding Strength powerful enough to shake the Heavenly River. This Strength does not exist for you alone, but for your entire race.
If a race wishes to survive, it cannot remain rootless.
Without a territory of its own, a race is like drifting duckweed.

In the Endless Starfield, races without a homeland are known by the world as "star wanderers." Wanderers are like rootless, withered leaves, blown about by the wind, suffering endless disdain and contempt. Without solid land, they cannot take root. Without roots, they cannot reproduce. Without reproduction, they can only decline day by day, until their bloodline and name both vanish into the depths of the star sea.
Therefore, you must forge a place for your people to stand—a complete pocket world.

The grade of a world determines the limit of what it can bear. A major world can accommodate supreme beings of High Divine-grade. A medium world can contain powerhouses of Low Divine-grade. As for a pocket world, it is the ceiling of the supreme-grade realm.
Do everything in your power to push your world to greater heights.
It is not merely your territory. It is the future of your race.
Mission Duration: Long-term
Mission Rewards: [Sacred Spring of Life] ×1, [Forbidden Curse Mage Class Awakening Scroll] ×1...
After Daniel finished reading the class change mission, he could not help but laugh.
Although this mission was marked as Exalted-grade, to him, it could not even be considered epic-grade.
The most difficult part was obtaining a pocket world.
He had already completed that part long ago.
The Aerial Realm was already in his hands.
The second difficult point was possessing an actual "pocket world."
One had to know that even Aetheria was still only a piece of World Fragments. From this alone, it was clear just how high this requirement was.
But Daniel had the World Tree Seed. Once it matured, the Aerial Realm would be elevated into a pocket world.
And so, this extremely difficult mission became incredibly simple again.
He shook his head.
This time, his luck was absurdly good.
"It’s time to properly develop my forces."
Daniel returned to the Polaris District.
Whoosh—!
He hovered in midair and was just about to land when he suddenly froze.
"That... what is that?"
His expression changed instantly.
A city had actually appeared in the sky!
A city floating among the clouds.
That city was faintly discernible, like a shadow hidden in mist. It could be seen, yet not touched.
Daniel narrowed his eyes and looked carefully. He could see cold flashes of weapons everywhere within the city. It was heavily guarded.
There were also waves of powerful Godkin auras spreading out from within, so dense they were like storm clouds.
"Godkin?"
Daniel frowned, killing intent surging in his eyes.
The Godkin were quite bold!
They had actually come to Aetheria?
Were they still planning to treat the human race like a soft persimmon they could squeeze however they liked?
At that moment, Carodion flew over.
"My King."
Daniel raised his hand, pointed at the city in the sky, and asked, "What is going on?"
Carodion glanced at the city in the clouds and gave a bitter smile.
"In answer to my King."

"Not long after you left, this city suddenly appeared. Aliris and I went up to investigate. It is one of the Godkin’s war cities—a war machine specifically used to conquer races across different planes."
After Daniel heard that, the killing intent on his body could no longer be suppressed.
A monstrous wave of killing intent surged out from him, causing even Carodion’s expression to turn solemn.
"The killing intent on the King... is becoming more and more terrifying."
Carodion was secretly shocked.
Just how many living beings had he killed to condense such heavy killing intent?
Daniel gritted his teeth and asked, "So, is there something strange about this city?"
Carodion sighed.
"My King is wise!"
"This war city is very peculiar. It seems to have separated space itself."

"To us, it is like a mass of transparent air... Whether we slash it with blades and axes or bombard it with magic, we cannot harm it in the slightest, because it is simply not in the same space as us. This is probably an extremely advanced spatial formation."
Daniel’s expression darkened.
A spatial formation!?
To put it simply, Aetheria was like a painting, and all living beings, including Daniel himself, were people inside the painting.
Meanwhile, that city in the clouds existed outside the painting. No matter how much the people inside the painting struggled, they could not harm anything outside the painting.
"In that case, we’re very passive."
Daniel took a deep breath.
With his current abilities, there was nothing he could do to that city.
Unless the other side willingly entered Aetheria’s space and stepped into the painting.
"However, it’s not that bad yet."
He had enough trump cards in his hands.
The Aerial Realm could contain all of Aetheria’s players and natives. It just could not be casually exposed.
He also had the Ancestral Totem and the statues of the forebears, which could protect humanity to a certain extent.
Besides, if the Godkin wanted to attack Aetheria, they would have to merge into this space.
Once they dared to step in, Daniel would dare let them experience what a nuclear explosion felt like!
Their passivity only came from the fact that the Godkin could watch this place at any time and send people here whenever they wished.
In truth, the problem was not too serious.
Thinking of this, Daniel sneered.
"Ignore them for now. Just send people to monitor them at all times."
"The most important thing right now is to increase humanity’s strength as quickly as possible and raise the strength of the adventurers."
Daniel returned to the Imperial City and paid no more attention to the city in the sky.
In any case, no matter how many Godkin dared to come, he would dare to kill them all.
With his current strength, supreme-grade beings were no different from ants.
As for Divine-grade powerhouses, they could not descend into this world.
So what was there to fear?
Right now, the most important matter was to comprehensively increase humanity’s strength.
He opened the world panel.
[World Tree Seedling]
[Growing]
Current Highest Limit: [Young Tree State]
[Complete Pocket World]
He glanced at it and closed the panel.
The World Tree’s growth speed was actually not slow. The progress bar had already moved past one-third.
Thinking of this, he took out the [Codex of Creation].
This was the reward the system had given him when he first occupied World Zone No. 1213. Now was precisely the time to use it!
Time was pressing. It was time to create a batch of equipment that would only appear in the future.
[Codex of Creation]
[Epic-grade]
Grade: Epic-grade
Effects:
Codex of Creation: This book contains 180,000 manufacturing blueprints of all kinds.
Genesis: Immortal Singularity can be used to light up the technology tree and determine the technological development direction of the empire.
Innovation: Immortal Singularity can be used to automatically deduce new manufacturing blueprints.
Description: The prosperity of a nation does not rely only on peerless powerhouses, but also on the flourishing of its people!
Daniel did not hesitate. He directly burned a sum of Immortal Singularity.
[Ding! You have consumed Immortal Singularity and unlocked technology tree development options. Please choose a technology tree branch.]
As soon as the system prompt fell, a whole pile of options appeared before his eyes.
[Bloodline Purification]
[Machine Intelligence]
[Mysteries of Magic]
[Magic Martial]
Daniel directly selected the two branches [Machine Intelligence] and [Mysteries of Magic].
[Ding! You have lit up the two technologies [Machine Intelligence] and [Mysteries of Magic]. They have automatically derived [Arcane Machinery]!]
He then proceeded to light up [Arcane Machinery].
[Ding! You have lit up [Arcane Machinery].]
[Arcane Machinery]
[Technology]
Effect: Allows the deduction of technological manufacturing blueprints belonging to the [Arcane Machinery] civilization.

chapters.title: Chapter 218 -218-Arcane Age, Astral Corsairs
paragraphs: After lighting up Arcane Machinery, Daniel immediately let out a breath of relief.

In his previous lives, humanity had relied on nothing but its own stubborn efforts, burying its head and pushing forward blindly. Who knew how many wrong turns they had taken, how many resources they had wasted, before finally achieving even the smallest results on the technological path of Arcane Machinery?
But now, all he had done was consume a little Immortal Singularity, and he had completed what would later become the crystallization of all human wisdom.
This was the benefit of the game system.
It was the same as the laws of destiny and causality. If he had to comprehend those laws by himself, it would be no different from a blind man feeling his way down an unknown road.
But with the game system, everything became much easier.
He knew very well just how powerful Arcane Machinery was. As long as there were blueprints, then in theory, anyone could become Iron Man.
And right now, he was not lacking materials either.
With that thought, he decisively began deriving manufacturing blueprints.
[Ding! You have consumed Immortal Singularity and successfully derived the [Arcane Armor Blueprint (legendary-grade)]!]
[Ding! You have consumed Immortal Singularity and successfully derived the [Elemental Arcane Cannon Blueprint (legendary-grade)]!]
As Daniel listened to the system notifications, a smile appeared at the corner of his mouth.
Excellent!
Arcane Armor was war equipment capable of giving ordinary people power comparable to a legendary-grade powerhouse.
As for the Elemental Arcane Cannon, it was exactly what its name suggested—a cannon!
The only difference was that both its energy source and materials were made from magical materials.
He opened the blueprint.
[Arcane Armor Blueprint (legendary-grade)]
Requirement: legendary-grade engineer
Grade: legendary-grade
Effect: After use, allows the creation of [Arcane Armor].
[Arcane Armor]: Can change size according to the wearer’s will. It can partially cover the body or fully envelop the wearer. It grants the wearer legendary-grade Strength and defense!
Required materials:
[A-grade Energy Source]
[A-grade or higher auxiliary materials]
[A-grade or higher arcane metal]
[legendary-grade magical rune array]
[legendary-grade combat cuneiform]
After Daniel finished reading it, he took out the other blueprint.
[Elemental Arcane Cannon Blueprint (legendary-grade)]
Requirement: legendary-grade engineer
Grade: legendary-grade
Effect: After use, allows the creation of [Elemental Arcane Cannon].

[Elemental Arcane Cannon]: Can gather elemental power and use elemental cannon shells as its means of attack. The longer elemental power is condensed, the farther the range. Its maximum damage limit is legendary-grade!
Required materials:
[A-grade Energy Source]
[A-grade or higher auxiliary materials]
[A-grade or higher arcane metal]
[legendary-grade magical array]
[legendary-grade combat cuneiform]
Daniel closed the panel.
Both of these war machine blueprints were quite impressive.
He already had all the required materials. In fact, he even had materials of a far higher level than what the blueprints demanded. Manufacturing them would not be a problem at all.
As for legendary-grade engineers, there were already some among Aetheria’s NPCs.
He immediately summoned Administrative Officer Roland.
"Gather all legendary-grade engineers. We’re going to concentrate our Strength and accomplish something major."
Roland was briefly stunned. Then he placed a fist against his chest and bowed.
"As you command!"
A sharp light flashed in Daniel’s eyes.
Once the Arcane Armor was manufactured and equipped on players, any player would be able to possess legendary-grade combat power.
Just imagine it.
Billions upon billions of steel warriors mobilizing together.
What kind of suffocating sight would that be?
A smile appeared on Daniel’s face.
The Endless Starfield.
A Starfall Isle was advancing at tremendous speed.
And the direction it was flying toward was unmistakably Aetheria!
A Starfall Isle was usually a drifting island in the starry void, formed by fusing together shattered fragments of worlds. It was the unmistakable symbol of the Astral Corsairs.
These Astral Corsairs had no fixed living world of their own. They could only survive by constantly plundering others.
On the Starfall Isle.
Conrad stood with his hands behind his back.
His long purple hair fluttered gently in the star wind.
His purple eyes gazed into the distance. Within them was anticipation, but also a heavy, oppressive worry.
The Starfarer Clan had wandered through the Endless Starfield for more than ten thousand years.
As the clan leader, Conrad’s desire for a living world where his people could settle down was even stronger than his pursuit of Strength.
Because he knew that sooner or later, the Starfarer Clan would either be casually wiped out by other pirates or slapped to death by some powerful being passing through the void.
That was why his lifelong wish was to find a living world where his clan could finally live in peace.
He was a once-in-a-million-years genius of the Starfarer Clan, and his power had already reached the quasi-sage level.
Logically speaking, he should have been able to smoothly break through to Divine-grade ten thousand years ago.

But unfortunately, the living world the Starfarer Clan had relied on for survival had reached the end of its lifespan. The entire planet had been covered in sky ash. If they had not left, the whole clan would have died.
So they had no choice but to follow the Divine-grade powerhouses of the clan, leave their homeland, and plunge headfirst into the abyss of the Endless Starfield.
But what kind of place was the Endless Starfield?
Even Divine-grade powerhouses were nothing more than slightly stronger ants there.
In less than ten thousand years, the Divine-grade powerhouses of the clan had died one after another.
Now, the strongest person left in the clan was Conrad.
Conrad carried the hopes of the entire clan on his shoulders. The life and death of the whole race rested upon him.
With such immense pressure weighing down on him, his mind could not flow freely. Worry had blocked his path of advancement completely.
And so, his strength had remained stuck at quasi-sage.

He understood very well that as long as he could settle his clansmen properly, then with the foundation he had accumulated over all these years, he might be able to break through to Divine-grade in an instant.
At some point, Mara had walked over to his side.
Conrad looked at her and smiled faintly.
"Mara, what brings you here?"
Mara sighed.
"Every clansman is excited. They all think we’re finally about to have a place to settle down. But I keep feeling that something about this is wrong."
Conrad was startled.
"Why?"
Mara shook her head.
"Because we’re being used by the Godkin. We’ve become their chess pieces. From now on, our lives and deaths will no longer be in our own hands."
Conrad gave a bitter smile.
"I understand that too. If the Godkin are willing to promise us an entire living world, then there must be something in Aetheria that even they can’t handle."
"But we have no choice."
Mara sighed again.
"I know. We no longer have a choice."
"If we continue drifting through the Endless Starfield, we’ll be finished sooner or later. Going to Aetheria at least gives us a chance to fight for survival."
Conrad comforted her.
"Don’t worry."
"The information the Godkin gave us is extremely detailed. The strongest warrior over there is only supreme-grade. I, however, am a quasi-sage."
Mara bit her lip. She seemed to want to say something, but in the end, she swallowed the words back down.
Finally, they turned into nothing more than a sigh.
She turned and began walking back. Then, suddenly, she stopped.
"Conrad... could you perhaps not kill so many people...?"
Conrad opened his mouth, but not a single word came out.
He turned back to look at Mara. Her back trembled slightly before she slowly walked away.
Conrad stood there just like that, unable to say anything.
The Endless Starfield was simply that cruel.
For the sake of his clansmen, he had done everything.
Astral Corsair. Assassin. Taking assassination commissions...
He had done every dirty and exhausting job imaginable. All he wanted was to let his clan survive.
But the condition offered by the Godkin was to slaughter every last human in Aetheria.
He had no right to bargain.
And he did not dare violate the oath.
As for the blood staining his hands?
Heh.
Everyone knew that the heavier the slaughter, the fiercer the karmic backlash would be, and the harder the future Divine-grade tribulation would be to survive.
But this world simply refused to leave the Starfarer Clan any path to survival.
What else could he do?
Such was the cruelty of the starry void.
Conrad closed his eyes and let the wind scrape past his ears.

chapters.title: Chapter 219 -219-The New World Forged by Faustus Himself
paragraphs: Luminara.
Hans did not have to wait for long.
Before much time had passed, a light and graceful figure appeared before him.
Helen came skipping over, lively and cheerful, like a happy little deer.
"Brother, have you been waiting for a long time?"
Hans looked at his younger sister, his eyes filled with doting affection.
"Not really. It hasn’t been that long."
In truth, Hans did have plans today.
His regular hunting party had already agreed to go monster farming together.
But his little sister had said she wanted to visit the Aerial Realm and broaden her horizons. As her older brother, how could he possibly refuse?
So he could only let the brothers in his party wait a little longer.
"Brother, why does Luminara look like it’s covered in spikes?"
"Oh, right, brother, what’s that thing floating in the sky?"
"And brother, what’s that iron lump over there?"
Helen looked exactly like someone who had just entered a grand city for the first time. Her big eyes darted everywhere, and everything she saw felt new and fascinating.
Hans smiled.
There was quite an age gap between the siblings, and he had always spoiled his little sister almost like a daughter.
He raised his hand and pointed toward Luminara.
At this moment, the entire city of Luminara had nearly been armed to the teeth.
Countless cannon barrels bristled from the city walls like the raised quills of a hedgehog, mounted there in a rough and intimidating fashion.
"Those are the barrels of the Elemental Arcane Cannons," Hans said.
"That’s not right!"
Helen frowned.
"The Elemental Arcane Cannons I’ve seen don’t have barrels at all."
The first-generation Elemental Arcane Cannons indeed did not have barrels.

Hans patiently explained, "These are the third-generation Elemental Arcane Cannons personally developed by Guildmaster Faustus. Their power is astonishing. They can instantly kill even high legendary-grade experts with a single shot, and even peak legendary-grade beings would have a hard time escaping serious injury."
"By the gods! Lord Faustus is forever divine!"
Helen’s eyes lit up like stars.
In the hearts of the players, the name Faustus carried a weight no one else could match.
He was a living legend, a traveler who stood at the very summit of the world.

Hans smiled faintly and continued, "The ship floating in the sky is called a Skyborne Dreadnought. It’s said that its main cannon is even more terrifying than the Elemental Arcane Cannon. If it fires a single shot, even a peak legendary-grade expert wouldn’t be able to withstand it."
"That’s incredible!"
Helen praised from the bottom of her heart.
Hans then pointed not far away.
There, a fully armored steel chariot was currently patrolling.

"That’s also a war-type Arcane Machinery developed by Guildmaster Faustus—the Arcane War Chariot. Its defense is comparable to that of a legendary-grade powerhouse, and its attack power is just as formidable. It can slay a high legendary-grade enemy in a single strike."
"Oh my gods!"
Helen’s eyes widened, and she kept muttering Faustus’s name under her breath.
Hans chuckled.
"But compared to the treasures inside the Aerial Realm, these things aren’t much at all."
Suddenly, he stretched out his hand and showed her the black bracer on his wrist.
"Guess what this is?"
He lifted his chin, his face full of smug pride.
Helen blinked, and a faint smile appeared at the corner of her lips.
"Brother, you don’t actually think your little sister came from the countryside, do you? That’s obviously Arcane Armor."
Hans puffed out his chest and declared loudly, "This is Arcane Armor Model III!"
He carefully observed his sister’s expression, hoping to harvest even the tiniest bit of satisfaction from her shock.
Unfortunately, all he saw in Helen’s eyes was confusion.
That look clearly said: It’s all Arcane Armor, isn’t it? What’s the difference?
Hans almost wanted to cry.
The difference was huge!

"You really beat me, little sis. You need to learn more," he sighed, then patiently explained, "This is Guildmaster Faustus’s latest masterpiece. It can raise the wearer’s combat strength to high legendary-grade."
High legendary-grade was the realm of true powerhouses.
This piece of equipment did not only symbolize Strength; it also displayed the owner’s wealth and authority.
It was not something one could buy simply by having money. One also needed an enormous amount of guild contribution points.
Basically, only the veteran brothers who had joined the guild in the very first batch had managed to save enough points to earn the right to purchase it.
Helen’s eyes instantly brightened.
She did not understand wealth or authority very well, but she understood what high legendary-grade meant.
"Brother, are you serious?"
Helen asked in astonishment.
"As long as you wear it, you can have high legendary-grade strength?"
"Of course!"
Hans replied proudly.
"Right now, I can kill a low legendary-grade BOSS with one punch. How about it? Your brother is pretty impressive, right? Hahahahaha!"
Helen was so envious that she immediately gave him a thumbs-up.
"Amazing, brother! You’re amazing!"
Then she looked at him with eager eyes.
"I wonder when I’ll be able to become as strong as you."
Hans raised an eyebrow.
"No rush. With your brother helping you level up, you’ll catch up very soon."
"Come on. Didn’t you want to see the Aerial Realm?"
Helen nodded vigorously.
"I heard people say that the Aerial Realm is a paradise for players."
"More or less."
Hans smiled.
He was one of the first players to set foot in the Aerial Realm. From the age of pioneering to the current era of Arcane Machinery, he had never fallen behind.
It was precisely because he had seized so many early advantages that he had been able to accumulate this fortune and buy the newest arcane equipment.
Aerial Realm.
Whoosh! Whoosh!
The figures of Hans and Helen appeared in this world.
In that instant, Helen felt as if her eyes could barely take everything in.
This world...
It was too miraculous!
"Brother, am I dreaming?"
Helen murmured.
Hans smiled and shook his head.
"No. Everything you’re seeing is real."
"Guildmaster Faustus is truly too great. All of this was built by his own hands."
Helen nodded silently.
Within her field of vision, countless players were soaring through the skies.
Some piloted mechas.
Some wore battle armor.
Whether mechas or battle armor, all of them were equipment capable of flight.
The silhouettes in the sky were so densely packed that, by contrast, the ground below seemed especially empty.
"What is that...?"
Helen was deeply drawn to the city before her eyes.
Was that really a city?
Before her stood a vast, layered ring-shaped structure that covered hundreds of thousands of meters, woven together from countless steel skybridges.
Each ring layer was connected by innumerable aerial walkways.
Layer upon layer, stacked and interlocked, they formed a circular dream city with a fully three-dimensional structure.
Even more shocking was the fact that those skybridges were constantly moving and changing.
Every shifting bridge altered the shape of the ring layer it belonged to. One layer affected another, and the rings linked together in a continuous chain of movement.
The entire city seemed to have come alive.
It was breathing.
It was pulsing.
This was a living city, a city forever in transformation.
Inside the city, countless players wandered through its structures. Some had even come here specifically to experience this strange and novel architecture.
Their faces were filled with disbelief.
This was a miracle.
It was too magical!
Helen also saw colossal objects soaring in the depths of the sky, even mightier than the Skyborne Dreadnought.
With just one glance, she knew that those things were iron-blooded creations born for war.
Even from afar, the sight of them sent chills down her spine. They did not look like mere war machines, but ancient beasts preparing to choose their prey and devour it whole.
Helen was completely stunned.
She felt that Aetheria represented one level of civilization, while the Aerial Realm represented another civilization entirely.
Hans looked at his little sister’s dazed expression and shook his head.
The Aerial Realm had developed too quickly and too well.
Everything here was Guildmaster Faustus’s handiwork.

"To be able to live in the same era as Guildmaster Faustus is truly our honor," he said to his sister. "And these aren’t even the most shocking things yet. Your brother will take you to see something even more astonishing!"
"Something even more astonishing?"
Helen blinked.
What else could possibly be more shocking than everything before her eyes?
This place had countless players equipped with Arcane Machinery.
It had gigantic war machines.
It even had such a fantastical mobile fortress.
What could be even more astonishing than this?

"No rush.
With your brother helping you level up, you’ll catch up very soon."
"Come on.
Didn’t you want to see the Aerial Realm?"
Helen nodded vigorously.
"I heard people say that the Aerial Realm is a paradise for players."
"More or less."
Hans smiled.
He was one of the first players to set foot in the Aerial Realm.
From the age of pioneering to the current era of Arcane Machinery, he had never fallen behind.
It was precisely because he had seized so many early advantages that he had been able to accumulate this fortune and buy the newest arcane equipment.
Aerial Realm.
Whoosh!
Whoosh!
The figures of Hans and Helen appeared in this world.
In that instant, Helen felt as if her eyes could barely take everything in.
This world...
It was too miraculous!
"Brother, am I dreaming?"
Helen murmured.
Hans smiled and shook his head.
"No.
Everything you’re seeing is real."
"Guildmaster Faustus is truly too great.
All of this was built by his own hands."
Helen nodded silently.
Within her field of vision, countless players were soaring through the skies.
Some piloted mechas.
Some wore battle armor.
Whether mechas or battle armor, all of them were equipment capable of flight.
The silhouettes in the sky were so densely packed that, by contrast, the ground below seemed especially empty.
"What is that...?"
Helen was deeply drawn to the city before her eyes.
Was that really a city?
Before her stood a vast, layered ring-shaped structure that covered hundreds of thousands of meters, woven together from countless steel skybridges.
Each ring layer was connected by innumerable aerial walkways.
Layer upon layer, stacked and interlocked, they formed a circular dream city with a fully three-dimensional structure.
Even more shocking was the fact that those skybridges were constantly moving and changing.
Every shifting bridge altered the shape of the ring layer it belonged to.
One layer affected another, and the rings linked together in a continuous chain of movement.
The entire city seemed to have come alive.
It was breathing.
It was pulsing.
This was a living city, a city forever in transformation.
Inside the city, countless players wandered through its structures.
Some had even come here specifically to experience this strange and novel architecture.
Their faces were filled with disbelief.
This was a miracle.
It was too magical!
Helen also saw colossal objects soaring in the depths of the sky, even mightier than the Skyborne Dreadnought.
With just one glance, she knew that those things were iron-blooded creations born for war.
Even from afar, the sight of them sent chills down her spine.
They did not look like mere war machines, but ancient beasts preparing to choose their prey and devour it whole.
Helen was completely stunned.
She felt that Aetheria represented one level of civilization, while the Aerial Realm represented another civilization entirely.
Hans looked at his little sister’s dazed expression and shook his head.
The Aerial Realm had developed too quickly and too well.
Everything here was Guildmaster Faustus’s handiwork.
"To be able to live in the same era as Guildmaster Faustus is truly our honor," he said to his sister.
"And these aren’t even the most shocking things yet.
Your brother will take you to see something even more astonishing!"
"Something even more astonishing?"
Helen blinked.
What else could possibly be more shocking than everything before her eyes?
This place had countless players equipped with Arcane Machinery.
It had gigantic war machines.
It even had such a fantastical mobile fortress.
What could be even more astonishing than this?

chapters.title: Chapter 220 -220-Astral Warship, Star-Ring Fortress
paragraphs: With a thought from Hans, the armor on his wrist instantly activated.
Layer after layer of metal plates suddenly extended outward, wrapping around his entire arm first, then half his body, and finally his whole form.
At this moment, his entire body was covered in a cold metallic sheen.
Helen had seen the transformation sequence of the first-generation armor before, but compared with Model III, the third generation was undoubtedly far more stylish, sharper, and more intimidating.
"Holy shit! That’s so cool!"
Helen praised from the bottom of her heart.
Hans’s voice came from within the armor.
"I’ll take you to see the Sacred Spring of Rebirth!"
Whoosh!
He picked Helen up and shot through the air.
Sacred Spring of Rebirth!
That was the sacred land where mortals crossed the boundary between humanity and divinity.
Anyone who completed the baptism here could truly step into the legendary-grade realm. From then on, they would no longer need battle armor or mechas to soar freely across the nine heavens.
At this moment, hundreds of players were lined up in a long queue in perfect order.
Each of them held a number plate in their hands. Their eyes burned with anticipation as they silently waited for the moment when their destiny would be overturned.
Whoosh!
Hans brought Helen down near the Sacred Spring of Rebirth, stopping at a distance. He did not dare approach even half a step closer.
Those who could wait here for rebirth were all peak experts.
In terms of strength, status, and wealth, they were far beyond what he could compare with.
Although Hans was already close to the threshold of Level 180, he still did not have the qualifications to bathe in the Sacred Spring.
Those qualified to undergo rebirth here were all top-tier players who had long since reached the summit.
Helen stared at the scene before her, her mouth slightly open. Her heart was filled with indescribable shock.
She had never imagined that there were already so many powerful players that even rebirth required lining up in a long queue.
Yet one question still lingered in her heart.
"Brother, what was that war machine just now? The one even bigger than the Skyborne Dreadnought?"
"That’s an Astral Warship."
When Hans said this, his tone was filled with admiration.
"That thing has supreme-grade combat power. Even now, the entire Aerial Realm has only built five of them. I heard that with one shot, it can instantly kill a low supreme-grade enemy."
Instantly kill a low supreme-grade enemy!
Helen’s mind went completely blank when she heard that.
Good heavens.
Wasn’t that far too ferocious?
It could blast even a supreme-grade being to death with one cannon shot?
She remained stunned for quite a while before finally coming back to her senses. Then she asked again, "Then... what’s that circular city called?"
"That’s the Star-Ring Fortress."
Hans smiled as he spoke.
"You can call it a city too, but that thing isn’t ordinary. It has several different forms."

"Most of the time, it’s just a livable city. But if it switches into flight mode, it’s about as powerful as an Astral Warship. And if it activates combat mode, its firepower isn’t any weaker than an Astral Warship’s either."
Helen was dumbstruck.
The shock in her heart was beyond words.
"Look over there."
Hans suddenly pointed toward the Sacred Spring of Rebirth.
Helen followed his hand and looked over.
By coincidence, a player had just walked out of the spring.
The moment he reached the shore, he began fusing with a divine spark. Immediately afterward, a blinding light erupted from his body!
He shot into the sky, flipping and spinning excitedly through the air, performing all kinds of flashy movements. He was so happy he looked as if he might go mad.
"Hahaha! I’ve become legendary-grade!"
"From today onward, I’m a legendary-grade powerhouse too!"
"This Strength, this feeling... this is too amazing! Praise Boss Faustus! Hahahaha!"
The players waiting in line for rebirth all raised their heads and looked excitedly at the newly advanced legendary-grade player.
Not a single person was jealous.
Not a single person was envious to the point of resentment.
Because very soon, it would be their turn.
Legendary-grade.
They would be able to step into that realm as well!
"Number thirty-nine! It’s your turn!"
Beside the Sacred Spring of Rebirth, volunteers were maintaining order. Most of them were legendary-grade experts who had already completed their rebirth and were working part-time here.
After all, working here for a single day could earn them quite a lot of guild contribution points.
These points could be exchanged not only for weapons, equipment, companion eggs, and skill books, but were also required to purchase arcane equipment.
More importantly, even divine sparks themselves had to be exchanged with contribution points.
Because of that, there were never enough points to spend.
So even legendary-grade experts would fight fiercely for opportunities to earn more contribution points.
Hans took his sister around for a while. Then he left her inside the Star-Ring Fortress and hurried toward the gathering point himself.
He could not let the brothers in his hunting party wait too long.
The gathering point was located inside one of the Star-Ring Fortresses.
The moment Hans arrived, his brothers immediately began shouting.
"Hans, you finally showed up! Jack was about to explode from waiting!"
"Hahaha... enough nonsense, hurry up! Today, we have to burst down that supreme-grade boss no matter what!"
"After this run, once I get the boss drops, I’ll be able to use my guild contribution points to exchange for purchase authorization and buy a brand-new Model III armor set!"
Hans quickly formed the party.
He also needed the boss drops badly. He was already close to max level now, so it was time for him to start preparing for his divine spark.
The more contribution points he had, the better the divine spark he could exchange for.
Besides, monster drops from the Aerial Realm could not only be exchanged for contribution points, but also sold for money.
Many big shots had made their fortunes in the Aerial Realm.
Although the monsters in the Aerial Realm did not drop experience or gold coins, the materials on their bodies were already a considerable fortune in themselves.
And the person who had determined the value of these materials was none other than Faustus!
Ordinary players might not understand the reasoning behind it, but Faustus knew very well.
The monsters of the Aerial Realm were treasures from head to toe. Their bones and scales could be mixed into Arcane Machinery to create all kinds of war machines.
Their energy cores had extremely high reserves and could continuously power war machines.
In the Arcane Age, energy was king!
Aerial Realm.
[Ding! The World Tree Seed has grown and taken shape! Current stage: Sapling stage — complete pocket world.]
[Ding! Class change mission [Complete Pocket World] has been completed!]
[Ding! Mission rewards obtained: [Sacred Spring of Life] ×1, [forbidden-grade Archer Class Awakening Scroll] ×1.]
Faustus listened to the notifications ringing beside his ears and stopped what he was doing.
While the Aerial Realm was still in its growth phase, he had rarely found the time to train his secondary class.
During this period, he had derived a large number of high-quality manufacturing blueprints.

New war machines such as the Astral Warship, Star-Ring Fortress, and Skyborne Dreadnought, as well as upgraded versions of the Elemental Arcane Cannon, battle armor, mechas, and more—these were all results of his work during this time.
The results were quite impressive.
Faustus had turned Aetheria into an iron-barrel defensive position.

Forget legendary-grade enemies. Even if groups of supreme-grade powerhouses attacked together, he would not need to take action personally to make them suffer so badly they would not be able to leave with their lives intact.
As for the Aerial Realm, his main base, he had developed it to an unparalleled degree.
It was no exaggeration to say that anyone below Divine-grade who came here would die, no matter how many arrived.
Faustus felt that his greatest achievements were two things.
First, he had cultivated tens of thousands of true legendary-grade experts.
These were genuine legendary-grade powerhouses who did not rely on arcane equipment, but had broken through purely through their own experience and strength.
Moreover, he had established a complete system for players to ascend to godhood.
One had to understand that divine sparks were not cabbages that could be found everywhere. The consumption required by the Sacred Spring of Rebirth was also terrifyingly immense.
But Faustus possessed an endless stream of resources, enough to allow every max-level player to successfully break through to legendary-grade.
These peak players would become the pillars of the human race in the future.
In the foreseeable future, they would step into supreme-grade, and perhaps even advance into Divine-grade.
Second, he had allowed millions of players to put on Arcane Armor and pilot mechas.
That was equivalent to adding millions of legendary-grade combatants to the human race out of thin air.
This was foundation!
Power was the foundation of a race.
It was the support a race relied on to survive.

chapters.title: Chapter 221 -221-Level 260, All-race Star Chart
paragraphs: Faustus walked up to the World Tree and opened the world authority interface.
[Aerial Realm — Complete Pocket World]
Sovereignty Restriction: Human Race
Authority: Faustus — First Sequence
Current mineral refresh rate: +100%
Current monster refresh rate, including quality: +100%
Current world area: +100%
Current drop rate, including grade: +100%
Current World Tree level, upper limit: Pocket World: Sapling — growth suspended
As expected, after the Aerial Realm advanced by one level, all of its attributes had doubled.
But what Faustus valued most was still the refresh rate and quality of monsters.
Although the Aerial Realm’s current rate was already twice as fast as when it had still been a fragmented world, he still felt it was not enough.
Because the players were currently in the middle of an explosive growth phase.
Especially after the appearance of the Phantom Emporium, the difficulty of leveling up for players was visibly decreasing day by day.
As the players’ strength soared, monsters above legendary-grade had suddenly become scarce.
This was something that would have been unimaginable in his previous lives.
Legendary-grade!
That was not some cabbage growing by the roadside.
That was an existence players had looked up to for more than a year.
But now, with the support of arcane technology, forget legendary-grade—even supreme-grade monsters were things players dared to charge at and hack down.
That was how fierce they had become.
Because of that, monster resources above legendary-grade were now severely insufficient.
"There are two methods right now," Faustus pondered. "One is to continue growing the World Tree. The other is to open up new worlds. I can do both at the same time."
Thinking of this, he directly took out the bottle of Sacred Spring of Life he had received as a mission reward and used it.
[Ding! You have used Sacred Spring of Life!]
[Prompt: The World Tree sapling has entered its growth phase. World upper limit progress: 50%.]
Faustus instantly understood.
So one bottle of Sacred Spring of Life was only enough for half the progress.
If he wanted to push the progress to 100% and allow the Aerial Realm to break through into a medium world, he would need another bottle!
Since that was the case, he would take it slowly.
Next, he took out the Class Awakening Scroll and used it.
[Prompt: The seal on your experience bar has been lifted. You may continue leveling up.]
Daniel did not hesitate and directly leveled up.
[Ding! Your level has increased! Current level: 241. You have obtained 20 attribute points.]
[Ding! Your level has increased! Current level: 250. You have obtained 20 attribute points.]
[Ding! Your level has increased! Current level: 260. You have obtained 20 attribute points.]

[Prompt: You have not yet completed the next stage of your class change mission. Your level cap has been sealed. Overflowing experience has been stored in the EXP pool. Please complete your class change mission as soon as possible to continue leveling up.]
Level 260!
Faustus took a deep breath.
This class change mission was almost ridiculously easy.
But this was not the end.
[Ding! You have achieved the achievement [Level 260]!]
[Prompt: Achievement reward obtained — [All-race Star Chart]!]
Faustus was startled.
What was going on?
There was an achievement reward too?
In his previous lives, he had never known this reward existed at all.
The reward was a Star Chart?
He blinked.
He remembered that when he was in Heavenscar, he had once looted the treasury of the Holy Kingdom and obtained a Star Chart there as well.
However, that one had been a Star Chart of the Endless Starfield, which was much higher-level than this.
Faustus took out the reward.
[All-race Star Chart — ???]
Level: ???
Grade: ???
Effect: After use, grants access to the map of the [All Races of the Starry Void].
Uses: Unlimited

Introduction: This is an All-race Star Chart. It is equivalent to a galactic map. Above galaxies are star rivers. Above star rivers are star domains. Above star domains are star seas. Countless star seas combined form the [Endless Starfield].

If the Endless Starfield is understood as a complete universe, then each star sea is like a kingdom, each star domain is like a province, each star river is like a region, and each galaxy is like a city. The living worlds of the major races are equivalent to towns.
Larger world planes are like great cities. Medium-sized ones are like counties. Smaller ones are like towns and villages. Incomplete ones are like abandoned villages...
This map records routes at the [galaxy] level, clearly marking the positions of each "town."
However, every world has its own protective mechanism. Without Divine-grade Strength or a fixed spatial passage, one cannot reach them.
There are also certain additional restrictions. For example, a pocket world cannot accommodate Divine-grade powerhouses.
After Faustus finished reading carefully, he gained a relatively systematic understanding of the Endless Starfield.
So the structure of this universe was far greater than he had imagined.
Without another word, he used the map.
[Ding! You have used [All-race Star Chart]!]
Whoosh—!
A vast image instantly filled his entire field of vision.
The Star Chart clearly marked his current location.
It was a very small misty cluster glowing with red light.
This should be the Aerial Realm!
And near the Aerial Realm—or more accurately, near both the Aerial Realm and Aetheria—there were more than ten thousand similar misty clusters, some large and some small.
The larger ones were over ten thousand times bigger than the Aerial Realm.
The smaller ones were like Aetheria, only half the size of the Aerial Realm.
Clearly, these misty clusters were the living worlds where the myriad races resided.
The Star Chart had clear coordinates. One could tell their locations at a glance.
But that was all.

Just as the introduction had said, if one wanted to travel to another world, one either had to possess Divine-grade Strength and forcibly blast open a passage, or use a spatial passage or a corresponding item.
"However... spatial passages are something I do have."
Faustus smiled.
Those had also been spoils he had obtained the last time he looted the Godkin.
However, all those items were Divine-grade, and the current him could not use them yet.
There were, however, some methods to unlock their usage in advance.
For example, he could have a sage unlock the usage authority for him.
But just thinking about it was enough.
Not every legendary-grade powerhouse possessed legendary-grade weapons.
Correspondingly, when a sage saw Divine-grade resources, they would also become greedy!
He shook his head.
"I’ll find another opportunity to break the seal in the future."
Just then, the system notification rang again.
[Ding! You have obtained the forbidden-grade archer class change mission. Do you accept?]
Faustus naturally did not hesitate.
"Yes!"
[Ding! You have accepted the class change mission [Realm Invasion]!]
[Prompt: A new mission has been added to your mission panel. Please view the details yourself.]
Faustus opened the mission panel.
[Realm Invasion] — forbidden-grade archer class change mission
Restriction: forbidden-grade archer
Mission Difficulty: Exalted-grade
Mission Objective: Enter a pocket world.
Mission Introduction:
Everything you possess, and even that which you have yet to possess, shall crawl beneath your feet.
Everything you lack, together with what little remains in your hands, shall be stripped away from you.
You must possess the Strength to command everything.
Otherwise, even that meager remnant you still cling to will be devoured completely by others.
This is the unwritten iron law of the depths of the Endless Starfield.
It is not a law of the world, yet it is colder and crueler than any law.
Want to survive?
Want to become stronger?
Then go plunder.
Go wage war.
Go seize.
The ideal cycle is this:
Take resources from those who have abundance and give them to those who are lacking.
But the truth is this:
Resources will be torn from the arms of the impoverished and offered up to those who are already wealthy.
Mission Time Limit: None
Mission Rewards: [Elemental Magic Core] ×1, [forbidden-grade Archer Class Awakening Scroll] ×1.

If he wanted to push the progress to 100% and allow the Aerial Realm to break through into a medium world, he would need another bottle!
Since that was the case, he would take it slowly.
Next, he took out the Class Awakening Scroll and used it.
[Prompt: The seal on your experience bar has been lifted.
You may continue leveling up.]
Daniel did not hesitate and directly leveled up.
[Ding!
Your level has increased!
Current level: 241.
You have obtained 20 attribute points.]
[Ding!
Your level has increased!
Current level: 250.
You have obtained 20 attribute points.]
[Ding!
Your level has increased!
Current level: 260.
You have obtained 20 attribute points.]
[Prompt: You have not yet completed the next stage of your class change mission.
Your level cap has been sealed.
Overflowing experience has been stored in the EXP pool.
Please complete your class change mission as soon as possible to continue leveling up.]
Level 260!
Faustus took a deep breath.
This class change mission was almost ridiculously easy.
But this was not the end.
[Ding!
You have achieved the achievement [Level 260]!]
[Prompt: Achievement reward obtained — [All-race Star Chart]!]
Faustus was startled.
What was going on?
There was an achievement reward too?
In his previous lives, he had never known this reward existed at all.
The reward was a Star Chart?
He blinked.
He remembered that when he was in Heavenscar, he had once looted the treasury of the Holy Kingdom and obtained a Star Chart there as well.
However, that one had been a Star Chart of the Endless Starfield, which was much higher-level than this.
Faustus took out the reward.
[All-race Star Chart — ???]
Level: ???
Grade: ???
Effect: After use, grants access to the map of the [All Races of the Starry Void].
Uses: Unlimited
Introduction: This is an All-race Star Chart.
It is equivalent to a galactic map.
Above galaxies are star rivers.
Above star rivers are star domains.
Above star domains are star seas.
Countless star seas combined form the [Endless Starfield].

If the Endless Starfield is understood as a complete universe, then each star sea is like a kingdom, each star domain is like a province, each star river is like a region, and each galaxy is like a city.
The living worlds of the major races are equivalent to towns.
Larger world planes are like great cities.
Medium-sized ones are like counties.
Smaller ones are like towns and villages.
Incomplete ones are like abandoned villages...
This map records routes at the [galaxy] level, clearly marking the positions of each "town."
However, every world has its own protective mechanism.
Without Divine-grade Strength or a fixed spatial passage, one cannot reach them.
There are also certain additional restrictions.
For example, a pocket world cannot accommodate Divine-grade powerhouses.
After Faustus finished reading carefully, he gained a relatively systematic understanding of the Endless Starfield.
So the structure of this universe was far greater than he had imagined.
Without another word, he used the map.
[Ding!
You have used [All-race Star Chart]!]
Whoosh—!
A vast image instantly filled his entire field of vision.
The Star Chart clearly marked his current location.
It was a very small misty cluster glowing with red light.
This should be the Aerial Realm!
And near the Aerial Realm—or more accurately, near both the Aerial Realm and Aetheria—there were more than ten thousand similar misty clusters, some large and some small.
The larger ones were over ten thousand times bigger than the Aerial Realm.
The smaller ones were like Aetheria, only half the size of the Aerial Realm.
Clearly, these misty clusters were the living worlds where the myriad races resided.
The Star Chart had clear coordinates.
One could tell their locations at a glance.
But that was all.

Just as the introduction had said, if one wanted to travel to another world, one either had to possess Divine-grade Strength and forcibly blast open a passage, or use a spatial passage or a corresponding item.
"However... spatial passages are something I do have."
Faustus smiled.
Those had also been spoils he had obtained the last time he looted the Godkin.
However, all those items were Divine-grade, and the current him could not use them yet.
There were, however, some methods to unlock their usage in advance.
For example, he could have a sage unlock the usage authority for him.
But just thinking about it was enough.
Not every legendary-grade powerhouse possessed legendary-grade weapons.
Correspondingly, when a sage saw Divine-grade resources, they would also become greedy!
He shook his head.
"I’ll find another opportunity to break the seal in the future."
Just then, the system notification rang again.
[Ding!
You have obtained the forbidden-grade archer class change mission.
Do you accept?]
Faustus naturally did not hesitate.
"Yes!"
[Ding!
You have accepted the class change mission [Realm Invasion]!]
[Prompt: A new mission has been added to your mission panel.
Please view the details yourself.]
Faustus opened the mission panel.
[Realm Invasion] — forbidden-grade archer class change mission
Restriction: forbidden-grade archer
Mission Difficulty: Exalted-grade
Mission Objective: Enter a pocket world.
Mission Introduction:
Everything you possess, and even that which you have yet to possess, shall crawl beneath your feet.
Everything you lack, together with what little remains in your hands, shall be stripped away from you.
You must possess the Strength to command everything.
Otherwise, even that meager remnant you still cling to will be devoured completely by others.
This is the unwritten iron law of the depths of the Endless Starfield.
It is not a law of the world, yet it is colder and crueler than any law.
Want to survive?
Want to become stronger?
Then go plunder.
Go wage war.
Go seize.
The ideal cycle is this:
Take resources from those who have abundance and give them to those who are lacking.
But the truth is this:
Resources will be torn from the arms of the impoverished and offered up to those who are already wealthy.
Mission Time Limit: None
Mission Rewards: [Elemental Magic Core] ×1, [forbidden-grade Archer Class Awakening Scroll] ×1.

chapters.title: Chapter 222 -222-The Two Who Had Been Marked Long Ago
paragraphs: Elemental Core!?
The reward for this class-change quest was actually an Elemental Core...
As long as he gathered ten of them, he would be able to undo the seal on the Chronoverse Prologue Codex and use it to deduce skills belonging to the laws of space-time.
Right now, Faustus already had five in his possession.
He only needed five more.
The cost-performance ratio of this quest was incredibly high!
More importantly, the difficulty was not that great either. As long as he entered a world, it would count as completing the quest.
"Not bad..."
Faustus murmured under his breath.
At present, the top players were already stepping across the threshold toward legendary-grade.
With the support of magic-powered equipment, the massive group of mid-tier players was clearly on the verge of rising as well.
Although he had the resources of both Aetheria and the Aerial Realm in his hands, it was still far from enough.
If he could obtain the resources of a few more worlds, the players’ development speed would increase greatly.
That could not be better.
Complete the quest and claim the reward, while also easing the shortage of resources.
Two birds with one stone!
Outside the world of Aetheria.
A vessel known as Starfall Isle was anchored at the edge of this world.
Conrad gazed at the living world before him, a planet shrouded in pale-blue radiance, and longing rose in his heart.
That pale-blue glow was the world barrier.
There were only three ways to descend into this living world.

The first was to smash through the barrier by force. As long as one possessed Divine-grade Strength, it would not be too difficult. But if he did that, he would inevitably alarm the entire world and provoke the backlash of the world’s will.
The second was to use a spatial passage-type item.
However, such things were extremely rare.
The third was to obtain a passage token created by whoever held the first-sequence authority over this world. With a passage token, one could freely enter and leave.
Conrad happened to have just such a passage item on him, given to him by the Godkin.
Within Aetheria’s authority sequence, the Godkin were ranked first.
They could grant authority to whomever they wished.
That was the privilege of supreme authority.
At this moment, a group of Starfolk powerhouses had gathered together.
They had already notified the entire race to prepare for war. Countless Starfolk warriors were quietly awaiting the order to attack.
All they needed was one command from their clan chief, and they would charge into Aetheria and begin the slaughter.
"Clan Chief, our Starfolk race has waited for so many years, all for a territory of our own. For this battle, we’re willing to risk everything!"
"For the glory and continuation of our race, we fear nothing!"
"Ten thousand years... Are we finally going to have a home of our own?"
Conrad looked at the burning gazes of his clansmen, and a faint smile appeared on his face.
That was right.
Ten thousand years.
The Starfolk had endured countless storms and hardships.
He only hoped that this time, it would be a good beginning.
Conrad’s strength could be considered demi-sage level.
He possessed Divine-grade Strength, but he had yet to carve out his own sage rank.
He could also smash through the world barrier by force, but there was no need.
If even the Godkin thought this matter was troublesome, then it was definitely not as simple as it looked.
It was better to be cautious.
"Mara, come with me."
"We’ll first investigate Aetheria’s situation."
Mara nodded.
"Mm. It’s always better to be careful."
"The Starfolk are relying on you alone now. We can’t withstand any more turmoil."
"Take this."
Conrad handed a jade token to Mara.
It was the passage token given by the Godkin.
Mara accepted the jade token.
Her strength had already reached the peak of supreme-grade. If the two of them entered together, they could look after each other if anything unexpected happened.
That was still better than Conrad going in alone.
"Let’s go."
Two streaks of light flashed and disappeared into the world of Aetheria.
Aetheria.
Two non-human figures with purple hair, purple skin, and purple eyes appeared out of thin air.
Huff—huff—
The two of them took deep breaths of the living world’s air.
Conrad was almost intoxicated by it.
"The aura of a living world... How many years has it been since I last felt this?"
"Compared to the Endless Starfield, this place is practically paradise!"
Mara’s tears fell on the spot.
Long ago, the Starfolk had also possessed their own living world.
But worlds had lifespans too.

Their world had existed for far too long. Its spiritual energy had dried up, and the entire planet had been buried beneath gray ash. Living beings could no longer survive there, so they had no choice but to wander the starry sky.
In the Endless Starfield, strength was the capital needed to survive.
The Starfolk did not have enough of that capital.
Even Divine-grade powerhouses were nothing more than slightly sturdier ants there.
The Astral Corsairs were their greatest threat, while the exhaustion of resources was another fatal problem.
In the end, all the Divine-grade powerhouses of the Starfolk died.
The burden of clan chief fell upon the shoulders of the strongest surviving member—
Conrad.
Mara shook her head.
"Let’s walk around."
Conrad nodded.
They went to lush forests.
They went to the boundless sea.
They went to human villages...
Luminara, inside a small tavern by the street.
Conrad and Mara sat in a corner, listening to the noisy clamor within the tavern and watching the endless flow of people on the street outside.
Their hearts were unexpectedly calm.
They did not feel out of place at all.
A prosperous civilization.
Abundant wealth.
Countless living beings.
Overflowing vitality.
That was the most direct impression Aetheria gave Conrad and Mara.
"Conrad, are we really going to destroy this place completely?"
Mara’s face was filled with hesitation, and confusion flickered in her eyes.

"This civilization is so prosperous. So many races live together in harmony here. If we could find a place to settle down, wouldn’t that be fine too? Do we really have to slaughter the entire civilization?"
Conrad took a deep breath. His eyelids twitched, and he let out a sigh.
"We don’t have a choice."
"The Godkin want us to slaughter every living being in Aetheria. If we refuse to obey them, what will they think?"
"They’ll only think we broke our promise. If we truly anger the Godkin, wiping out our entire race would not be difficult for them at all."
Mara’s expression changed, and she retorted,

"You’re already a demi-sage. By all rights, you should be invincible beneath Divine-grade. And in a small world like this, Divine-grade powerhouses can’t even descend. Why are you so afraid of the Godkin?"
A bitter smile tugged at Conrad’s lips.
He shook his head.
After pondering in silence for quite some time, he finally spoke slowly.
"There are differences in strength even among demi-sages. I may not be weak, but I’m still far from the peak of the demi-sage rank."
He stared at Mara, his voice trembling slightly.
"Star-wandering races like ours are countless in the Endless Starfield. And among the Astral Corsairs, transcendent demi-sage ranks are as numerous as the stars."
"If the Godkin can find us, what makes you think they can’t find other star-wandering races? What makes you think they can’t find those powerful pirates?"
"If the Godkin invite three or four demi-sages over, what am I supposed to use to stop them?"
His voice sank.
"The final result would be the complete destruction of my Starfolk race!"
After listening to him, Mara could not help letting out a long sigh.
The weak were prey to the strong.
That was the iron law of the Endless Starfield.
The Starfolk only wanted to survive.
They had no choice at all.
Just then—
Whoosh!
A supreme-grade powerhouse suddenly appeared before them.
Conrad and Mara’s gazes sharpened.
At the same time, their hearts sank.
They had been discovered!
The supreme-grade powerhouse walked straight up to the two of them and said coldly,
"Carodion comes by order of my king to invite the two of you over for a talk."
They had been discovered?
How was that possible?
Neither of them had sensed that they were being watched at all.
The waters of Aetheria seemed to run far deeper than they had imagined.
