chapters.title: Chapter 223 -223-Invincible Beneath Sage
paragraphs: At the corner tavern.
Carodion stood coldly before the two of them.
"By order of my king, I invite the two of you to come as guests."
Conrad and Mara were deeply shaken.
They had been so cautious, yet they had still been discovered. This could only mean that the powerhouses hidden within the world of Aetheria were far from as simple as they appeared on the surface.
What they did not know was that from the moment they stepped into Aetheria, Faustus had already learned of the arrival of outsiders through the alert sent out by the Arcane Weave Sky Net.
The Sky Net was a fusion of magic energy and technology. Not only did it cover all of Aetheria, but the Aerial Realm also had an independent system of its own.
Forget powerhouses from other worlds—even if a butterfly flew in, the Sky Net would detect it.
After Faustus discovered these two, he did not act rashly.
Since they had chosen to sneak in, he wanted to see exactly what they intended to do.
Through the Sky Net, Faustus watched their every move.
He could see through Mara’s foundation. She was at the peak of supreme-grade. She was indeed not weak.
But Conrad’s strength was something he could not quite pin down.
It felt as if Conrad was stuck somewhere between supreme-grade and Divine-grade. He was far stronger than ordinary supreme-grade beings, yet he had not truly touched the threshold of Divine-grade.
Under the eyes of the Sky Net, the two of them were like torches in the night. There was no hiding at all.
Faustus followed their trail the whole way and repeatedly went over their conversation, roughly piecing together the cause and effect behind the matter.
So these Starfolk powerhouses were blades hired by the Godkin to destroy the human race.
But this blade seemed to be hesitating!
In the end, they were nothing more than pitiful wanderers with nowhere to call home.
Faustus made up his mind.
He would use them to make a move.
If the Godkin could use them, why couldn’t he?
Not only would he use them, he would also make them turn around and bite the Godkin back.
The Godkin were too troublesome. They kept playing dirty tricks behind the scenes.
Then he would let them have a taste of being stabbed in the back too.
Conrad and Mara exchanged a glance, instantly understanding each other’s thoughts.
Conrad had always been cautious.
Mara shook her head slightly, signaling that he must not go.
Although the Starfolk had become wandering people of the stars, precisely because of that, they had seen many things out there.
What if the other side had set up some sinister magic formation?
What if they had hidden some strange artifact?
If the two of them foolishly barged in without knowing anything, it might be difficult to leave afterward.
The corner of Carodion’s mouth curled in disdain, and he let out a cold laugh.
"As expected, exactly as my king guessed. You have ghosts in your hearts! Fine, then. If you want to fight, come."
"Wait!"
Conrad suddenly called out to stop him.
His expression turned solemn. He turned to Mara and said,
"You stay here. I’ll go take a look."
Mara was just about to speak, but Conrad raised his hand and stopped her.
"I’m a demi-sage. I can come and go as I please."
"You’re different. Wait here. I want to see exactly what the powerhouses of this place are trying to do."
"Mm... Then you must be careful!"
"If things really don’t work out, we can leave this star region and stay far away from the Godkin!"
Conrad nodded gravely.
Whoosh!
Carodion brought Conrad to a reception hall.
"My king."
Carodion walked behind Faustus and bowed respectfully.
Faustus studied Conrad.
This purple-skinned non-human being was a type of lifeform he had never seen before.
The other party had sealed away his aura completely, so Faustus could not accurately judge his foundation either.
At the same time, Conrad was also sizing up Faustus.
Legendary-grade?
That was all?
How could someone like this command a supreme-grade powerhouse?
It seemed he was not as simple as he looked on the surface.
Either this person was hiding his true strength, or he had someone powerful backing him!
Conrad had always been cautious. He never underestimated any opponent.
"Starfolk, Conrad."
He was the first to announce his name.
"Human race, Faustus."
Boom—!
The aura around Conrad suddenly erupted.
Carodion’s expression darkened.
What a powerful aura!
That pressure far exceeded supreme-grade. It had already reached a higher level of Strength.
Could he be Divine-grade?
Carodion instantly tensed.
Even if the one before him was truly Divine-grade, he had nothing to fear.
With Faustus here, even if he had to die, he had to ensure Faustus’s safety.
Faustus raised an eyebrow.
Sure enough—
This non-human race member had not yet reached Divine-grade. He was still half a step away.
He should be considered a demi-sage.
Conrad did not attack.
What he was doing was a display of strength.
My strength is right here. If you cannot show something worthy in return, then don’t blame me for what happens next!
Only if you can reveal Strength no weaker than mine can you intimidate me.
Faustus saw through the other party’s thoughts clearly.
Whoosh—!
A mass of light suddenly emerged in his palm.
Conrad’s gaze locked firmly onto that light.
The aura of the light surged upward layer by layer.
In the end, it actually transformed into a black hole!
The radiance was too intense. Even space could not withstand it and teetered on the verge of shattering. To the naked eye, it looked like light, yet all one could see was a pitch-black abyss.
Conrad sucked in a cold breath.
What terrifying strength!
Although it was still inferior to Divine-grade, it was not too far off.
At the very least, within the realm of supreme-grade, this kind of strength was already invincible.
Even he, Conrad, would not be able to withstand sustained damage of this level.
Conrad’s expression turned completely solemn.
But inside, his heart was already churning violently.
Damn it!
He was clearly only legendary-grade, so how could he unleash damage that was invincible beneath Divine-grade?
This was far too absurd!
Now, he understood.
The person opposite him truly had confidence.
No wonder the Godkin found this world so troublesome. They would rather seek out outsiders than take action themselves.
Against a monster like Faustus, no matter how many supreme-grade Godkin came, they would only die.
And since Divine-grade beings could not descend, this person was an invincible existence within this world.
Faced with such a burning hot potato, the Godkin could only borrow another’s blade to kill.
Conrad instantly understood.
This job really would not be easy!
Faustus smiled.
"What do you think?"
Conrad took a deep breath.
"You’re very strong."
His eyes darkened.
"It’s still not enough."
The corner of Faustus’s mouth lifted.
"What if I told you that this is only a fraction of my strength?"
What kind of joke is that?
Conrad’s heart trembled.
Could a legendary-grade really be this strong?
But Faustus’s next words completely stunned him.
"If I truly wanted to keep you here, you wouldn’t be able to leave."
Faustus’s tone was calm, as if he were talking about something utterly ordinary.
"I have also fought Divine-grade powerhouses of the Godkin before—even a sage could do nothing to me."
Boom—!
Conrad’s entire worldview shattered.
How great was the distance between legendary-grade and Divine-grade?
It was even greater than the gap between a human and an ant.
A legendary-grade going head-to-head against a Divine-grade?
Was he joking?
Wait...
Faustus?
Why did that name sound somewhat familiar?
A bolt of lightning flashed through Conrad’s mind. His entire body staggered several steps back, and even his voice changed from shock.
"Faustus—you’re the one who ascended Cloudcrest Peak! The supreme-grade starlight of this generation, Faustus!"
Boom—!
Conrad instantly figured everything out!
Cloudcrest Peak.
Faustus.
This was the heaven’s chosen who would suppress an entire era!
Everything matched.
That explained why Faustus, despite being merely legendary-grade, could be powerful to such an extent.
He had reached the summit of Cloudcrest Peak!
That was the supreme honor of the Endless Starfield.
Although it was merely an honor in a symbolic sense, it was still a genuine achievement, a feat that could be sung across countless universes...
He was actually the one who had reached the summit!

sentences.text: At the corner tavern.
Carodion stood coldly before the two of them.
"By order of my king, I invite the two of you to come as guests."
Conrad and Mara were deeply shaken.
They had been so cautious, yet they had still been discovered.
This could only mean that the powerhouses hidden within the world of Aetheria were far from as simple as they appeared on the surface.
What they did not know was that from the moment they stepped into Aetheria, Faustus had already learned of the arrival of outsiders through the alert sent out by the Arcane Weave Sky Net.
The Sky Net was a fusion of magic energy and technology.
Not only did it cover all of Aetheria, but the Aerial Realm also had an independent system of its own.
Forget powerhouses from other worlds—even if a butterfly flew in, the Sky Net would detect it.
After Faustus discovered these two, he did not act rashly.
Since they had chosen to sneak in, he wanted to see exactly what they intended to do.
Through the Sky Net, Faustus watched their every move.
He could see through Mara’s foundation.
She was at the peak of supreme-grade.
She was indeed not weak.
But Conrad’s strength was something he could not quite pin down.
It felt as if Conrad was stuck somewhere between supreme-grade and Divine-grade.
He was far stronger than ordinary supreme-grade beings, yet he had not truly touched the threshold of Divine-grade.
Under the eyes of the Sky Net, the two of them were like torches in the night.
There was no hiding at all.
Faustus followed their trail the whole way and repeatedly went over their conversation, roughly piecing together the cause and effect behind the matter.
So these Starfolk powerhouses were blades hired by the Godkin to destroy the human race.
But this blade seemed to be hesitating!
In the end, they were nothing more than pitiful wanderers with nowhere to call home.
Faustus made up his mind.
He would use them to make a move.
If the Godkin could use them, why couldn’t he?
Not only would he use them, he would also make them turn around and bite the Godkin back.
The Godkin were too troublesome.
They kept playing dirty tricks behind the scenes.
Then he would let them have a taste of being stabbed in the back too.
Conrad and Mara exchanged a glance, instantly understanding each other’s thoughts.
Conrad had always been cautious.
Mara shook her head slightly, signaling that he must not go.
Although the Starfolk had become wandering people of the stars, precisely because of that, they had seen many things out there.
What if the other side had set up some sinister magic formation?
What if they had hidden some strange artifact?
If the two of them foolishly barged in without knowing anything, it might be difficult to leave afterward.
The corner of Carodion’s mouth curled in disdain, and he let out a cold laugh.
"As expected, exactly as my king guessed.
You have ghosts in your hearts!
Fine, then.
If you want to fight, come."
"Wait!"
Conrad suddenly called out to stop him.
His expression turned solemn.
He turned to Mara and said,
"You stay here.
I’ll go take a look."
Mara was just about to speak, but Conrad raised his hand and stopped her.
"I’m a demi-sage.
I can come and go as I please."
"You’re different.
Wait here.
I want to see exactly what the powerhouses of this place are trying to do."
Then you must be careful!"
"If things really don’t work out, we can leave this star region and stay far away from the Godkin!"
Conrad nodded gravely.
Whoosh!
Carodion brought Conrad to a reception hall.
"My king."
Carodion walked behind Faustus and bowed respectfully.
Faustus studied Conrad.
This purple-skinned non-human being was a type of lifeform he had never seen before.
The other party had sealed away his aura completely, so Faustus could not accurately judge his foundation either.
At the same time, Conrad was also sizing up Faustus.
Legendary-grade?
That was all?
How could someone like this command a supreme-grade powerhouse?
It seemed he was not as simple as he looked on the surface.
Either this person was hiding his true strength, or he had someone powerful backing him!
Conrad had always been cautious.
He never underestimated any opponent.
"Starfolk, Conrad."
He was the first to announce his name.
"Human race, Faustus."
Boom—!
The aura around Conrad suddenly erupted.
Carodion’s expression darkened.
What a powerful aura!
That pressure far exceeded supreme-grade.
It had already reached a higher level of Strength.
Could he be Divine-grade?
Carodion instantly tensed.
Even if the one before him was truly Divine-grade, he had nothing to fear.
With Faustus here, even if he had to die, he had to ensure Faustus’s safety.
Faustus raised an eyebrow.
Sure enough—
This non-human race member had not yet reached Divine-grade.
He was still half a step away.
He should be considered a demi-sage.
Conrad did not attack.
What he was doing was a display of strength.
My strength is right here.
If you cannot show something worthy in return, then don’t blame me for what happens next!
Only if you can reveal Strength no weaker than mine can you intimidate me.
Faustus saw through the other party’s thoughts clearly.
Whoosh—!
A mass of light suddenly emerged in his palm.
Conrad’s gaze locked firmly onto that light.
The aura of the light surged upward layer by layer.
In the end, it actually transformed into a black hole!
The radiance was too intense.
Even space could not withstand it and teetered on the verge of shattering.
To the naked eye, it looked like light, yet all one could see was a pitch-black abyss.
Conrad sucked in a cold breath.
What terrifying strength!
Although it was still inferior to Divine-grade, it was not too far off.
At the very least, within the realm of supreme-grade, this kind of strength was already invincible.
Even he, Conrad, would not be able to withstand sustained damage of this level.
Conrad’s expression turned completely solemn.
But inside, his heart was already churning violently.
Damn it!
He was clearly only legendary-grade, so how could he unleash damage that was invincible beneath Divine-grade?
This was far too absurd!
Now, he understood.
The person opposite him truly had confidence.
No wonder the Godkin found this world so troublesome.
They would rather seek out outsiders than take action themselves.
Against a monster like Faustus, no matter how many supreme-grade Godkin came, they would only die.
And since Divine-grade beings could not descend, this person was an invincible existence within this world.
Faced with such a burning hot potato, the Godkin could only borrow another’s blade to kill.
Conrad instantly understood.
This job really would not be easy!
Faustus smiled.
"What do you think?"
Conrad took a deep breath.
"You’re very strong."
His eyes darkened.
"It’s still not enough."
The corner of Faustus’s mouth lifted.
"What if I told you that this is only a fraction of my strength?"
What kind of joke is that?
Conrad’s heart trembled.
Could a legendary-grade really be this strong?
But Faustus’s next words completely stunned him.
"If I truly wanted to keep you here, you wouldn’t be able to leave."
Faustus’s tone was calm, as if he were talking about something utterly ordinary.
"I have also fought Divine-grade powerhouses of the Godkin before—even a sage could do nothing to me."
Boom—!
Conrad’s entire worldview shattered.
How great was the distance between legendary-grade and Divine-grade?
It was even greater than the gap between a human and an ant.
A legendary-grade going head-to-head against a Divine-grade?
Was he joking?
Wait...
Faustus?
Why did that name sound somewhat familiar?
A bolt of lightning flashed through Conrad’s mind.
His entire body staggered several steps back, and even his voice changed from shock.
"Faustus—you’re the one who ascended Cloudcrest Peak!
The supreme-grade starlight of this generation, Faustus!"
Boom—!
Conrad instantly figured everything out!
Cloudcrest Peak.
Faustus.
This was the heaven’s chosen who would suppress an entire era!
Everything matched.

chapters.title: Chapter 224 -224-I’ve Got My Eye on a Piece of Godkin Territory
paragraphs: Faustus blinked.
Was his reputation really that great?
"Then now, do you believe what I said?"
Faustus asked.
How could Conrad not believe him now?
What level of potential did one need to suppress an entire generation of heaven’s chosen in the Endless Starfield?
It was simply unimaginable.
"I believe you."
Conrad gave a bitter smile.
"It seems I won’t be able to complete this job for the Godkin."
If he could not complete the job, then he could only continue drifting through the Endless Starfield, continuing to be a rootless wanderer.
Otherwise, he would have to clash head-on with Faustus.
But right now, Conrad did not dare.
He had always been cautious by nature, and he did not want to take even the slightest risk.
The Starfolk could no longer afford any more turmoil.
When Faustus heard this, he immediately smiled.
"I know what you want. We can cooperate."
"Isn’t it just a living world?"
The Godkin held so many planes in their hands. So what if he seized a few from them?
The corner of Faustus’s mouth lifted.
Conrad’s eyes widened, and even his breathing became hurried.
The Godkin ruled over more than a dozen planes, yet they were not even willing to give the Starfolk a place to settle down.
If the Starfolk wanted a piece of territory, they had to risk the extinction of their entire race and go to war with Faustus...
But judging from Faustus’s tone, it seemed as if he did not care much about a living world at all.
"What you want is nothing more than a living world."
Faustus said, "And I just so happen to know of the All-Race Star Chart. Getting a living world will be easy."
Hiss—!
Conrad could not help sucking in a cold breath.
At that moment, he felt like a beggar on the street who had suddenly encountered a wealthy man sitting on a mountain of gold.
The wealthy man said to him: You want bread? Too small. Your vision is too small! I’ll give you a mountain of gold instead...
What else could Conrad say?
For ten thousand years, all the Starfolk had sought was a stable place to settle down, so they no longer had to suffer the torment of wandering the stars.
They were like homeless wanderers who had drifted outside for an entire lifetime, asking for nothing more than a small house that could shelter them from wind and rain.
But there was no free meal in this world.
Nor would pies simply fall from the sky.
If one wanted to obtain something, one had to exchange something for it.
Faustus called it "cooperation," but perhaps that word was not quite so pleasant in reality.
Right now, all initiative was in Faustus’s hands.
How they would cooperate depended entirely on what Faustus demanded.
Conrad understood this perfectly, so he hurriedly asked,
"What are your conditions?"
The corner of Faustus’s mouth curled upward.
"Very simple. Become a vassal race of the human race. I’ll arrange a living world for you. Sign a racial vassal contract, and I’ll give you everything you want."
A vassal contract.
That meant bringing the entire race under Faustus’s command!
Conrad fell silent.
But in truth, he did not hesitate for long.
He had already reached the end of the road.
If he went to war with Faustus, even returning alive would be difficult, and the Starfolk would certainly be doomed along with him.
If he refused to fight and returned to the Endless Starfield, the Starfolk would still be finished sooner or later.
One side was life.
The other was death.
Everyone wanted to live.
Only those who had crawled out of hell knew just how difficult it was to stay alive.
"Fine. I agree."
Conrad agreed readily, but he was still wary of the Godkin.
"But... how do you plan to deal with the Godkin?"
Faustus had confiscated the blade handed over by the Godkin.
Would the Godkin just let this go?
Impossible!
After suffering such a huge loss, the Godkin would never let the matter end here.
What Conrad feared most was this:
What if the Godkin brought over a group of demi-sages next time?
That was Conrad’s greatest concern.
With the Godkin’s enormous power, they had plenty of methods to deal with disobedient opponents.
Otherwise, with the Godkin ruling more than a dozen planes and countless living beings, there would inevitably be some rebels.
If a single supreme-grade invincible being could render them helpless, would the Godkin still have the face to call themselves overlords?
Unless one was truly invincible beneath Divine-grade, no one could withstand all the dirty tricks of the Godkin.
But in Faustus’s eyes, Conrad’s worries were not even a problem.
"I’ll be honest with you."
"As long as Divine-grade does not appear, I am invincible."
Faustus’s confidence was absolute.
"No matter how many come, I’ll kill them all."
When Faustus said he was invincible, he meant truly invincible.
He could even wrestle with Divine-grade powerhouses.
It was just that even if he said this out loud, few would believe him, and even fewer could understand it.
Conrad thought Faustus meant he was invincible at supreme-grade.
But in reality, Faustus was far stronger than he imagined.
Boom—!
Even so, after hearing Faustus’s words, Conrad’s heart surged violently.
He looked at this heaven’s chosen before him, the one who had reached the summit of Cloudcrest Peak, and the shock in his heart was impossible to describe.
As expected of the one who had reached the summit.
This absolute confidence was something even he did not possess!
He was a demi-sage, yet even he did not dare claim to be invincible beneath Divine-grade.
But Faustus dared.
And he said it with complete confidence.
"Remember this."

Faustus continued, "A vassal contract is not a master-servant contract. To put it plainly, it is a relationship between superior and subordinate. That is my bottom line. If you want to negotiate anything else, then there’s nothing more to discuss."
He had to make the ugly words clear first.
Faustus did not intend to grip the Starfolk too tightly.
The burden on his shoulders was already heavy enough. He had plenty of matters to worry about for the human race. If he added the Starfolk on top of that, he would only make himself even more tired.
He also had no intention of letting the Starfolk live together with the human race.
The Aerial Realm would not be opened to them.
As long as they obediently stayed in one place and did not cause trouble, that would be enough.
Conrad smiled bitterly.
"That is acceptable."
He sighed.
"The Godkin are no good people either. If they were truly sincere toward us, they would not have sent us to risk our lives against you."

"In the end, we Starfolk are nothing more than chess pieces. Perhaps we would even be schemed against by the Godkin in the end. From beginning to end, all we wanted was a piece of land where we could survive."
Originally, Conrad had no choice.
Aside from risking his life for the Godkin, he had no other path of retreat.
But now, he had another road.
Submit to Faustus.
As long as Faustus could truly remain invincible beneath Divine-grade, the survival of the Starfolk would be secured!
Conrad was not afraid that Faustus was deceiving him either.
The Godkin hated Aetheria to the bone. Compared to the Starfolk, the human race had even less room to retreat.
Conrad was willing to believe him.
Very soon, Faustus signed a vassal contract with Conrad.
This contract was looser than a master-servant contract, but it still bound the two races together.
The contract clearly stated the responsibilities the Starfolk had to bear as a vassal race, such as obeying the commands of the human race and abiding by the rules of the human race.
To put it plainly, the human race was the superior.
The Starfolk were the subordinate.
Faustus then brought out those Divine-grade items and had Conrad undo their seals one by one.
In truth, this was also one of the reasons he had chosen to persuade Conrad to surrender.
Although Conrad was not a sage, he already possessed a portion of a sage’s Strength.
Even though undoing these seals was still rather strenuous for him, he at least had the qualifications to do so!
After Conrad finished unsealing all of them, Faustus finally took out the All-Race Star Chart.
"This is the Star Chart."
The Star Chart!
Conrad’s eyes lit up, and he stared fixedly at the map.
With the Star Chart, one could know where living worlds were located.
The reason he had managed to find Aetheria was also because he had obtained its coordinates.
Without coordinates, he would not even be able to find the door.
In other words, with this map in hand, one could find all the living worlds within this region of the starry sky.
The corner of Faustus’s mouth curved.
"You are a demi-sage, so you should be able to smash open a world barrier. As long as you break through it, we can fight our way in and occupy the entire world!"
As long as he could enter, his class-change quest would be considered complete.
And as for invasion and occupation, that went without saying!
Conrad nodded.
"I possess a portion of Divine-grade authority. I simply cannot open up a sage rank. Breaking through a world barrier will not be difficult."
"That’s good."
Faustus unfolded the Star Chart and pointed at one cluster of light.
"This place is called the Divine Wind Realm. It is a small world under the Godkin."
Conrad’s eyes almost popped out of their sockets.
"Wait! You’re planning to move against the Godkin’s territory?"

chapters.title: Chapter 225 -225-Divine-Grade Puppet, Endless Starfield
paragraphs: Audacious beyond belief!
Why was this human leader so insane?
According to common sense, shouldn’t one pick on the weakest target first?
But not him.
He went straight for the Godkin.
Did he think his life was too long?
Faustus smiled.
"The Godkin dared to make a move against me, so why wouldn’t I dare to make a move against them?"
"Sage rank powerhouses can’t descend into small worlds. So what if I seize one of their worlds?"
One had to know that in his previous lives, Aetheria had always been the one being bullied.
Faustus had long since had enough of that.
Why should others be the only ones allowed to attack you?
Now that he had the strength, why couldn’t he attack others?
Just as the Star Chart had written.
The most ideal cycle in this universe was—
To take resources from those who had abundance and give them to those who lacked.
But the truth was—
Resources would be robbed from the arms of the barren and offered up to those who were already wealthy!
To put it plainly, it was the law of the jungle.
The weak were prey to the strong.
So why should the human race be the only one getting robbed?
Conrad looked deeply at Faustus.
This human leader had courage!
No—
He was mad!
Conrad took a deep breath.
"Everything will be decided by you, my lord. My Starfolk are willing to cooperate with your operation!"
Faustus said calmly,
"Then we’ll act now. Let’s make the Godkin bleed first."
Conrad had already been tied to the same rope as Faustus.
After the two of them roughly discussed how the attack would proceed, Conrad returned to consult his clansmen about the invasion.
Faustus, meanwhile, returned to the Polaris District.
He took out the items he had seized from the Holy Kingdom’s treasury.
Conrad had helped him undo the seals, so those Divine-grade items could now be used.
At this moment, he was holding a small humanoid doll.
The doll was mottled by the erosion of time, and it looked somewhat old.
But Faustus liked it very much.
[Lifelike Puppet — Divine-grade]
Restriction: legendary-grade
Consumption: Immortal Singularity
Use: Consume an unknown amount of Immortal Singularity to activate this item. The item’s maximum strength limit is peak Divine-grade.

Effect: After activation, the puppet can perfectly replicate all of the main body’s strength, including talents, buffs, and skills. It can also grow alongside the main body’s strength, while sharing information and vision.

Description: A small trinket casually made by an Oracle-grade existence. Once its strength reaches its upper limit, it can no longer advance. As for how much Immortal Singularity is needed to activate it... heaven knows.
After reading it, Faustus frowned.
The puppet was a good puppet.
But this "unknown amount" felt a little wrong, didn’t it?
He muttered inwardly.
Was this some kind of trap?
But compared to the benefits of this treasure, even if it was a trap, he had to jump in!
This thing was too important.
He could not do without it.
Faustus could not stay cooped up in this small world forever.
He had to go to medium worlds.
He had to go to the Endless Starfield.
But once he stepped outside, the Godkin would definitely seize the opportunity to make a move.
He was not afraid for himself.
After all, he could not truly die.
What he feared was that the moment he left, the Godkin would come in right behind him and raid his home.
That would be far too passive!
Now that he had this Divine-grade puppet, there would be nothing to fear.
No matter how many Godkin beneath Divine-grade came, the puppet would kill them all.
Without another word, he began activating it.
[Ding! You have consumed 1,000 points of Immortal Singularity. This item has not yet been activated!]
[Ding! You have consumed 5,000 points of Immortal Singularity. This item has not yet been activated!]
[Ding! You have consumed 50,000 points of Immortal Singularity. This item has not yet been activated!]
Faustus rolled his eyes several times in succession.
It really was a trap!
It had swallowed tens of thousands already, yet there was not even the slightest reaction.
Fortunately, he had prepared for this.
Gritting his teeth, he used the Replica Crystal to replicate one million Immortal Singularity.
"I refuse to believe this..."
Continue!
[Ding! You have consumed 100,000 points of Immortal Singularity. This item has not yet been activated!]
[Ding! You have consumed 300,000 points of Immortal Singularity. This item has not yet been activated!]
[Ding! You have consumed 600,000 points of Immortal Singularity. This item has not yet been activated!]
This was way too ridiculous!
Only now did Faustus understand what "unknown amount" meant.
Even one million was not enough to feed it!
He replicated another batch.
[Ding! You have consumed 500,000 points of Immortal Singularity. This item has not yet been activated!]
[Ding! You have consumed 800,000 points of Immortal Singularity. This item has not yet been activated!]
[Ding! You have consumed 1,000,000 points of Immortal Singularity—Congratulations! This item has been activated!]
Faustus froze for a moment.
It was finally activated!
After throwing several million points of Immortal Singularity into it, it was finally activated!
The instant the system notification rang out, the puppet in his hand suddenly disappeared.
A streak of light flashed before his eyes, transforming into a blurry shadow.
The shadow grew clearer and clearer, eventually turning into Daniel’s appearance.
The puppet had perfectly replicated everything about the main body.
In other words, there were now two Daniels.
Puppet Daniel would remain here to guard this side, while Daniel’s true body broke through the world barrier and arrived beyond the world.
This was his second time leaving this world.
The last time was when he went to Heavenscar.
But this time, it was his first time stepping out in this manner.
Daniel looked out into the distance.
Everywhere was dark chaos.
The starry sky was like a bottomless sea, while he was like a tiny fish at the bottom of that sea.
"So this is the Endless Starfield?"
Desolate and boundless.
Mysterious and profound!
He felt an indescribable sense of alienation.
When one was inside a living world, the moon and sun seemed close enough to touch.
But when one became one star among the endless stars, only then would they realize that everything was unimaginably far away.
The Canaan Star Region.
Oracle-grade Justin suddenly felt something stir in his heart.
With a thought, countless dense threads of karma immediately appeared before his eyes.
Among them, one thread was shining so brightly that it was dazzling!
Justin frowned and reached out to tap that thread.
Buzz—!
The face of a human powerhouse appeared before him.
It was Daniel!
Justin’s brows furrowed even more tightly.
He remembered Faustus.
This person was the Angel King’s enemy.
Back then, the Angel King had sought his help and given him several million units of Light Crystal to kill Faustus.
But at that time, Faustus had been hiding inside a living world, protected by the laws of the world. Not only had Justin failed, but he had also suffered backlash.
Justin looked at Faustus, hesitation flickering in his eyes.
Originally, this person had not been his enemy.
He had been the Angel King’s enemy.
The problem was that Justin had made a move.
Because of that, karma had formed between him and Faustus.
And it was life-and-death karma!
For an Oracle-grade existence, this already counted as a mortal enemy in a fight to the death.
Oracle-grade beings valued karma the most.
Justin could not possibly wait for Faustus to grow up and then fight him fairly.
Powerhouses were not fools.
If one wanted to eliminate weeds, one had to pull them out by the roots.
But he was also afraid of the Fortune Points on Faustus.
Once he attacked, not only would his odds of victory be low, he might even suffer backlash again.
Was he supposed to jump into the same pit twice?
Unless he stood right in front of Faustus now and killed him on the spot...
"He has walked out of the living world..."
Justin calculated his chances of making a move.
Without the protection of the world’s laws, the difficulty had indeed decreased somewhat.
"Don’t rush."
Justin flipped his wrist, and a gemstone appeared in his palm.
"I’m only a level-three Oracle-grade. Relying on myself alone, I can’t see through Faustus’s fate. I’ll borrow this treasure first and take a look at what he will become in the future."
"If he is destined to become a great figure, then forget it."
"But if he is destined to die, then I’ll personally send him on his way!"
He shook his head.
In the end, his own strength was still insufficient.
If he could reach level-six Oracle-grade, then he would not need a treasure at all. He could confidently crush the other party to death!
"Let’s take a look at his future first."
Justin activated the gemstone.
Buzz—!
Justin’s pupils abruptly contracted.
A scene was reflected within his eyes.
A level-six Oracle-grade Justin was crawling at Faustus’s feet, trembling like a sieve.
Faustus stood high above, looking down at him.
As if looking at a worm!

sentences.text: Audacious beyond belief!
Why was this human leader so insane?
According to common sense, shouldn’t one pick on the weakest target first?
But not him.
He went straight for the Godkin.
Did he think his life was too long?
Faustus smiled.
"The Godkin dared to make a move against me, so why wouldn’t I dare to make a move against them?"
"Sage rank powerhouses can’t descend into small worlds.
So what if I seize one of their worlds?"
One had to know that in his previous lives, Aetheria had always been the one being bullied.
Faustus had long since had enough of that.
Why should others be the only ones allowed to attack you?
Now that he had the strength, why couldn’t he attack others?
Just as the Star Chart had written.
The most ideal cycle in this universe was—
To take resources from those who had abundance and give them to those who lacked.
But the truth was—
Resources would be robbed from the arms of the barren and offered up to those who were already wealthy!
To put it plainly, it was the law of the jungle.
The weak were prey to the strong.
So why should the human race be the only one getting robbed?
Conrad looked deeply at Faustus.
This human leader had courage!
No—
He was mad!
Conrad took a deep breath.
"Everything will be decided by you, my lord.
My Starfolk are willing to cooperate with your operation!"
Faustus said calmly,
"Then we’ll act now.
Let’s make the Godkin bleed first."
Conrad had already been tied to the same rope as Faustus.
After the two of them roughly discussed how the attack would proceed, Conrad returned to consult his clansmen about the invasion.
Faustus, meanwhile, returned to the Polaris District.
He took out the items he had seized from the Holy Kingdom’s treasury.
Conrad had helped him undo the seals, so those Divine-grade items could now be used.
At this moment, he was holding a small humanoid doll.
The doll was mottled by the erosion of time, and it looked somewhat old.
But Faustus liked it very much.

chapters.title: Chapter 226 -226-Lose Your Mettle, Lose Everything
paragraphs: Bang—!
The scene before his eyes shattered, as though crushed into dust by an invisible giant hand.
Justin collapsed to the ground, his whole body trembling uncontrollably.
"Future Faustus is actually that powerful..."
At this moment, his heart was filled with regret.
The future he had deduced ended with him being crushed by Faustus. His future was bleak!
Justin hated the Angel King to the bone.
If not for that idiot... he would never have had anything to do with Faustus.
"Angel King, you damned moron...!"
He gnashed his teeth.
How could he still dare to plot against Faustus now?
All Justin wanted was to make amends.
"If I hand the Angel King over to Faustus, maybe I can... no, that still won’t be enough!"
His eyes flickered uncertainly. "I also have to protect Faustus while he’s still weak... Only then might he let bygones be bygones!"
Divine Wind Realm, Divine Descent Hall.
The heads of the major Luminari families had all gathered together.
Each of them wore a different expression, and everyone had something to say.
"Progenitor Camille’s path is almost at its end. The position of Swordlord has to be decided quickly."
"I don’t think there’s any need to decide at all, is there? Haven’t we been doing just fine without a Swordlord?"
"Exactly. The Swordlord is an outdated relic. Why should the fate of our entire race be held in the hands of one person?"
The Luminari were the strongest race in the Divine Wind Realm, with billions of clansmen.
The leaders present here represented the entire Luminari race.
At that moment, a clear voice rang out.

"In Divine Wind Calendar Year 201, the Godkin invaded our world. In Divine Wind Calendar Year 215, unable to endure the Godkin’s oppression any longer, we Luminari rose up in resistance. That year, Progenitor Camille established Lamu Palace and created the position of Swordlord."
"In Divine Wind Calendar Year 6490, which is this year, Progenitor Camille’s life-flame is about to be extinguished..."
The leaders quietly listened to these words.
They knew at least some of this history, but that did not stop them from wanting to abolish the Swordlord.
The Swordlord held the life and death of the entire world in his hands—why?
Why should their lives be decided by someone else?
Shouldn’t every person be the master of their own fate?!
One leader stepped forward and shouted, and immediately, a crowd followed him in making a racket.
"The Godkin haven’t come for thirty thousand years. I don’t think they’ll ever come again."
"Exactly. Progenitor Camille is about to enter extinction. Some people are probably clinging to the Swordlord system because they want to monopolize power for themselves, right?"
"That must be it. We will never agree to this!"
"Our lives are ours to decide!"
The leader who had recited the history of the Divine Wind Realm listened as everyone shouted themselves hoarse in opposition to the Swordlord, and his heart gradually turned cold.
He suddenly stood up and swept his gaze around the hall.
Not a single person stood up to support him.
Some pretended to be mute, while others raised both hands in favor of abolishing the Swordlord.
He alone stood there, isolated, stubbornly holding the line.
He gave a bitter smile. "Progenitor Camille endured all these years alone so that our race could survive, so that our race could preserve its dignity!"
"Who did he do it for? He did it for the Luminari! Without the Swordlord, this world will fall sooner or later. The Luminari will perish sooner or later!"
But his words were met only with a hall full of mockery.
"The Luminari will perish? So just because you open your mouth, we’re doomed? Hahahaha..."
On Mount Lamu, within Lamu Palace.
An old man sat motionless like a stone statue.
Suddenly, a shadow flashed in.
"Vade pays respects to Progenitor Camille!"
He was the very person who had been the only one in Divine Descent Hall to firmly defend the Swordlord system.
Progenitor Camille abruptly opened his eyes, and two dim rays of light flickered in his eye sockets.
Vade looked at Progenitor Camille, and for no reason, his heart ached.
Back then, Progenitor Camille had been astonishingly brilliant, a peerless genius!
He had long since touched the threshold of the peak of quasi-Divine-grade, just one tiny step away from crossing into Divine-grade.
But in the battle against the Godkin years ago, Progenitor Camille had suffered grievous injuries. He had never recovered, and his strength had never been able to advance even a single step further.
Moreover, every single day, Progenitor Camille had to endure immense pain.
A full six thousand years.
Progenitor Camille had carried it all alone for so many years!
At this thought, Vade felt so stifled that he could not speak.
If Progenitor Camille had not been injured back then, he would have become a Divine-grade powerhouse long ago. How would there still be any need for this damned matter of the Swordlord?
As long as Progenitor Camille remained, the Swordlord remained.
And as long as the Swordlord remained, the Luminari could live with their backs straight.
"You’re here..."
Camille spoke faintly. "How did the discussion over the next Swordlord go?"
Vade lowered his head, clenched his fists, and said in a trembling voice, "Progenitor Camille, I... they..."
Camille gave a bitter laugh and shook his head. "I already expected it."
"This world has been at peace for too long. No one remembers anymore what it felt like when the Luminari struggled on the edge of life and death. Times have changed."

His tone was calm. "I hold in my hand something that can blow this entire world flat. Now, no one is willing to see someone else control that bomb. They all want to abolish the Swordlord, don’t they?"
Vade lowered his head even further, his voice filled with helplessness. "Yes, Progenitor Camille."

Camille drew in a deep breath. "Sigh. I can no longer suppress the injuries in my body. Tomorrow will likely be the day of my extinction. After that, whatever happens will no longer be mine to control."
"Progenitor Camille!"
Vade cried out in a trembling voice.
Camille smiled and said, "The Luminari have had a glorious history and a brilliant civilization. While we were here, we already made this stretch of time full enough."
"After I die, I hope you can still guard this light. Do not throw away the entire soul of the Luminari just to cling to life."
Vade nodded. "Yes, Progenitor Camille."
Camille shook his head.
He did not know whether his words would be of any use.
He slowly stood up, and a sword appeared in his hand out of thin air.
It was a sword, and also a weapon capable of destroying this world. It was also a bundle of explosives hanging over the head of every living being.
Destruction or survival—everything rested on a single thought from the Swordlord!
Camille held the sword and walked to Vade’s side, then suddenly asked, "How long has it been since you last looked up at the stars?"
Vade froze. "A very, very long time. So long that I can no longer remember."
Camille smiled faintly. "Though we are all ants crawling in the dust, we still have to look up at the stars from time to time."

"Above us is the Endless Starfield. There are things there that we cannot even imagine. Perhaps it is cruel, or perhaps it is dreamlike. But as long as I think that such unimaginable places exist to be witnessed, I feel that being alive is truly wonderful."
Vade nodded.
He thought that if Progenitor Camille had not been the Swordlord, he would certainly have ventured into the Endless Starfield.
Progenitor Camille loved looking at the stars so much, yet he had never left this world his entire life.
He had not only given his life to his race.
He had also given his dreams to them.
"Go back and tell them."
Camille looked up at the sky and slowly said, "This sword will disappear from this world."
Vade trembled all over.
Camille suddenly smiled. "I will give you one sentence. I will also give it to the Luminari."
Vade said solemnly, "Please speak, Progenitor Camille."
"If you lose your humanity, you will lose much. But if you lose your mettle, you will lose everything."
After Camille finished speaking, he waved his hand.
"Go. I want to be alone for a while."
Vade nodded softly, and his figure instantly vanished from the spot.

"After I die, I hope you can still guard this light.
Do not throw away the entire soul of the Luminari just to cling to life."
Vade nodded.
"Yes, Progenitor Camille."
Camille shook his head.
He did not know whether his words would be of any use.
He slowly stood up, and a sword appeared in his hand out of thin air.
It was a sword, and also a weapon capable of destroying this world.
It was also a bundle of explosives hanging over the head of every living being.
Destruction or survival—everything rested on a single thought from the Swordlord!
Camille held the sword and walked to Vade’s side, then suddenly asked, "How long has it been since you last looked up at the stars?"
Vade froze.
"A very, very long time.
So long that I can no longer remember."
Camille smiled faintly.
"Though we are all ants crawling in the dust, we still have to look up at the stars from time to time."
"Above us is the Endless Starfield.
There are things there that we cannot even imagine.
Perhaps it is cruel, or perhaps it is dreamlike.
But as long as I think that such unimaginable places exist to be witnessed, I feel that being alive is truly wonderful."
Vade nodded.
He thought that if Progenitor Camille had not been the Swordlord, he would certainly have ventured into the Endless Starfield.
Progenitor Camille loved looking at the stars so much, yet he had never left this world his entire life.
He had not only given his life to his race.
He had also given his dreams to them.
"Go back and tell them."
Camille looked up at the sky and slowly said, "This sword will disappear from this world."
Vade trembled all over.
Camille suddenly smiled.
"I will give you one sentence.
I will also give it to the Luminari."
Vade said solemnly, "Please speak, Progenitor Camille."
"If you lose your humanity, you will lose much.
But if you lose your mettle, you will lose everything."
After Camille finished speaking, he waved his hand.
"Go.
I want to be alone for a while."
Vade nodded softly, and his figure instantly vanished from the spot.

chapters.title: Chapter 227 -227-The Fall of the Luminari, Regeneration Crystal
paragraphs: Camille held the sword in his arms and looked up at the sky.
Fifty thousand years ago, when he had still been a young man, he had stood in this very posture.
Fifty thousand years later, now that he was about to die, he was still in this same posture.
The wind howled, lifting Camille’s white hair and stirring up the withered leaves on the ground.
The leaves spun into the air, then drifted back down again.
Camille let out a sigh.
For all these years, he had been like a lion, standing firmly against a pack of wolves.
But he had never imagined that the race behind him would be raised into sheep by his protection.
Now, the sheep blamed the lion for blocking their path.
And the lion was old.
He was about to die.
If the destruction of the Luminari could not be avoided, then perhaps death would be a blessing for him after all.
At the very least, he would not have to witness that heart-wrenching scene with his own eyes!
Divine Wind Calendar, Year 6490.
Luminari Progenitor Camille passed away and was buried within Lamu Palace.
Five years later, Lamu Palace was torn down and reduced to a pile of rubble.
The entire Luminari race celebrated.
There was no Swordlord anymore.
At long last, they could decide their own life and death.
Divine Wind Calendar, Year 6500.
The Godkin invaded!
The Luminari could not withstand them at all. Their entire race was captured and turned into divine slaves.
Every Luminari powerhouse above legendary-grade had their Immortal Singularity drained dry and died without exception.
From then on, billions of clansmen became slaves and servants, living lives worse than death.
The Luminari civilization was utterly destroyed!
Outside the realm, in the depths of the void.
An inexplicable palpitation suddenly slammed into Faustus’s heart.
Faustus’s eyes narrowed.
It had come again!
This feeling was exactly the same as last time.
But this time, the palpitation was especially intense, as though something in the unseen depths of fate was staring at him through the void.
Whoosh—!
All the lines of karma on his body suddenly emerged.
They appeared so abruptly that he had not activated them himself at all.
"Is some powerhouse spying on me by following the lines of karma?"
Faustus stared at those lines, but he could not see anything.
He could not quite understand it.
"Perhaps my Destiny Law of Causality is still too shallow."
He shook his head and withdrew the karmic lines.
Just then, a Starfall Isle slowly appeared before his eyes.
"Starfall Isle?"
Faustus blinked, and a faint smile appeared on his lips.
"Starfolk, Mara, greets you, my lord."
"Starfolk, Conrad, greets you, my lord."
Two figures appeared before Faustus.
Faustus nodded. "Set off! Divine Wind Realm!"
Conrad invited Faustus onto Starfall Isle. Then, they sped toward Divine Wind Realm.
Before long, Starfall Isle stopped outside the world barrier of Divine Wind Realm.
Conrad gazed at the invisible screen before him, his expression incomparably excited.
Finally...
The Starfolk were finally about to have a place where they could take root!
"Break the world barrier."
Faustus stood with his hands behind his back, his tone calm. "There is no need to worry about alarming the living beings of this realm. Use your full strength."
Conrad took a deep breath. "Yes, my lord."
He could not help sighing inwardly. The feeling of having someone backing him up was truly reassuring.
If he had been alone, he would definitely have had to act with extreme caution.
Conrad flew down before the barrier of Divine Wind Realm.
He stretched out both hands. Countless runes lit up from his body, circling and dancing around him.
Those runes surged toward his palms, transforming into two masses of energy. Immediately after, a powerful aura spread out from within those two masses of energy.
Faustus’s eyes lit up.
That was the Strength of a sage!
Conrad was a quasi-sage, only without the sage rank.
In truth, he had already gained preliminary mastery over Divine-grade Strength.
Conrad pushed both hands forward. The two masses of energy roared out and slammed into the world barrier.
Endless energy poured from his palms, crashing against that barrier like a raging tide.
Mara stared nervously at Conrad.
She knew that this was Conrad’s first time truly attacking a world barrier.
It had to succeed!
Boom—!
There was an explosive sound.
The world barrier could no longer withstand that tremendous force and shattered apart.
The barrier had successfully been broken.
Faustus immediately nodded.
Mara instantly gave the order, and Starfall Isle sailed through the shattered gap in the barrier into Divine Wind Realm.
Conrad had already charged in ahead of them.
Whoosh—!
Starfall Isle landed steadily within Divine Wind Realm.
[Ding! You have discovered Divine Wind Realm. Mental State +1!]
[Ding! Congratulations, you have become the first player to step into a living world beyond your home star system! Special reward: Regeneration Gem (supreme-grade) ×1!]
Faustus listened to the system prompts ringing in his ears, his brows furrowing tightly.
Mental State?
Daniel was slightly taken aback.
This was the first time he had ever seen such a thing.
In his previous lives, he had never heard of it at all. The only thing he could think of was that advancements in things like the Law of Causality might require Mental State.
As for this supreme-grade Regeneration Gem—revival-type items and skills had always been extremely rare.
Still, since it had been given by the system, it had to be something good.
He subconsciously opened his backpack.
Mental State +1.
The number looked pitifully small, but Faustus knew clearly that the system never acted without reason.
This single point of Mental State might very well be a stepping stone, one he himself might not have been able to touch for who knew how long.
"Mental State... The more of it I have, the better."
The corners of his lips curled upward.
Others had to accumulate it one point at a time.
He was different.
He had Millionfold Boost!
Immediately, he opened the guild warehouse and listed that insignificant point of Mental State for sale.
[Ding! You have sold Mental State ×1 to Doom Guild for 1 copper coin, triggering Millionfold Boost!]
"Quantity boost."
Faustus did not hesitate.
Buzz—!
[Ding! Congratulations, you have obtained Mental State ×1,000,000!]
Faustus opened his eyes, and a sharp gleam flashed through them.
One million points of Mental State!
He was in no hurry to study it. There was no need to rush. It would not be too late to study it when he needed it.
He turned his gaze toward the second reward.
"Regeneration Gem... supreme-grade."
He frowned slightly.
Revival-type items had always been rare, but supreme-grade...
It was neither low nor especially high.
In Aetheria, it could be considered a realm-guarding treasure.
But when placed against the vast Endless Starfield, it was not enough.
Without hesitation, he listed the Regeneration Gem in the guild warehouse.
[Ding! You have sold Regeneration Gem (supreme-grade) ×1 to Doom Guild for 1 copper coin, triggering Millionfold Boost!]
"Quality boost."
He took a deep breath, as though placing a bet.
Light erupted!
The gem glowing with a faint golden luster trembled violently in his palm, as though gripped by an invisible giant hand and repeatedly hammered, forged, and tempered.
Cracks spread across its surface, only to heal in the very next instant!
[Ding! Congratulations, you have obtained Regeneration Crystal (Divine-grade) ×1!]
Faustus held that crystal in his palm and felt the heavy fluctuations of law within it. The corners of his mouth slowly rose.
"It worked."
[Regeneration Crystal (Divine-grade)]
Effect: Can be used on a target below Divine-grade to regenerate them.
Note: Only effective on targets who have been dead for no more than one minute.
Special: After regeneration, the target retains all strength and memories from before death and regenerates in peak condition.
Description: A little toy casually made by an Oracle-grade existence out of boredom...
After Faustus finished reading, he secretly praised it.
This was simply a top-tier treasure!
It could regenerate powerhouses below Divine-grade. In other words, even quasi-sages could be regenerated!
Too incredible.
However, the timing had to be precise. There was only a one-minute window.
And it could not be used on just anyone.
Regenerating a Godkin powerhouse?
That would be true stupidity.
He put away the crystal and continued observing.

chapters.title: Chapter 228 -228-Fifth-Class Race, Starsea Covenant
paragraphs: Before long, Conrad returned to Starfall Isle.
"My lord, I went out and made a brief investigation into this world’s situation," Conrad said.
Faustus nodded.
Conrad had always been cautious. That was one of his strengths.
"What did you find?"
Conrad pondered for a moment, then a strange expression appeared on his face.
"My lord, I discovered that this world’s original native civilization is already gone."
"The ones living here now are all Godthralls that the Godkin captured from various places."
"Godthralls?"
Faustus raised an eyebrow.
Conrad explained, "My lord, you may not know this, but the Godkin divide all living beings into several ranks."

"The first class, of course, is the Godkin themselves. They stand high above all others and don’t need to do anything. The second class are allied races, who help the Godkin manage certain planes. The third class are covenant races. They have a little freedom and some basic authority. The fourth class are lowly races, with almost no freedom and almost no authority. And the fifth class are Godthralls!"

"The first- and second-class races can slaughter them at will, and even the third class can bully them however they like. Godthralls are nothing more than tools for the Godkin. They do the hardest and most exhausting labor—mining, planting, and even feeding divine beasts with the flesh and blood of their own kind... Their status is no different from livestock."
Faustus listened carefully.
Inwardly, he began to wonder what class the human race of Aetheria counted as in the eyes of the Godkin.
After thinking it over, they were probably only fourth-class lowly races—little freedom, low authority.
As for Godthralls... humanity had not fallen to that point yet.
The Godkin treated Godthralls like beasts of burden.
The human race had fled from the Endless Starfield and had fought the Godkin for so many years. At the very least, they had not been reduced to the fifth class.
But in the end, being fourth class was only slightly better in name. It was not all that different from being Godthralls.
The human race could not feel proud simply because they were not Godthralls.
In this starry sky, humanity also had to become the ones who made the rules.
They had to charge toward that supreme and peerless racial status!
Faustus asked, "We must have alerted the Godkin experts in this world. What are they doing?"
A cold gleam flashed in Conrad’s eyes. "My lord, they are already prepared and are gathering their army. Also... several demi-sages are stationed here."
Demi-sages...
There was not the slightest ripple on Faustus’s face. He merely smiled faintly. "Since we have to fight anyway, it’s better to settle this quickly."
"But let me make one thing clear first—this world will be split evenly between you and me."
When Conrad heard this, he was instantly overwhelmed with gratitude. "Thank you, my lord!"
He had already inspected this Divine Wind Realm. It was a complete minor world.
The land was vast, resources were abundant, and there were countless good things here.
Conrad’s entire race only numbered a few hundred million. One-fifth of the territory would already be enough for them to survive and slowly develop.
The terms Faustus offered were enough to make him overjoyed.
A surge of gratitude welled up in Conrad’s heart.
Faustus looked at Conrad’s expression and merely smiled.
In this battle, Faustus was only one person.
Meanwhile, Conrad and his clansmen had mobilized their entire race.
For the sake of their own territory, they would definitely charge at the front and contribute the most.
Faustus could not only complete his class change quest, but also obtain half of a minor world for free. This deal was all profit, no loss.
As for Conrad’s gratitude, that was merely something he had picked up along the way.
"This is only the first world."
Faustus continued, "My goal is to occupy every plane controlled by the Godkin!"
Conrad sucked in a breath of cold air. "My lord’s sights are set on the Endless Starfield. I am far too lacking in comparison."
"There’s no need for unnecessary words. Prepare for war."
Faustus’s gaze turned toward the distance, his tone calm.
"Guests have arrived."
Faustus raised his eyes and looked into the distance. Countless powerful auras surged closer from afar, like a tide.
"Those are the garrison legions the Godkin left to guard this world," Conrad said in a deep voice.
Boom—!
The aura around Conrad erupted violently.
At the same time, the entire war machine of Starfall Isle activated at full power.
Countless Starfolk warriors formed ranks and marched out, a dark mass stretching across the sky and covering the land.
Swish, swish, swish—!
Peak supreme-grade experts stood solemnly behind Conrad.
Everyone’s expression was grave as they faced the powerful enemy before them.
War had come!
Not only did they not retreat, their eyes instead blazed with surging battle intent!
Boom, boom, boom, boom...
From the four directions around Starfall Isle, four legions pressed forward at the same time.
Those were the Godkin’s troops. They were led by Godkin experts, but the warriors charging at the very front were all cannon fodder from other races.
The Godkin ruled over more than a dozen planes. Naturally, they had no shortage of loyal slave races and followers.
Moreover, true Godkin experts were extremely few in number. They would not personally enter the battlefield easily.
The four legions stopped not far from Starfall Isle, surrounding it so tightly that not even water could pass through.
At that moment, a Godkin expert flew out and landed steadily in front of Starfall Isle.
Faustus’s gaze fell on that figure.
A demi-sage!
At this moment, the Godkin demi-sage’s face was filled with rage.
The Divine Wind Realm was Godkin territory, and the Godkin were one of the strongest major forces in the starry sky of myriad races.
Yet now, someone actually dared to break through the world barrier and barge into Godkin territory to run wild?
This was simply a slap in the Godkin’s face!
He sized up Starfall Isle from top to bottom, then spoke furiously.
"You starry-sky vagrants have truly grown too bold!"
"Instead of staying obediently in the Endless Starfield, you came to a life world to seize territory?"
He raised his hand and pointed at Starfall Isle, so angry that his voice trembled. "Have you forgotten the Starsea Covenant? Or do you take my Godkin race for easy prey?"
Faustus raised an eyebrow and turned to ask Conrad, "Starsea Covenant? What is that?"
Conrad blinked, then explained, "The Endless Starfield places great importance on life worlds. No matter which star region it is, there are similar regulations."
"The covenant states that if starry-sky vagrants or Astral Corsairs attack a life world, all major forces in the local star region will join forces to suppress them."
So that was it...
Faustus nodded, but he did not take it seriously at all.
What a bullshit treaty!
So-called treaties were forever shackles placed on the weak, and sharp blades used by the strong to consolidate their interests.
"Enough nonsense."
He said indifferently, "Kill him."
Conrad nodded in response and, without another word, charged straight at the Godkin demi-sage.
Behind him, the peak supreme-grade experts led the Starfolk legion forward like a surging tide, crashing toward the Godkin garrison army.
Seeing this, the Godkin demi-sage felt his scalp go numb instead.
When he saw Conrad charging over, he did not hesitate at all. He turned and immediately withdrew into the depths of the army, commanding the troops to meet the attack.
Boom—!
The warriors of the Godkin legion simultaneously burned their Immortal Singularities, and their auras instantly soared to the peak of supreme-grade.
At the same time, the garrison legion’s Divine Domain unfolded.
In the void, a long spear and a beast claw appeared!
Wait!
Faustus’s pupils constricted.
The long spear was indeed a Divine Domain, but that beast claw...
The aura contained within that beast claw actually carried a trace of sage-rank charm!

Conrad sucked in a breath of cold air.
"My lord’s sights are set on the Endless Starfield.
I am far too lacking in comparison."
"There’s no need for unnecessary words.
Prepare for war."
Faustus’s gaze turned toward the distance, his tone calm.
"Guests have arrived."
Faustus raised his eyes and looked into the distance.
Countless powerful auras surged closer from afar, like a tide.
"Those are the garrison legions the Godkin left to guard this world," Conrad said in a deep voice.
Boom—!
The aura around Conrad erupted violently.
At the same time, the entire war machine of Starfall Isle activated at full power.
Countless Starfolk warriors formed ranks and marched out, a dark mass stretching across the sky and covering the land.
Swish, swish, swish—!
Peak supreme-grade experts stood solemnly behind Conrad.
Everyone’s expression was grave as they faced the powerful enemy before them.
War had come!
Not only did they not retreat, their eyes instead blazed with surging battle intent!
Boom, boom, boom, boom...
From the four directions around Starfall Isle, four legions pressed forward at the same time.
Those were the Godkin’s troops.
They were led by Godkin experts, but the warriors charging at the very front were all cannon fodder from other races.
The Godkin ruled over more than a dozen planes.
Naturally, they had no shortage of loyal slave races and followers.
Moreover, true Godkin experts were extremely few in number.
They would not personally enter the battlefield easily.
The four legions stopped not far from Starfall Isle, surrounding it so tightly that not even water could pass through.
At that moment, a Godkin expert flew out and landed steadily in front of Starfall Isle.
Faustus’s gaze fell on that figure.
A demi-sage!
At this moment, the Godkin demi-sage’s face was filled with rage.
The Divine Wind Realm was Godkin territory, and the Godkin were one of the strongest major forces in the starry sky of myriad races.
Yet now, someone actually dared to break through the world barrier and barge into Godkin territory to run wild?
This was simply a slap in the Godkin’s face!
He sized up Starfall Isle from top to bottom, then spoke furiously.
"You starry-sky vagrants have truly grown too bold!"
"Instead of staying obediently in the Endless Starfield, you came to a life world to seize territory?"
He raised his hand and pointed at Starfall Isle, so angry that his voice trembled.
"Have you forgotten the Starsea Covenant?
Or do you take my Godkin race for easy prey?"
Faustus raised an eyebrow and turned to ask Conrad, "Starsea Covenant?
What is that?"
Conrad blinked, then explained, "The Endless Starfield places great importance on life worlds.
No matter which star region it is, there are similar regulations."
"The covenant states that if starry-sky vagrants or Astral Corsairs attack a life world, all major forces in the local star region will join forces to suppress them."
So that was it...
Faustus nodded, but he did not take it seriously at all.
What a bullshit treaty!
So-called treaties were forever shackles placed on the weak, and sharp blades used by the strong to consolidate their interests.
"Enough nonsense."
He said indifferently, "Kill him."
Conrad nodded in response and, without another word, charged straight at the Godkin demi-sage.
Behind him, the peak supreme-grade experts led the Starfolk legion forward like a surging tide, crashing toward the Godkin garrison army.
Seeing this, the Godkin demi-sage felt his scalp go numb instead.
When he saw Conrad charging over, he did not hesitate at all.
He turned and immediately withdrew into the depths of the army, commanding the troops to meet the attack.
Boom—!
The warriors of the Godkin legion simultaneously burned their Immortal Singularities, and their auras instantly soared to the peak of supreme-grade.
At the same time, the garrison legion’s Divine Domain unfolded.
In the void, a long spear and a beast claw appeared!
Wait!
Faustus’s pupils constricted.
The long spear was indeed a Divine Domain, but that beast claw...
The aura contained within that beast claw actually carried a trace of sage-rank charm!

chapters.title: Chapter 229 -229-Strength That Crushed Everything in Its Path
paragraphs: His memories of sage rank were far too deep.
Back in the God realm, he had held the Law of Causality in his hands, yet inside a sage’s sage rank, he could only rely on self-destruction to escape with his life.
After that, he had relied on Immortal Revival to massacre a city and threaten Divine-grade experts.
No one understood better than him just how terrifying sage rank was.
This beast claw was very similar to the sword of Divine Wrath. Both carried a portion of sage-rank Strength.
Just then, runes flashed in Conrad’s hand, condensing into a rune longsword. With a single slash, he shattered the Divine Domain spear opposite him.
But when that beast claw came slamming down, his rune longsword instantly collapsed like paper.
The beast claw pressed its advantage. In the blink of an eye, it blotted out the sky and covered the sun, smashing down at Conrad with terrifying force.
Divine-grade experts possessed the ability known as Thoughtstep.
Although Conrad was only a demi-sage and had yet to awaken sage rank, he had still barely grasped Thoughtstep.
With a flicker of thought, he narrowly dodged.
"Holy Relic!"
Conrad’s face turned pale as he stared fixedly at that beast claw.

A Holy Relic was a treasure containing a portion of sage-rank power. It was personally created by Divine-grade experts at an enormous cost, and its might was terrifyingly great. Ordinary demi-sages were simply no match for it.
Conrad had always been cautious. Naturally, he would not clash head-on with such a threat.
He could only dodge, and for the moment, he had no strength to fight back.
The battle situation in the other three directions was not looking optimistic either.
The Godkin garrison legions all had identical configurations.
The legendary-grade legion experts burned their Immortal Singularities, erupting with supreme-grade strength, while also possessing both Divine Domains and Holy Relics.
The Starfolk only had ordinary Divine Domains. Faced with the attacks of the Holy Relics, their defensive lines were on the verge of collapse.
Faustus understood.
So this was the proper way to fight a world war.
Swish—!
Ninety-nine clones appeared at the same time, moving to meet those Holy Relics.
Holy light gathered in Faustus’s palm.
Under the enhancement of a massive amount of Immortal Singularity, the holy light shattered space and distorted light, transforming into a dark black hole.
"Break for me!"
Boom, boom, boom...!
The holy light and the Holy Relics collided with a thunderous crash.
Both sides were annihilated into nothingness.
At that moment, the warriors of the Godkin legions were stunned.
Conrad was stunned as well. That Godkin demi-sage was equally dumbfounded.
The Holy Relic was just... gone?
Hiss—!
Conrad sucked in a breath of cold air.
At this moment, he finally saw Faustus’s true strength.
He was strong.
Truly strong—ridiculously strong!
Far stronger than Conrad, a demi-sage!
When he recalled how he had nearly fought Faustus back then, cold sweat instantly broke out across his back.
In front of a Holy Relic, Conrad could only flee with his head in his hands.
But what about Faustus?
He had directly attacked and violently shattered it in one blow.
The gap between them was clear at a glance.
The morale of the Starfolk warriors instantly soared.
Without the Holy Relics, both sides had returned to the same starting line.
Who was afraid of whom?
Faustus stepped steadily forward.
With one step, he arrived before the legion where the Godkin demi-sage was located.
His clones also reached the other three battlefields at the same time.
The destiny woven by the Law of Causality shifted invisibly.
"Go and listen to the wails of those countless souls slain by Divine Wrath!"
"Arrow of Judgment!"
Light suddenly erupted, like a scorching sun descending into the mortal world.
The warriors of the Godkin garrison legions melted away silently like snowmen in spring.
Including that Godkin demi-sage...
All annihilated!
Instant kill!
Faustus alone, with his own strength, wiped out every Godkin guard in the entire Divine Wind Realm.
The whole process was effortless and understated, as though he had merely wiped dust from a tabletop.
The Starfolk warriors were all dumbstruck.
They watched helplessly as the enemies who had been burning their Immortal Singularities and fighting desperately against them one second were dead and gone the next.
The scene was indescribably horrifying.
Mara was just as shocked.
She was grateful that Conrad had chosen the right path. Otherwise, the fate of the Starfolk would have been extermination.
Conrad’s eyes were equally wide, his expression as if he had seen a ghost.
Was this still human?
Instantly killing a Holy Relic. Instantly killing a demi-sage. Instantly killing four great legions and tens of millions of legendary-grade warriors...
This kind of Strength actually came from a legendary-grade expert...
It was simply absurd.
Compared to him, Conrad was no different from trash.
Fortunately.
Fortunately, he had chosen correctly back then!
When he thought of what would have happened to his people if he had chosen the wrong path, Conrad could not help but shudder.
This Faustus was far too terrifying!
The Starfolk absolutely could not come into conflict with him!
At Faustus’s ear, notifications about obtaining Primal Spirit rang out continuously.
Moreover, rewards such as Divine Blood, Divine Bone, and Divine Soul were all complete.
It could be considered a fairly significant harvest.
As for ordinary equipment, skill books, gold coins, and experience, he had long since stopped caring about them.
[Ding! You have completed your class change quest!]
[Ding! You have obtained [Wind Elemental Core] ×1!]
[Ding! You have obtained [Nature Elemental Core] ×1!]
[Ding! You have obtained [Forbidden-Grade Archer Class Awakening Scroll] ×1!]
"Elemental cores."
Faustus took a deep breath, staring at the seven faintly glowing gemstones in his backpack.
He was another major step closer to unlocking the seal on the Chronoverse Prologue Codex.
Once he gathered ten of them, that ancient codex, which recorded the mysteries at the source of the Laws of Time and Space, would open its gates to him.
He already had seven in hand now.
Only the final three were missing!
He took out the Class Awakening Scroll and chose to use it.
[Ding! The seal on your experience bar has been lifted. You may continue leveling up.]
He was currently stuck at Level 260. There was still an entire gap of 140 levels before he reached supreme-grade.
After using this scroll, it could push him to Level 280!
[Ding! Your level has increased! Current level: 261. You have obtained 20 attribute points.]
[Ding! Your level has increased! Current level: 270. You have obtained 20 attribute points.]
[Ding! Your level has increased! Current level: 280. You have obtained 20 attribute points.]
One golden light after another exploded from his body, like fireworks in the dark night.

[Notice: You have not yet completed the next stage of your class change quest. Your level cap has been sealed. Overflow experience has been stored in the Exp Pool. Please complete your class change quest as soon as possible to continue leveling up.]
Level 280!
Faustus lowered his head and glanced at his panel, then raised it again.
He remembered that he had obtained a level achievement back when he reached Level 260.
Why was there nothing afterward?
However, he did not dwell on it too much. The system’s notification had already sounded.
[Ding! You have obtained a new forbidden-grade archer class change quest. Do you accept?]
"Accept!"
[Ding! You have accepted the class change quest [Swordlord]. New quest content has been added to your quest log. Please check it for details!]
Faustus casually opened the quest log.
[Swordlord]
[Forbidden-Grade Archer Class Change Quest]
Restriction: Forbidden-Grade Archer
Quest Difficulty: Epic-Grade

Quest Objective: Beneath Mount Lamu in the Divine Wind Realm lies an unnamed grave. Buried within the grave is a sword. That sword is connected to the source of destruction deep underground and can instantly blow the entire world into fragments. Obtain this sword, and you will truly grasp this world’s lifeline.

Quest Description: The first Swordlord, Camille, is buried beneath Mount Lamu together with his sword. The survival and destruction of the entire world are closely tied to this sword. Only the one who holds it is the true master of this world.
Time Limit: None
Quest Reward: [Epic-Grade Forbidden Spell: Icefire Judgment] ×1, [Forbidden-Grade Archer Class Awakening Scroll] ×1.
Faustus read the quest details again from beginning to end.
The rewards were good.
An epic-grade forbidden spell had enough weight.
But this quest itself...
It was somewhat strange.
Swordlord?
A single sword could decide the fate of an entire world?
In other words, even if he conquered this world, it would not truly be over.
If this sword fell into someone else’s hands, then if that person became unhappy, the entire world would be gone?
