chapters.title: Chapter 230 -230-Chrono Reversal Circle
paragraphs: With that thought, he turned to Conrad and said,
"You all stay here and stabilize the situation. I need to go somewhere."
By now, Conrad’s awe toward Faustus had sunk deep into his bones.
In his eyes, Faustus was a Divine-grade powerhouse. No—he was even more terrifying than a Divine-grade powerhouse.
"As you command, my lord."
Conrad answered honestly and respectfully.
Daniel nodded, then shot into the air and rushed toward the coordinates.
Taking over a world was not that simple. The cities, the resources, the population, and all those various special buildings had to be seized and brought under control one by one!
Once his class change quest was complete, he would open the portal interface and move a batch of NPCs over from Aetheria to slowly clean up the situation.
Mount Lamu.
Daniel landed at the coordinate point.
Without wasting words, he raised his right foot and stomped heavily on the ground.
Boom—!
The earth split open in an instant. Cracks spread in every direction like a spiderweb, revealing a tomb buried deep underground for who knew how many years.
"Rise."
Daniel raised a hand, and the wind elements surged out as if they had come alive.
The entire tomb was uprooted from the ground. The outer concealment shattered and scattered everywhere, exposing the coffin within.
The coffin opened.
Inside, there was only a corpse and a sword.
The corpse had not decayed. It looked as though it had only been buried yesterday, and an astonishing aura still faintly lingered around it.
The sword’s blade was bright and polished, lying there alone beside the corpse.
"So this is the sword?"
Daniel reached out and beckoned from afar.
The sword flew out of the coffin and landed steadily in his palm.
However—!
A terrifyingly powerful wave of mind power crashed into his head like a tsunami.
The impact was so overwhelming that it felt as if ten thousand steel needles had pierced through his skull at the same time. The pain nearly made him lose his footing.
Clang—!
His hand loosened, and the sword fell to the ground, letting out a crisp ring.
That deadly mind power vanished in an instant.
Daniel took a breath, and his mind finally cleared.
He lowered his head and stared at the sword, stunned for quite a while.
What a domineering sword.
What a domineering spiritual impact!
He was not even afraid of Divine-grade powerhouses, yet this sword had actually caught him off guard.
But he soon figured it out.
This sword was not simple.
What made it unusual was that the Strength of a certain powerhouse was sealed inside it.
The form of that Strength was very similar to a sage rank.
What he was facing was not a sword, but a sage rank.

It was just that this sage rank was incomplete, full of holes everywhere. It did not look like something opened up by a Divine-grade powerhouse. Instead, it was more like the work of someone stuck at the peak of demi-sage rank, someone who could not cross that final threshold no matter what, and had forcefully stuffed their own sage rank into the sword!
This was an unorthodox path.
And the price was that breaking through to Divine-grade would become extremely difficult!
"Why?"
Daniel shook his head.
A powerhouse who dared to do something like this was basically walking down a path no one else had ever taken.
It was like standing in a vast desert and refusing to follow the tracks left behind by predecessors, insisting instead on charging toward a place no one had ever gone.
There might be a road there.
Or there might be nothing at all.
"If I can’t subdue this sword, the quest can’t be completed."
Daniel frowned.
If he could not control this sword, then he could not control the fate of this world.
After pondering for a while, he understood.
This powerhouse must have feared that after his death, the sword would fall into someone else’s hands.
So he had simply bound himself and the sword together.
Without Divine-grade strength, there was no chance of subduing this sword.
But a Divine-grade powerhouse could not descend into this small world.
In other words, this powerhouse had been determined to lock this sword away completely.
No one was allowed to touch it.
Daniel felt a little headache coming on.
Wait—!
A flash of light suddenly streaked through the pitch-black void of his mind.
An idea struck Daniel.
Since only the Swordlord himself could undo the restriction on this sword, then he could just let the man do it himself!
His gaze fell on the corpse inside the coffin.
Buried together with the sword—who else could it be but the Swordlord?
He took an item out of his backpack.
It was not impossible to meet the Swordlord himself.
[Chrono Reversal Circle(Divine-grade)]
Category: One-use spacetime Holy Relic
Grade: Divine-grade
Effect: Upon activation, it can reverse the flow of time within a selected area, causing shattered time to piece itself back together and allowing fragments of the past to reappear.

Consumption: The farther the reversal and the longer it is maintained, the more Immortal Singularity must be sacrificed. The greater the sacrifice, the deeper the reversal and the longer time can be suspended in reverse.

Inscription: Only a high Oracle-grade existence who has glimpsed the past and future and grasped authority over the laws of spacetime has the ability to forge such a forbidden vessel that overturns fate.
Immortal Singularity?
The corner of Daniel’s mouth lifted.
He had the Replica Crystal, which could endlessly replicate Immortal Singularity fragments.
Immortal Singularity was something he did not lack at all!
He selected the area around Mount Lamu and activated the Chrono Reversal Circle.
[Prompt: This action will consume a massive amount of Immortal Singularity. Confirm?]
"Confirm."
[Ding! Item activated!]
In a single instant, hundreds of thousands of Immortal Singularity vanished into thin air!
The Chrono Reversal Circle began to move.
The space before him rippled like the surface of a lake wrinkled by the wind. The once-dead air began to stir in circles, spreading out layer by layer.
Spacetime began to flow backward.
Daniel stood outside the circle and watched everything before him reverse with his own eyes!

The ground that he had shattered with one stomp began to close and restore itself at a speed visible to the naked eye, as if someone were picking up the pieces of a broken plate and putting them back together one by one.
The sword also followed the reversal of time and flew back into the coffin on its own.

The scattered stones around the coffin returned to their original positions, reassembling into the tomb chamber. Then the chamber sank back underground, becoming once again that unknown grave no one had ever discovered.
The spacetime around him kept changing, and soon, everything returned to the way it had looked when Daniel first arrived.
Watching time reverse was like watching a play being performed backward.
[Prompt: You have consumed 1,000,000 Immortal Singularity.]
Daniel listened to the prompts ringing repeatedly beside his ear, but he was not panicked at all.
Before coming to Divine Wind Realm, he had already replicated a vast amount of Immortal Singularity. He was not afraid of running out.
What he cared about more right now was the scene in front of him.
Not because the scene itself was so shocking, but because this item was simply too heaven-defying.
Something casually made by an Oracle-grade existence already contained such profound spacetime laws.
If he were to face an existence of that level in person, just how terrifying would that be?
With a wave of their hand, they could turn him into a swaddled infant, or directly reduce him to a pile of withered bones.
Who could withstand that?
And there was more.
Back when he had forcibly initiated the World War, he had encountered a supreme powerhouse capable of roaming through the Time River.
That human ancestor could freely move between the past and the future, and could even attack enemies across all timelines at once!
Against someone like that, even Immortal Revival would be useless.
They could uproot his existence from any point in time and any point in space.
By then, even if he could regenerate infinitely, he would only fall into an endless cycle of "revival—death—revival—death."
How would that be any different from true death?
Thinking of this, Daniel’s obsession with unlocking the Chronoverse Prologue Codex deepened even further.
"As long as I unlock the Chronoverse Prologue Codex, I’ll be able to touch the threshold of the laws of spacetime."
"With a method like this time reversal, I won’t need to rely on any item. I’ll be able to use it myself. Whether it’s for killing, saving my life, or anything else, it’ll be a heaven-defying skill."
He took a deep breath.
He was only short three elemental cores.
A small problem!
At that moment, as time continued reversing, increasingly obvious changes began to appear within the spacetime inside the great circle.
Daniel stared fixedly ahead.
Within his field of vision, scene after scene began to emerge.
Countless fleeing beings crowded onto this mountain, crying to the heavens and wailing toward Mount Lamu.
"Progenitor Camille, we should never have refused to listen to you back then!"
"Progenitor Camille! Progenitor Camille! The Luminari are finished! We are about to be destroyed by our own hands!"
"Progenitor Camille, please come back and save us!"
"We were wrong! We were wrong! The Luminari... are doomed!"
"Our civilization is going to perish... We were wrong!"

sentences.text: With that thought, he turned to Conrad and said,
"You all stay here and stabilize the situation.
I need to go somewhere."
By now, Conrad’s awe toward Faustus had sunk deep into his bones.
In his eyes, Faustus was a Divine-grade powerhouse.
No—he was even more terrifying than a Divine-grade powerhouse.
"As you command, my lord."
Conrad answered honestly and respectfully.
Daniel nodded, then shot into the air and rushed toward the coordinates.
Taking over a world was not that simple.
The cities, the resources, the population, and all those various special buildings had to be seized and brought under control one by one!
Once his class change quest was complete, he would open the portal interface and move a batch of NPCs over from Aetheria to slowly clean up the situation.
Mount Lamu.
Daniel landed at the coordinate point.
Without wasting words, he raised his right foot and stomped heavily on the ground.
Boom—!
The earth split open in an instant.
Cracks spread in every direction like a spiderweb, revealing a tomb buried deep underground for who knew how many years.
"Rise."
Daniel raised a hand, and the wind elements surged out as if they had come alive.
The entire tomb was uprooted from the ground.
The outer concealment shattered and scattered everywhere, exposing the coffin within.
The coffin opened.
Inside, there was only a corpse and a sword.
The corpse had not decayed.
It looked as though it had only been buried yesterday, and an astonishing aura still faintly lingered around it.
The sword’s blade was bright and polished, lying there alone beside the corpse.
"So this is the sword?"
Daniel reached out and beckoned from afar.
The sword flew out of the coffin and landed steadily in his palm.
However—!
A terrifyingly powerful wave of mind power crashed into his head like a tsunami.
The impact was so overwhelming that it felt as if ten thousand steel needles had pierced through his skull at the same time.
The pain nearly made him lose his footing.
Clang—!
His hand loosened, and the sword fell to the ground, letting out a crisp ring.
That deadly mind power vanished in an instant.
Daniel took a breath, and his mind finally cleared.
He lowered his head and stared at the sword, stunned for quite a while.
What a domineering sword.
What a domineering spiritual impact!
He was not even afraid of Divine-grade powerhouses, yet this sword had actually caught him off guard.
But he soon figured it out.
This sword was not simple.
What made it unusual was that the Strength of a certain powerhouse was sealed inside it.
The form of that Strength was very similar to a sage rank.
What he was facing was not a sword, but a sage rank.
It was just that this sage rank was incomplete, full of holes everywhere.
It did not look like something opened up by a Divine-grade powerhouse.

Instead, it was more like the work of someone stuck at the peak of demi-sage rank, someone who could not cross that final threshold no matter what, and had forcefully stuffed their own sage rank into the sword!
This was an unorthodox path.
And the price was that breaking through to Divine-grade would become extremely difficult!
"Why?"
Daniel shook his head.
A powerhouse who dared to do something like this was basically walking down a path no one else had ever taken.
It was like standing in a vast desert and refusing to follow the tracks left behind by predecessors, insisting instead on charging toward a place no one had ever gone.
There might be a road there.
Or there might be nothing at all.
"If I can’t subdue this sword, the quest can’t be completed."
Daniel frowned.
If he could not control this sword, then he could not control the fate of this world.
After pondering for a while, he understood.
This powerhouse must have feared that after his death, the sword would fall into someone else’s hands.
So he had simply bound himself and the sword together.
Without Divine-grade strength, there was no chance of subduing this sword.
But a Divine-grade powerhouse could not descend into this small world.
In other words, this powerhouse had been determined to lock this sword away completely.
No one was allowed to touch it.
Daniel felt a little headache coming on.
Wait—!
A flash of light suddenly streaked through the pitch-black void of his mind.
An idea struck Daniel.
Since only the Swordlord himself could undo the restriction on this sword, then he could just let the man do it himself!
His gaze fell on the corpse inside the coffin.
Buried together with the sword—who else could it be but the Swordlord?
He took an item out of his backpack.
It was not impossible to meet the Swordlord himself.
[Chrono Reversal Circle(Divine-grade)]
Category: One-use spacetime Holy Relic
Grade: Divine-grade
Effect: Upon activation, it can reverse the flow of time within a selected area, causing shattered time to piece itself back together and allowing fragments of the past to reappear.
Consumption: The farther the reversal and the longer it is maintained, the more Immortal Singularity must be sacrificed.
The greater the sacrifice, the deeper the reversal and the longer time can be suspended in reverse.

Inscription: Only a high Oracle-grade existence who has glimpsed the past and future and grasped authority over the laws of spacetime has the ability to forge such a forbidden vessel that overturns fate.
Immortal Singularity?
The corner of Daniel’s mouth lifted.
He had the Replica Crystal, which could endlessly replicate Immortal Singularity fragments.
Immortal Singularity was something he did not lack at all!
He selected the area around Mount Lamu and activated the Chrono Reversal Circle.
[Prompt: This action will consume a massive amount of Immortal Singularity.
Confirm?]
"Confirm."
[Ding!
Item activated!]
In a single instant, hundreds of thousands of Immortal Singularity vanished into thin air!
The Chrono Reversal Circle began to move.
The space before him rippled like the surface of a lake wrinkled by the wind.
The once-dead air began to stir in circles, spreading out layer by layer.
Spacetime began to flow backward.
Daniel stood outside the circle and watched everything before him reverse with his own eyes!

The ground that he had shattered with one stomp began to close and restore itself at a speed visible to the naked eye, as if someone were picking up the pieces of a broken plate and putting them back together one by one.
The sword also followed the reversal of time and flew back into the coffin on its own.
The scattered stones around the coffin returned to their original positions, reassembling into the tomb chamber.
Then the chamber sank back underground, becoming once again that unknown grave no one had ever discovered.
The spacetime around him kept changing, and soon, everything returned to the way it had looked when Daniel first arrived.
Watching time reverse was like watching a play being performed backward.
[Prompt: You have consumed 1,000,000 Immortal Singularity.]
Daniel listened to the prompts ringing repeatedly beside his ear, but he was not panicked at all.
Before coming to Divine Wind Realm, he had already replicated a vast amount of Immortal Singularity.
He was not afraid of running out.
What he cared about more right now was the scene in front of him.
Not because the scene itself was so shocking, but because this item was simply too heaven-defying.
Something casually made by an Oracle-grade existence already contained such profound spacetime laws.
If he were to face an existence of that level in person, just how terrifying would that be?
With a wave of their hand, they could turn him into a swaddled infant, or directly reduce him to a pile of withered bones.
Who could withstand that?
And there was more.
Back when he had forcibly initiated the World War, he had encountered a supreme powerhouse capable of roaming through the Time River.
That human ancestor could freely move between the past and the future, and could even attack enemies across all timelines at once!
Against someone like that, even Immortal Revival would be useless.
They could uproot his existence from any point in time and any point in space.
By then, even if he could regenerate infinitely, he would only fall into an endless cycle of "revival—death—revival—death."
How would that be any different from true death?
Thinking of this, Daniel’s obsession with unlocking the Chronoverse Prologue Codex deepened even further.
"As long as I unlock the Chronoverse Prologue Codex, I’ll be able to touch the threshold of the laws of spacetime."
"With a method like this time reversal, I won’t need to rely on any item.
I’ll be able to use it myself.
Whether it’s for killing, saving my life, or anything else, it’ll be a heaven-defying skill."
He took a deep breath.
He was only short three elemental cores.
A small problem!
At that moment, as time continued reversing, increasingly obvious changes began to appear within the spacetime inside the great circle.
Daniel stared fixedly ahead.
Within his field of vision, scene after scene began to emerge.
Countless fleeing beings crowded onto this mountain, crying to the heavens and wailing toward Mount Lamu.
"Progenitor Camille, we should never have refused to listen to you back then!"
"Progenitor Camille!
Progenitor Camille!
The Luminari are finished!
We are about to be destroyed by our own hands!"
"Progenitor Camille, please come back and save us!"
"We were wrong!
We were wrong!
The Luminari... are doomed!"
"Our civilization is going to perish...
We were wrong!"

chapters.title: Chapter 231 -231-A Colossal Joke and a Bitter Irony
paragraphs: The reversal of time was still continuing, but the scene before him had become deeply thought-provoking.
The fleeing beings from just now had vanished.
In their place appeared a group of dignified, lavishly dressed beings.
They appeared atop Mount Lamu, staring at Lamu Palace with faces full of disdain.
"What is this garbage?"
One of the beings spat viciously toward the magnificent palace.
"This mountain is useless now. Does this broken palace even deserve to remain?"
"Everyone! Why don’t we tear this wretched palace down together?"
"We can use it to celebrate the fact that we’ll never be manipulated by anyone again!"
"This is a great era—an era without the Swordlord!"
The group of beings wantonly destroyed Lamu Palace, then pushed down Mount Lamu itself before finally leaving in satisfaction.
When Daniel saw this, his brows knitted tighter and tighter.
He stood outside time itself, watching everything with the eyes of a bystander. Because of that, he saw more clearly than anyone else.
One moment ago, those beings had been crying to the heavens in despair, filled with regret and remorse.
The next moment, they had put on an entirely different face—arrogant, disdainful, and fearless.
The two scenes overlapped, like a blunt knife carving into the heart again and again.
It was an irony so painful it pierced straight to the marrow.
He shook his head and continued watching.
The scene within the magic circle shifted once again.
A group of beings carried wine jars and fine food as they flooded onto Mount Lamu.
They were reveling, getting drunk, and celebrating at the top of their lungs.
"Hahaha—there’s finally no more Swordlord!"
"Exactly. No one will ever ride above our heads and order us around again."
"That’s right. We won’t have to live in fear every day either, worrying that we’ll be blown into ashes along with this world."
"Not just us. Our sons, our grandsons, and all our descendants after them won’t have to be afraid either."
"We should never have created any Swordlord in the first place. Why should our fate be held in someone else’s hands?"
"The era of the Swordlord is over!"
"Come, let us toast this great new era—the era of freedom! The era of peace!"
Daniel silently watched everything unfold.
He did not know whether these beings knew that beneath their feet lay a nameless grave.

He did not know whether these beings knew that many years later, they would kneel here in utter misery, weeping bitterly and drowning in regret, begging Progenitor Camille to crawl out of his grave and save them.
He did not know whether these beings knew that the Godkin would uproot their civilization entirely and trample every last one of them into the mud as slaves...
And from beginning to end, a traveler from another world was watching this absurd farce with cold eyes.
How ironic.
Daniel shook his head.
He could not feel even the slightest sympathy or pity for these people.
All of this was the result of their own choice.
The Endless Starfield had always been a jungle where the weak were prey to the strong.
The Luminari had personally snapped off their own fangs and ground down their own claws.
In that case, their ending had already been waiting for them.
Beasts with sharper claws and fangs would tear them to pieces.
They had lost their gamble!
They had gambled that all beasts were like them, willing to share this world peacefully and warmly.
That was not stupidity.
It was ignorance.
Ignorance toward survival.
Ignorance toward life.
Ignorance toward the starry sky!
"One must have reverence in their heart, but also keep their fists clenched."
Daniel clenched his hand tightly.
The fate of the Luminari struck his heart like a heavy hammer.
He was glad that in his previous lives, he had walked the darkest and bloodiest paths.
That road had taught him only one thing.
Survival mattered more than anything else!
He might be the de facto "Swordlord of humanity," but he would never allow anyone to take this sword from his hand.
Whoever dared to reach for it would die.
No matter who they were.
Even if they were human too, it still would not be allowed.
A cold gleam flashed in Daniel’s eyes like the edge of a blade.
"Perhaps I am not the best leader."
"But I will become the strongest leader."
"If I want to steer the future of humanity, then all I need is to be strong enough!"
He continued observing the time reversal before him.
Time turned and shifted, and the celebrating crowd receded like a tide.
Between heaven and earth, only one old man remained!
Daniel’s pupils shrank slightly.
That was the Swordlord!
He recognized the old man.
He also recognized the sword.
At this moment, Daniel was still standing outside the circle.
If he wanted to truly come into contact with the Swordlord, he had to step into the magic circle and walk into that reversed fragment of time.
Daniel paused the spacetime within the magic circle, then calmly stepped inside.
Inside the Chrono Reversal Circle.
Camille was sitting at the end of his years, waiting for death to arrive.
Just then, a figure appeared out of thin air before him.
Daniel studied the old man who was about to fade away and said,
"I am Faustus. How should I address you?"
"Camille."
A hint of confusion flashed through Camille’s eyes.
He sized Daniel up.
Legendary-grade?
But the aura around this man was absurdly powerful.
He could not see through this young man’s purpose.
Daniel glanced at the sword and said calmly,
"I come from many years in the future."
Camille’s eyes suddenly lit up.
This person had actually come from the future!
For some reason, he did not doubt it.
He simply felt that a powerhouse with such bearing would not bother lying.
But very soon, that light in his eyes dimmed again.
He was too intelligent.
So intelligent that he saw through the truth at a glance!
Divine Wind Realm was probably already finished.
Otherwise, this man would not have crossed time to find him.
Or more accurately, the other party had probably come for this sword!
"The Luminari..."
Camille opened his mouth, but stopped himself.
Even though he already had the answer in his heart, he still could not help asking.
Daniel nodded, his tone incomparably calm.
"The Godkin invaded in force. The civilization of this world has already been erased. Every Luminari powerhouse above legendary-grade is dead."
"The rest were enslaved by the Godkin for countless years. By now, I’m afraid there may not even be anyone left who remembers the name Luminari."
The Luminari had fallen!
Even though Camille had already prepared himself for it, his heart still felt as though someone had carved out a piece of it with a knife.
It was like knowing that a loved one would eventually pass away one day.
But when that day truly came, the pain still made it impossible to breathe.
However, Camille was no ordinary person.
He pressed the grief deep into his heart. Following this line of thought, he suddenly raised his eyes and looked at Daniel.
"So, you wish to oppose the Godkin of this world, and therefore you want this sword?"
Daniel could not help looking at Camille with greater respect.
The old man before him had a truly penetrating mind. He understood everything with the slightest hint. As expected of the leader of an entire race.
Daniel did not bother hiding anything either.
Before someone this intelligent, concealment would only seem laughable.
"That’s right."
Daniel’s gaze fell on the sword.
"I used the Chrono Reversal Circle to come here precisely so I could obtain it."
Camille pondered for a moment.
"Why must I give it to you?"
A faint smile appeared at the corner of Daniel’s mouth as he asked in return,
"And why would you refuse?"
There was no reason.
The Luminari were already gone.
Moreover, the other party wanted this sword in order to fight the Godkin.
In that case, what reason did Camille have to refuse?
He no longer had any roots.
Camille gave a bitter smile.
"Forget it. If you want it, then take it."
Daniel’s heart stirred slightly.
He could not help asking,
"Do you... have any unfulfilled wishes?"
He did not want to owe this karma for nothing.
If Camille had any lingering wish, he would help if he could.
Taking something for free might feel wonderful, but it would leave his heart uneasy.
"Sigh..."
Camille looked at Daniel and let out a long sigh.
His voice was filled with unwillingness...

chapters.title: Chapter 232 -232-The Rebirth of the Swordlord, Judgment of Frost and Flame
paragraphs: "Originally, I could have become a sage, but the Godkin trapped me here and kept me firmly restrained."
"I held on alone for thousands of years. After my death, the Godkin uprooted my entire race... My whole life was ruined by the Godkin."
He paused, and his voice sank lower.

"Sometimes, I wonder why I was given this talent at all. Wouldn’t it have been better to be an ordinary person? Birth, aging, sickness, and death would only last a few hundred years. How could there be so much suffering?"
He looked at Daniel, a trace of hope in his eyes.

"If you fight the Godkin, they will not let you off easily. I only hope that you... kill a few more Godkin. That will be enough. I can no longer change anything. I might as well calmly walk toward death."
Death?
But you are clearly filled with unwillingness.
If there were still a chance, how could you give up?
Daniel did not believe it.
"Are you truly willing to die?"
"I mean, what if you could continue fighting?"
Daniel suddenly asked.
"Hmm!?"
Camille abruptly raised his head, his eyes filled with shock.
Boom—!
A powerful aura at the peak of demi-sage rank suddenly erupted from his body.
Faustus narrowed his eyes slightly.
So strong!
This Swordlord had probably already reached the threshold of breaking through to Divine-grade.
Camille pointed his sword toward the sky, his eyes filled with endless battle intent.

"If I could continue living, I would slaughter my way into the Godkin and make their blood flow like rivers! I would make them taste what it feels like to have their people massacred and to live in endless suffering!"
Faustus took a deep breath.
In his heart, he made his decision.
"I can let you be reborn."
Camille’s eyes suddenly widened.
Reborn!
Faustus flipped his hand and took out that crystal, his tone calm.
"I have a treasure called the Regeneration Crystal. It can allow someone on the verge of death to be reborn in peak condition while retaining all their memories and consciousness."
Camille suppressed the surging emotions in his heart and asked solemnly,
"So, what price do I need to pay?"
He knew the value of such a treasure. He absolutely did not believe that the other party would let him be reborn unconditionally.
A ruthless man who had endured purgatory, supported everything alone for thousands of years, and had always been prepared to drag billions of beings in this world down together with the Godkin.
An old man who would rather shoulder ten thousand years of loneliness.
Someone like him did not believe that pies would simply fall from the sky.
A faint smile tugged at the corner of Faustus’s mouth.
"The condition is that I will establish a Godslayer Alliance. After you are reborn, you must join it."
Camille did not hesitate in the slightest.
"No problem!"
Faustus nodded.
"Then you can die."
Rebirth meant dying and being born again.
Only by dying could he live!
Camille laughed brightly, then aimed the tip of his sword at his own heart.
Pfft—!
The sword pierced through his heart.
This sword had never existed for the sake of drawing blood.
It had been born to protect.
To protect the entire plane.
To protect an entire race.
But today, it had drawn blood.
And it was Camille’s own blood.
That blood was incomparably hot.
Blood that had lain dormant for nearly ten thousand years was still burning hot.
Within that blood was the flame of hatred.
Within it was all the grief and rage of a powerhouse who had endured ten thousand years of loneliness.
At the same time, Faustus raised the Regeneration Crystal in his hand.
[Ding! Confirm use of [Regeneration Crystal] to regenerate [Camille]? This item is extremely precious. Once used, it cannot be reversed.]
"Confirm."
[Prompt: Regeneration conditions fulfilled. Regeneration successful! You have successfully regenerated the peak demi-sage rank powerhouse [Camille]!]
The instant the system prompt sounded, a change appeared before Faustus.
A mass of blazing light completely enveloped Camille, and the aura of life slowly awakened!
A moment later, a perfectly intact Camille stood before him.
The strongest being in Luminari history, the demi-sage rank powerhouse who had endured thousands of years of solitude, had been reborn.
Faustus and Camille looked at each other and smiled.
The silent oath between them no longer needed words.
Faustus waved his hand.
Buzz—!
The Chrono Reversal Circle abruptly vanished.
Camille still existed.
That sword still existed as well.
Moreover, the Camille standing there now was in perfect condition!
He sensed the wounds in his body that had once tormented him beyond endurance.
At this moment, all of them had completely disappeared.
A scorching gratitude surged in Camille’s heart.
It was the grace of being dragged back from the abyss of death.
It was not charity.
It was not pity.
It was rebirth.
This favor was higher than the heavens and deeper than the sea.
This debt of gratitude pressed heavily against his heart!
Faustus looked at the sword in Camille’s hand and spoke calmly.
"Can I borrow that sword?"
His quest was to obtain this sword.
Camille laughed heartily. Without the slightest hesitation, he offered the sword with both hands.
The instant the hilt fell into Faustus’s palm, a system prompt exploded beside his ear.
[Ding! Camille is willing to acknowledge you as his master. Please confirm.]
Faustus was slightly stunned and raised his eyes to look at Camille.
There was no hesitation in the old man’s eyes.
Only certainty.
"Confirm."
Camille solemnly knelt on one knee.
"Camille greets Master."
"Rise."
Faustus reached out and helped him up.
"From this day forward, you and I will fight side by side. We are comrades!"
Camille straightened, light burning in his eyes.
"Against whom shall we fight?"
Faustus gazed into the void and said indifferently,
"Against the gods! And against those fools who want to sit above our heads and act like our masters."
"As you command!"
The instant the sword hilt entered his hand—
[Ding! You have completed the class change quest [Swordlord]!]
[Ding! You have obtained [epic-grade forbidden spell · Judgment of Frost and Flame] ×1!]
[Ding! You have obtained [forbidden-grade archer Class Awakening Scroll(Level 300)] ×1!]
The class change quest was complete.
That sword was no longer something he absolutely had to hold.
Faustus returned the sword to Camille.
Now that Camille was one of his people, it made no difference whose hands the sword was in.
Only then did he check his gains from this quest.
[epic-grade forbidden spell · Judgment of Frost and Flame]
Restriction: forbidden-grade archer
Effect: A compound epic-grade forbidden spell formed from the dual elements of ice and fire. Its power is extremely terrifying!
Special: Damage scales with the strength of the caster.
Consumption: 10% MP
Duration: None

Description: Ice and fire are among the most primordial elements, and the most primordial Strength is often also the most ultimate Strength. The pinnacle of elemental magic is often to shatter complexity until only the simplest true essence remains. This forbidden spell is the best answer to that principle.

[Ding! You have learned the epic-grade forbidden spell [Judgment of Frost and Flame]!]
[Prompt: Your skill panel has been updated. Please check the details yourself.]
With that, he had gained yet another offensive epic-grade forbidden spell.
Aside from Arrow of Judgment, he now also had Judgment of Frost and Flame.
He took out the forbidden-grade archer Class Awakening Scroll and chose to use it.
[Ding! The seal on your EXP bar has been removed. You may continue leveling up.]
Daniel felt that this was probably the leveling speed of ordinary class players.
After all, hidden class change quests were as difficult as ascending to the heavens.
By contrast, the more ordinary the class, the simpler its class quests were, and the faster one could level.
That was why ordinary players became higher and higher in level as time went on, while many hidden class players leveled more and more slowly instead.
It was not that they were weak.
It was that their path was too difficult to walk.
Faustus did not hesitate and directly leveled up to the limit.
[Ding! Your level has increased! Current level: 281. You have obtained 20 attribute points.]
[Ding! Your level has increased! Current level: 290. You have obtained 20 attribute points.]
[Ding! Your level has increased! Current level: 300. You have obtained 20 attribute points.]

[Prompt: You have not yet completed the next stage of your class change quest. Your level cap has been sealed. Please complete your class change quest as soon as possible to unlock leveling authority.]
Level 300!
Faustus smiled.
Only the final 100 levels remained before he advanced to supreme-grade!

sentences.text: "Originally, I could have become a sage, but the Godkin trapped me here and kept me firmly restrained."
"I held on alone for thousands of years.
After my death, the Godkin uprooted my entire race...
My whole life was ruined by the Godkin."
He paused, and his voice sank lower.
"Sometimes, I wonder why I was given this talent at all.
Wouldn’t it have been better to be an ordinary person?
Birth, aging, sickness, and death would only last a few hundred years.
How could there be so much suffering?"
He looked at Daniel, a trace of hope in his eyes.
"If you fight the Godkin, they will not let you off easily.
I only hope that you... kill a few more Godkin.
That will be enough.
I can no longer change anything.
I might as well calmly walk toward death."
Death?
But you are clearly filled with unwillingness.
If there were still a chance, how could you give up?
Daniel did not believe it.
"Are you truly willing to die?"
"I mean, what if you could continue fighting?"
Daniel suddenly asked.
"Hmm!?"
Camille abruptly raised his head, his eyes filled with shock.
Boom—!
A powerful aura at the peak of demi-sage rank suddenly erupted from his body.
Faustus narrowed his eyes slightly.
So strong!
This Swordlord had probably already reached the threshold of breaking through to Divine-grade.
Camille pointed his sword toward the sky, his eyes filled with endless battle intent.
"If I could continue living, I would slaughter my way into the Godkin and make their blood flow like rivers!
I would make them taste what it feels like to have their people massacred and to live in endless suffering!"
Faustus took a deep breath.
In his heart, he made his decision.
"I can let you be reborn."
Camille’s eyes suddenly widened.
Reborn!
Faustus flipped his hand and took out that crystal, his tone calm.
"I have a treasure called the Regeneration Crystal.
It can allow someone on the verge of death to be reborn in peak condition while retaining all their memories and consciousness."
Camille suppressed the surging emotions in his heart and asked solemnly,
"So, what price do I need to pay?"
He knew the value of such a treasure.
He absolutely did not believe that the other party would let him be reborn unconditionally.
A ruthless man who had endured purgatory, supported everything alone for thousands of years, and had always been prepared to drag billions of beings in this world down together with the Godkin.
An old man who would rather shoulder ten thousand years of loneliness.
Someone like him did not believe that pies would simply fall from the sky.
A faint smile tugged at the corner of Faustus’s mouth.
"The condition is that I will establish a Godslayer Alliance.
After you are reborn, you must join it."
Camille did not hesitate in the slightest.
"No problem!"
Faustus nodded.
"Then you can die."
Rebirth meant dying and being born again.
Only by dying could he live!
Camille laughed brightly, then aimed the tip of his sword at his own heart.
Pfft—!
The sword pierced through his heart.
This sword had never existed for the sake of drawing blood.
It had been born to protect.
To protect the entire plane.
To protect an entire race.
But today, it had drawn blood.
And it was Camille’s own blood.

Blood that had lain dormant for nearly ten thousand years was still burning hot.
Within that blood was the flame of hatred.

Buzz—!

chapters.title: Chapter 233 -233-Godkin Wrath, the Divine Might Legion
paragraphs: He was too lazy to travel the long way, so he took out the Starfield Portal on the spot.
This thing had also been taken from the Godkin treasury. Previously, it had remained sealed the entire time.
He had Conrad undo the seal, and now it could finally be used.
[Starfield Portal(Divine-grade)]
Grade: Divine-grade
Effect: After use, it can establish a two-way portal that crosses planes.
Description: This item was specially created by Oracle-grade existences for plane wars.
Faustus chose to use it without the slightest hesitation.
[Ding! You have used [Starfield Portal]!]
[Prompt: Please set the city to bind!]
[Ding! Setting successful!]
He bound the other end of the portal to Aerial Realm.
In this way, there was now a direct passage between Aerial Realm and Divine Wind Realm.
In the future, if players wanted to come to Divine Wind Realm, they would have to transfer through Aerial Realm first.
After setting up the portal, Faustus brought Camille back to Starfall Isle.
At this moment, Conrad and Mara were so busy that their feet barely touched the ground.
After all, taking over the mess of an entire world was never going to be easy.
Godkin, Hall of Divine Grace.
A group of Godkin powerhouses had gathered inside the grand hall, every face covered in frost.
No matter who it was, if their own territory had been forcefully bitten off by someone else, their expression would not look good.
The news sent up from the lower realm was like a knife, stabbing viciously into the Godkin’s lungs.
A group of starfield wanderers had appeared in Divine Wind Realm. The stationed garrison had gone to confront them, only to be completely wiped out. Not even a single messenger had survived.
This matter could not be hidden.
Nor could it be suppressed.
The entire God realm was shaken.
The Hall of Divine Grace was the seat of authority in the God realm that specifically governed conquest, war, and slaughter.
At this moment, the hall master, Hiram, wore a dark expression as he personally questioned them about the details.
"Conrad? It was him?"
Hiram’s voice squeezed out from between his teeth, fury surging in his throat like magma.
Back then, he had been the one who personally released that mad dog Conrad, ordering him to gnaw on the bone that was Aetheria and fight Faustus to the death.
But now?
That dog had not gone to bite Faustus.
Instead, it had turned around and sunk its teeth into the leg of the God realm itself.
How dare he?
How dare he challenge the God realm and seize the God realm’s territory?
"The inspectors also discovered something else."
His subordinate carefully added,
"Among those starfield wanderers, there were traces of the human race—it was Faustus!"
Him again.
The muscles on Hiram’s face twitched violently, as if someone had slapped him across the face.
The name Faustus was like a thorn lodged in the Godkin’s throat.
They could not swallow it.
Nor could they pull it out.
Suddenly, his eyes lit up.
Faustus was not in Aetheria?
Then didn’t that mean Aetheria had become an empty city?
A ferocious curve tugged at the corner of his mouth.
"Send the Divine Blood Legion to Aetheria. Kill every last human."
He felt that was still not enough to vent his hatred, so he added another order.
"Have the Divine Might Legion go to Divine Wind Realm and crush Faustus for me!"
Inside the grand hall, the eyes of the Godkin powerhouses all lit up at once.
If Faustus was not in Aetheria, then what was there to fear?
The City Above the Clouds was hanging right there in that sky. With a single command, countless Godkin warriors could instantly trample that land to pieces.

Although the Divine Blood Legion did not number in the hundreds of millions, it still had several million legendary-grade warriors. Once they burned immortal matter, every one of them could erupt with supreme-grade battle power, and they even held Holy Relics in their hands.
Crushing a tiny Aetheria would be effortless, wouldn’t it?
As for the Divine Might Legion, it was not a single legion.
It was a collection of thirteen legions!
They were the sharpest fangs of the Godkin, a super war machine composed entirely of legendary-grade warriors from non-human races. Their total military strength exceeded ten million.

Within the legion, demi-sages were as numerous as ox hairs. No matter how strong Faustus was, as long as they were willing to pay a bloody price, it was not impossible to nail him to the ruins of Divine Wind Realm.
Everyone accepted their orders one after another and hurriedly dispersed.
Godkin, Zenith Temple.
Boom—!
Majestic energy condensed into a fist. Wherever it passed, space shattered like glass. Carrying an unstoppable momentum, it blasted toward a Godkin powerhouse standing opposite it.
That Godkin powerhouse looked calm and composed.
He neither dodged nor evaded.
Boom—!
The fist smashed solidly into his body.
Yet he did not move an inch.
Not even the hem of his clothes lifted.
Huff, huff—
"Aldor, that shell of yours is seriously harder than a turtle’s."
Nubat panted heavily and shook his head with a bitter smile.
"What level have you reached now?"
Aldor smiled faintly.
"Demi-sage. But compared to Raylor, I am still far behind."
Nubat grinned.
"I’m also a demi-sage, but standing in front of you, I feel like a legendary-grade facing a supreme-grade. This gap is way too ridiculous."
"The demi-sage realm is far too deep."
Aldor nodded.
"It is. If it were Raylor, he could kill you instantly."
He paused, then explained slowly,

"The demi-sage tier is actually divided in great detail. Touching the threshold of Divine-grade power counts as low-grade. Mastering Thoughtstep counts as mid-grade. Only by opening up the rudimentary form of a sage rank can one be considered high-grade!"
"Only when one’s sage rank has been opened up to a nearly complete state can one qualify as Transcendent Peak!"
He gave a bitter smile.
"Raylor has already crossed that transcendent line. His sage rank is lingering right at the boundary between success and failure."
"He is even a notch stronger than Transcendent Peak. As expected of someone who can represent the Godkin in competing for the Starlight Rankings."
Nubat sighed.
"With him around, I’m afraid you don’t have much of a chance."
Aldor shook his head.
"He is a madman. Other than becoming stronger, there is nothing else in his mind. I won’t compare myself to him."
Nubat shrugged.
"You still have a chance to fight for a seat in the Starlight Rankings. I’m completely out of the running. I plan to descend to the lower realm and deal with that Faustus."
"Faustus?"
Aldor frowned.
He remembered that name.
It was carved into his bones!
His own younger brother, Kahn, had died at Faustus’s hands.
Nubat grinned and patted him on the shoulder.
"Don’t worry. I’ll settle this debt for your brother."
Kahn had been a genius of the Godkin, Aldor’s younger brother. At Heavenscar, Faustus had pierced his skull with a single arrow.
Aldor remained silent for a moment. He looked at Nubat, as if wanting to say something, but hesitated.
"As for Faustus’s strength, I have gone through all the intelligence we have. I have a rough idea in my heart. You... are probably not his match."
Nubat smiled dismissively.
"Didn’t he just wipe out one garrison legion in Divine Wind Realm?"
He blinked.
"Don’t forget, I am a divine guard of the Hall of Divine Grace. This full set of Holy Relics on me isn’t just for show."
"My own strength may not be equal to his, but with these treasures protecting me, it won’t be that easy for him to kill me."
Aldor opened his mouth, wanting to say something, but swallowed the words back down.
He had originally wanted to tell Nubat that external objects were external objects in the end.
Borrowed Strength was like duckweed, drifting without roots.
Raylor was the best example.
That fellow held the Godkin’s top-tier resources in his hands, yet he had never cared to use them.
What he relied on was death-defying bitter cultivation.
He had hidden himself in desperate situations, forcing himself to the brink of death day after day, and that was how he had reached his current level.
But Aldor understood Nubat too well.
Nubat would not listen to such words!
Nubat turned to leave, but suddenly stopped again.
"I think you should still fight for the Starlight Rankings. In Godkin history, there have been several cases where two people competed for the rankings at the same time."
Battle intent ignited in Aldor’s eyes, and he smiled.
"That goes without saying. I won’t easily yield to anyone. Raylor may be very strong, but I’m not exactly weak either."
Nubat smiled as well.
"When I return with Faustus’s head, I’ll go with you."
Aldor took a deep breath and silently muttered in his heart.
You must not underestimate that human...
Otherwise, you may not come back.
He did not say those words aloud.
If he said them, Nubat would not believe him.
He would only become displeased!
Nubat was a genius of the Godkin, the youngest son of the Hall of Divine Grace’s master, and someone who had grown up with a golden spoon in his mouth.
The full set of Holy Relics he wore had been personally forged for him by his divine father. Ordinary Divine-grade powerhouses could not even break through that shell.
He had an almost blind trust in his own Strength.
So Aldor could only keep those words buried in his stomach.

Nubat smiled as well.
"When I return with Faustus’s head, I’ll go with you."
Aldor took a deep breath and silently muttered in his heart.
You must not underestimate that human...
Otherwise, you may not come back.
He did not say those words aloud.
If he said them, Nubat would not believe him.
He would only become displeased!
Nubat was a genius of the Godkin, the youngest son of the Hall of Divine Grace’s master, and someone who had grown up with a golden spoon in his mouth.
The full set of Holy Relics he wore had been personally forged for him by his divine father.
Ordinary Divine-grade powerhouses could not even break through that shell.
He had an almost blind trust in his own Strength.
So Aldor could only keep those words buried in his stomach.

chapters.title: Chapter 234 -234-Soloing the Divine Blood Legion
paragraphs: Starlight Rankings.
This was a grand event of the Starfield Tier.
However, there was one important point: only powerhouses below Divine-grade were qualified to appear on this ranking.
The ranking would be cleared and reset every once in a while. Every reset was a carnival for demi-sages from all kinds of powerful factions.
Any powerhouse who made it onto the ranking would be watched by forces across the entire star domain. They would be sought after, courted, and offered enormous benefits.
Starfield Tier!
Countless demi-sages sharpened their heads and fought with everything they had, all just to carve their names onto it.
Divine Wind Realm, Starfall Isle.
[Ding! You have received a new forbidden-grade archer class change quest. Please check it.]
Faustus casually opened the quest panel.
[Divine Might](forbidden-grade archer class change quest)
Restriction: forbidden-grade archer
Quest Difficulty: Exalted-grade
Quest Objectives:
Repel the Godkin’s attack.
Successfully survive.
Quest Introduction: You turned Conrad against the Godkin and occupied Divine Wind Realm. This action is equivalent to tearing the Godkin’s face off and stomping on it again and again.
The Godkin army will arrive very soon. You must stand firm within the Godkin’s wrath!
Quest Duration: Long-term
Quest Reward: [Scroll of Version Upgrade] ×1, [forbidden-grade archer Class Awakening Scroll] ×1.
Scroll of Version Upgrade?
Faustus was slightly startled.
Good grief, here it came again!
There was not much to say about the quest itself.
As long as Divine-grade powerhouses did not descend, he could walk sideways across this entire world.
No matter how many Godkin came, he would take them all.
No matter how many came, that was how many would die!
What truly stirred his heart was the scroll itself.
A new version...
What would it bring this time?
Could it be... the fusion of the game and reality?
After all, quite a few signs of fusion had already appeared in the real world!
Especially for top-tier players like him. The strength of their bodies in reality was already almost no different from in the game!
He was already at the level where he could stand still and let artillery shells bombard him without them doing anything to him.
Faustus took a deep breath.
No matter what it was, what was meant to come would come eventually!
However, there was still one more thing he needed to consider.
The Godkin were about to make a move, and judging from the situation, it would not take too long!
The information revealed by this quest was already more than enough.
At the very least, he had roughly grasped the Godkin’s movements.
Thinking of this, he immediately recalled Conrad and the others and began preparing for war.
Aetheria.
For no reason at all, Carodion felt a wave of panic in his heart.
It was not fear, but an indescribable throbbing, like the dead silence in the instant before dark clouds pressed down on the world.
He kept feeling that something was coming.
Whoosh—!
Faustus’s puppet avatar appeared in front of him.
"My king."
Carodion lowered his head and saluted.
He knew this was his master’s puppet.
It possessed the exact same Strength as the main body and could even share all gains with him.
At this moment, the puppet’s level had also soared along with the main body, already rushing all the way to Level 300!
Daniel nodded, then raised his eyes to look at the war fortress suspended in the sky. His tone was calm.
"Carodion, prepare the entire army for battle!"
Carodion’s heart tightened.
Sure enough.
What was meant to come had finally arrived!
He did not dare delay and immediately ordered the entire realm to enter a state of war readiness.
The defensive magic arrays in every city were activated in full. On the city walls, those cold war machines lit up one after another with a dark glow, like sleeping beasts opening their eyes.
Daniel had no intention of using the players’ Strength.
In Divine Wind Realm, he had personally witnessed how terrifying Holy Relics were.
With the players’ current foundation, they could not withstand that kind of thing.
In fact, he did not even plan to let anyone else make a move.
He alone was enough!
Just then, movement came from the fortress in the clouds.
Millions of Divine Blood Legion warriors split into two vast torrents and poured out from the city, stepping out of that fortress hanging beyond the painting.
The moment they entered the world of Aetheria, Daniel sensed them.
It was like a drop of ink falling into clear water.
There was no hiding it at all.
He had no way to deal with the cloud fortress hidden inside the spatial crevice, but as for these prey that had already walked into the painting—
He had plenty of methods.
Boom! Boom! Boom!
Several powerful auras erupted without the slightest concealment.
That was the pressure of demi-sages, on the same level as Conrad. There were a full four or five of them.
Daniel raised an eyebrow, and his figure instantly disappeared from where he stood.
When he reappeared, he was already standing above the heads of the two legions.
Boom! Boom!
The Divine Blood Legion reacted extremely quickly and entered combat state in an instant.
Immortal Singularity ignited like dry firewood. Divine Domains spread open like a curtain across the heavens. The might of Holy Relics bore down like mountains.
Those five demi-sages surrounded him from every side.
And yet, no matter how one looked at this scene, it felt strange.
It was clearly they who had surrounded Daniel, but the feeling it gave was more like Daniel alone had trapped all of them inside a cage!
Daniel’s sudden appearance had caught them off guard.
Hadn’t the master of the Hall of Divine Grace said this fellow was not in Aetheria?
The intelligence was wrong!
But at this point, they had no time to care about that.
The arrow was already nocked on the bowstring. Whether Daniel was here or not, since they had run into him, they would fight.
Boom, boom, boom!
The demi-sages burned Immortal Singularity with all their might.
They knew better than anyone just how powerful Daniel was.
This battle was bound to be filled with danger!
They had surrounded Daniel, but it looked far more like Daniel had nailed them to the execution rack.
At the same time, the divine artifacts on them transmitted the entire scene back to the God realm without missing a single detail.
"Kill—!"
Following the Godkin commander’s order, the Divine Blood Legion unleashed ten thousand arrows at once.
The five demi-sages attacked at the same time as well, sealing off all of Daniel’s paths of retreat from five directions.
No one cared about outnumbering him.
They only wished they had a hundred times or a thousand times more companions beside them.
Because Daniel was too strong!
They were fighting this war with the resolve to die.
If Daniel did not die, then they would.
The Godkin demi-sages were already staking their lives.
Rumble—!
The Divine Blood Legion’s frenzied bombardment, the Godkin demi-sages’ pincer attack from all directions, Divine Domains surging over like tides, Holy Relics smashing down like mountains—
Daniel’s figure was instantly submerged inside an endless torrent of energy.
However, Daniel strolled leisurely, neither hurried nor flustered.
Every attack missed him by the tiniest margin, but no matter what, none of them could touch even the corner of his clothes.
Even divine arts that covered an area and forced a guaranteed hit somehow veered off course when they reached him.
It was as though a blade had been placed against the side of his neck, yet that blade would forever remain one hair’s breadth away and could never truly cut down.
Daniel stood there without moving an inch.
Yet not a single killing move that filled the sky could touch him.
This incomparably bizarre sight made the Godkin demi-sages feel a chill rising from their bones.
"Faustus... has actually become this strong!"
"Impossible! This is absolutely impossible!"
"It’s over. We underestimated him."
"How did this human grow to such a level..."
They believed they had already taken Daniel seriously enough. They had even used everything they had.
But Daniel was even more monstrous than they had imagined.
And not just by a little.
The gap was so vast that they could not even hope to catch up.
The corner of Daniel’s mouth lifted slightly.
This was the power of the Fate Law of Causality!
As long as he altered the result, he could achieve this level of effect.
He was confident that even if a million demi-sage ranks stood before him, the result would not be any different!
Because what he held in his hand was law.
Law stood above the Strength of all elements.
"It’s my turn."
He spoke indifferently.
Before his voice had even faded, endless ice and fire elements suddenly surged out from the void, gathering into a vast, heaven-shaking ocean.
Upon seeing this scene, the demi-sages’ faces turned ashen, and some of them instantly fell into despair!

chapters.title: Chapter 235 -235-Three Are More Than Enough to Face Divine Might
paragraphs: "The aura of an epic-grade forbidden spell!"
"How is this possible? No!"
"Run! Run!"
"Escape! Why did the Godkin give us false information? Did they send us here just to die?!"
Faced with life and death, these demi-sages ultimately chose to live.
Most of them were not direct descendants of the Godkin. They were merely enslaved vassals under the Godkin’s rule. The Divine Blood Legion was the same.
The Godkin would never be willing to fill a pit with their own lives.
So when these people fled, they felt no psychological burden at all.
It was not that they had not tried hard enough.
The enemy was simply far too powerful!
The boundless ocean of ice and fire elements surged violently.
Crash, crash, crash—!
Towering waves instantly swallowed every enemy before them.
Countless damage numbers leaped wildly within the elemental sea.
-3 billion!
-3 billion!
-3 billion!
[Ding! You have killed a Godkin powerhouse and obtained equipment: Divine Blood Battle Armor, peak supreme-grade ×1!]
[Ding! You have killed a Godkin powerhouse and obtained skill: Shadowless, peak supreme-grade ×1!]
[Ding! You have killed a large number of enemies and obtained Primal Spirit ×10,000, Immortal Singularity Fragment ×10,000...]
Daniel had an auto-loot buff active on him. A tremendous amount of loot poured into his infinite backpack with a rushing clatter.
In the blink of an eye, not a single living enemy remained before him.
Millions of soldiers from the Divine Blood Legion, along with those few demi-sages, had all turned into dust of the world.
Just like at the very beginning.
Their attacks could not harm Daniel in the slightest.
And no matter how much strength they exhausted over their lifetimes, they could not dodge Daniel’s attacks.
True damage combined with overwhelming firepower—
Instant kill!
Daniel coldly looked toward the fortress hidden within the clouds. The corner of his mouth pulled into a mocking curve.
"Keep coming. No matter how many you send, I’ll take them all."
Divine Wind Realm.
Above the sky, clouds churned as if boiling.
Thirteen legendary-grade legions descended abruptly!
Tens of millions of legendary-grade warriors, tens of thousands of supreme-grade powerhouses, and hundreds of demi-sages...
This was the full force the God Realm had dispatched for this campaign.
They released their auras without the slightest restraint. Their murderous intent shot straight into the clouds, stirring the heavens and earth until the world itself changed color.
All living beings in the Divine Wind Realm trembled beneath this pressure, as though doomsday had arrived.
Starfall Isle.
Conrad’s expression changed sharply.
"It’s the Godkin. They’re here."
At this moment, a deep furrow formed between his brows.
He worriedly glanced at the clansmen behind him, who were still busy at work, then turned to Faustus.
"My lord, I will go with you for this battle. Please let my people remain here."
Faustus nodded, understanding Conrad’s concern.
Camille, on the other hand, had long since had nothing left to worry about. His hand trembled with excitement as it gripped the hilt of his sword.
"They came at the perfect time. My sword has been thirsty for far too long!"
Faustus said calmly, "Move out."
Whoosh—!
Three figures tore through the void and landed steadily before the Godkin army.
The Godkin formation entered their sight. The expressions of the three were completely different.
A heavy worry surfaced in Conrad’s eyes as he said in a low voice, "The Godkin have truly invested everything this time."
"Thirteen legions. Tens of millions of legendary-grade warriors... Each legion is comparable to a peak demi-sage. And there are hundreds of demi-sage rank powerhouses holding the line."
He paused for a moment.
"This level of strength is simply terrifying."
But Camille’s eyes burned with light.
A mad, blazing light.
He licked his cracked lips. His voice was hoarse, yet scorching hot.
"Thousands of years... I have finally waited until this day."
Faustus’ expression remained unchanged, as if he were watching a play that had nothing to do with him.
The instant the three of them appeared, a sharp shout rang out from the opposite side.
"Form ranks!"
Hundreds of demi-sages quickly formed a military formation.
Nubat and several demi-sages stood outside the formation, arms crossed over their chests, their expressions arrogant.
Nubat’s gaze scraped across the three of them like a blade before finally pinning itself on Faustus’ face.
He lifted his chin. His voice carried a condescending contempt.
"You are Faustus of the human race?"
Faustus glanced at him but did not answer.
A savage smile tugged at Nubat’s mouth. His eyes shot forward like two sharp swords.
"Faustus, do you dare fight me?"
"A duel?"
Faustus’ voice was as faint as a breeze.
"You are not worthy."
Nubat’s face instantly twisted.
He suddenly remembered what Aldor had said before their departure, and rage erupted inside him at once.
"You’re courting death, you insignificant ant!"
As soon as he finished speaking, he transformed into a streak of flowing light. The longsword at his waist left its sheath, wrapped in a world-destroying momentum as it cleaved straight down.
His voice echoed through the air.
"Faustus, die—!"
Daniel did not even lift his eyelids.
He simply clenched his fist.
And punched.
Boom—!
That punch was as fast as light and as heavy as a mountain.
Nubat’s sword was clearly only a hair’s breadth away from landing, yet it strangely deviated, slicing into empty air.
Meanwhile, Daniel’s fist struck solidly against his chest.
In the blink of an eye, Nubat’s body shattered into pieces and turned into a cloud of blood mist.
[Ding! You have killed the Godkin genius Nubat...]
Conrad’s mouth fell open.
He stared blankly at Daniel, his voice trembling.
"My lord... that punch of yours..."
Camille was also stunned for a moment. Then he grinned.
"That Nubat had about seventy percent of my strength. If I wanted to kill him, I’d have to go all out. But Master killed him like crushing an ant."
He shook his head.
"So the Godkin are nothing special after all."
The Godkin legions instantly erupted into chaos.
"Lord Nubat was instantly killed!"
"This... this is impossible!"
A Godkin demi-sage finally recovered from his shock. His face turned ashen as he roared at the top of his lungs.
"Fight to the death!"
The moment those words rang out, every legion warrior ignited their Immortal Singularity at the same time.
Golden flames connected into a single vast sea of fire, illuminating the entire void.
This battle was destined to be a fight to the death.
Daniel looked at that golden sea of fire, his expression calm as ever.
He calmly spat out one word.
"Kill."
"Kill—!"
Camille and Conrad answered at the same time.
Runes coiled around Conrad’s entire body. The runes transformed into ferocious beasts, blades, swords, and massive boulders, surging toward the enemy formation like an overwhelming tide.
But the enemy’s defense was like an iron wall. His offensive only splashed a few ripples across the surface.
Camille, however, charged into the army of tens of millions alone with one sword in hand.
Wherever his sword light passed, blood sprayed wildly, and screams rose one after another.
"With my sword, I shall split mountains and rivers!"
"With my sword, I shall shatter the clouds!"
Sword energy arced like a rainbow. Godkin warriors continued to fall within the enemy formation, like wheat swept down by a storm.
"Kill him! Kill that sword-wielding madman!"
"Hold the line! We’re falling into a passive position!"
"What kind of joke is this? Are these guys demons?"
Seeing that the situation was turning unfavorable, the Godkin demi-sage army activated its formation.
A half-bodied phantom emerged from the void, radiating a suffocating divine-grade pressure.
The surrounding space began collapsing in large swaths. The entire heaven and earth trembled.
Camille threw his head back and laughed wildly, his laughter filled with unrestrained arrogance.
"So this is all the Godkin amount to? Excellent! This feels amazing!"
He fearlessly looked toward that sage-rank phantom and shouted.
The longsword in his hand plowed open a deep spatial black hole. Wherever it passed, shattered fragments fell one after another.
The half-bodied phantom raised a massive palm and slammed it down, only to be pierced through by a single sword strike.
Immediately afterward, the sword light penetrated the entire sage-rank phantom.
Hundreds of demi-sages vomited blood at the same time.
The formation collapsed.
One sword broke a sage rank!
"Heavenly Light!"
Camille shouted.
The sword light flew back into his hand.
Whoosh—
He transformed into a streak of flowing light and charged into the group of demi-sages, slaughtering wildly.
