"This level of strength is simply terrifying."
But Camille’s eyes burned with light.
A mad, blazing light.
He licked his cracked lips.
His voice was hoarse, yet scorching hot.
"Thousands of years...
I have finally waited until this day."
Faustus’ expression remained unchanged, as if he were watching a play that had nothing to do with him.
The instant the three of them appeared, a sharp shout rang out from the opposite side.
"Form ranks!"
Hundreds of demi-sages quickly formed a military formation.
Nubat and several demi-sages stood outside the formation, arms crossed over their chests, their expressions arrogant.
Nubat’s gaze scraped across the three of them like a blade before finally pinning itself on Faustus’ face.
He lifted his chin.
His voice carried a condescending contempt.
"You are Faustus of the human race?"
Faustus glanced at him but did not answer.
A savage smile tugged at Nubat’s mouth.
His eyes shot forward like two sharp swords.
"Faustus, do you dare fight me?"
"A duel?"
Faustus’ voice was as faint as a breeze.
"You are not worthy."
Nubat’s face instantly twisted.
He suddenly remembered what Aldor had said before their departure, and rage erupted inside him at once.
"You’re courting death, you insignificant ant!"
As soon as he finished speaking, he transformed into a streak of flowing light.
The longsword at his waist left its sheath, wrapped in a world-destroying momentum as it cleaved straight down.
His voice echoed through the air.
"Faustus, die—!"
Daniel did not even lift his eyelids.
He simply clenched his fist.
And punched.
Boom—!
That punch was as fast as light and as heavy as a mountain.
Nubat’s sword was clearly only a hair’s breadth away from landing, yet it strangely deviated, slicing into empty air.
Meanwhile, Daniel’s fist struck solidly against his chest.
In the blink of an eye, Nubat’s body shattered into pieces and turned into a cloud of blood mist.
[Ding!
You have killed the Godkin genius Nubat...]
Conrad’s mouth fell open.
He stared blankly at Daniel, his voice trembling.
"My lord... that punch of yours..."
Camille was also stunned for a moment.
Then he grinned.
"That Nubat had about seventy percent of my strength.
If I wanted to kill him, I’d have to go all out.
But Master killed him like crushing an ant."
He shook his head.
"So the Godkin are nothing special after all."
The Godkin legions instantly erupted into chaos.
"Lord Nubat was instantly killed!"
"This... this is impossible!"
A Godkin demi-sage finally recovered from his shock.
His face turned ashen as he roared at the top of his lungs.
"Fight to the death!"
The moment those words rang out, every legion warrior ignited their Immortal Singularity at the same time.
Golden flames connected into a single vast sea of fire, illuminating the entire void.
This battle was destined to be a fight to the death.
Daniel looked at that golden sea of fire, his expression calm as ever.
He calmly spat out one word.
"Kill."
"Kill—!"
Camille and Conrad answered at the same time.
Runes coiled around Conrad’s entire body.
The runes transformed into ferocious beasts, blades, swords, and massive boulders, surging toward the enemy formation like an overwhelming tide.
But the enemy’s defense was like an iron wall.
His offensive only splashed a few ripples across the surface.
Camille, however, charged into the army of tens of millions alone with one sword in hand.
Wherever his sword light passed, blood sprayed wildly, and screams rose one after another.
"With my sword, I shall split mountains and rivers!"
"With my sword, I shall shatter the clouds!"
Sword energy arced like a rainbow.
Godkin warriors continued to fall within the enemy formation, like wheat swept down by a storm.
"Kill him!
Kill that sword-wielding madman!"
"Hold the line!
We’re falling into a passive position!"
"What kind of joke is this?
Are these guys demons?"
Seeing that the situation was turning unfavorable, the Godkin demi-sage army activated its formation.
A half-bodied phantom emerged from the void, radiating a suffocating divine-grade pressure.
The surrounding space began collapsing in large swaths.
The entire heaven and earth trembled.
Camille threw his head back and laughed wildly, his laughter filled with unrestrained arrogance.
"So this is all the Godkin amount to?
Excellent!
This feels amazing!"
He fearlessly looked toward that sage-rank phantom and shouted.
The longsword in his hand plowed open a deep spatial black hole.
Wherever it passed, shattered fragments fell one after another.
The half-bodied phantom raised a massive palm and slammed it down, only to be pierced through by a single sword strike.
Immediately afterward, the sword light penetrated the entire sage-rank phantom.
Hundreds of demi-sages vomited blood at the same time.
The formation collapsed.
One sword broke a sage rank!
"Heavenly Light!"
Camille shouted.
The sword light flew back into his hand.
Whoosh—
He transformed into a streak of flowing light and charged into the group of demi-sages, slaughtering wildly.

chapters.title: Chapter 236 -236-Fusion with Reality, Lord of Earth
paragraphs: Conrad looked at the figure rampaging through the enemy formation, and even the tip of his heart trembled.
What a terrifying existence!
He had originally thought Faustus was already heaven-defying enough—
Yet this Camille was also astonishing beyond belief.
As expected of someone infinitely close to becoming a sage.
Conrad shook his head. He had to hurry and break through to divine-grade. He absolutely could not become dead weight.
"The ship led by Faustus is one my Starfolk must never miss."
At this moment, above Daniel’s head, ice and fire elements condensed into a colossal palm that reached the heavens, almost covering the entire plane.
Rumble—!
The giant palm fell like a meteor.
Boom, boom, boom—!
That heaven-spanning palm crashed down, like a mountain smashing into an anthill.
Wherever the palm wind swept past, the Godkin warriors melted away like frost flowers beneath the blazing sun, vanishing without a sound.
Tens of millions of living beings did not even have time to let out a single scream before they were crushed into nothingness.
-3 billion!
-3 billion!
-3 billion!
System notifications surged in like a tsunami. Every single one was like the wail of countless Godkin warriors.
[Ding! Obtained Primal Spirit ×10,000, Immortal Singularity Fragment ×10,000...]
[Ding! Obtained Primal Spirit ×10,000, Immortal Singularity Fragment ×10,000...]
The notification sounds crackled endlessly, with no sign of stopping.
In just a single breath, there was not a single living creature left in this sky.
Faustus’ Law of Causality was like an invisible shield, firmly protecting Conrad and Camille.
The two powerhouses standing behind him did not even have the hems of their clothes lifted by the wind.
Instant kill!
This was not slaughter.
This was not battle.
This was one-sided crushing.
"Hahahaha—!"
Camille was covered in blood. Golden, purple, and black blood had smeared all over his body.
He threw his head back and laughed. A flash of light passed over him, and all that filth fell away cleanly, as if scattered by the wind.
He flew back to Daniel’s side, his voice still trembling with killing intent that had yet to fade.
"Refreshing! That was too satisfying!"
Faustus glanced at him, the corners of his mouth lifting slightly.
In his heart, his satisfaction toward this powerhouse he had taken in halfway rose by another degree.
At the same time—
[Ding! You have completed the class change quest — Divine Might!]
[Ding! You have obtained Scroll of Version Upgrade ×1 and forbidden-grade archer Class Awakening Scroll, Level 320 ×1!]
Faustus took out that Class Awakening Scroll and used it.
[Ding! The seal on your experience bar has been removed. You may continue leveling.]
He did not hesitate and leveled up directly.
[Ding! Your level has increased! Current level: 301. Obtained 20 attribute points.]
[Ding! Your level has increased! Current level: 310. Obtained 20 attribute points.]
[Ding! Your level has increased! Current level: 320. Obtained 20 attribute points.]

[Prompt: You have not yet completed the next stage of your class change. Your level cap has been sealed again. Excess experience has been temporarily stored in your Exp Pool. Please complete your class change quest as soon as possible to remove the cap.]
Level 320!
Faustus silently calculated in his heart.
After completing four more class change quests, he would be able to step across the threshold of supreme-grade.
He looked toward the other scroll in his backpack.
[Scroll of Version Upgrade, Special]
Type: Unique Special Item.
Effect: After use, opens the game’s new version — The Starsea.

Description: Once The Starsea Chapter begins, the real world and the game world will rapidly merge into one. All player game data will be retained in reality, and all game systems will continue operating.
Note: Method of fusion — the real Earth will become an independent small world and publicly reveal its coordinates to all races among the stars.

In addition, players who die accidentally in Aetheria will no longer be able to resurrect, except those who possess resurrection skills, resurrection buffs, resurrection items, or resurrection equipment.
Whoever controls Earth’s World Origin will possess the highest authority over Earth’s interface!
Faustus held the scroll and lowered his head, staring at it for a long time.
In his eyes, there were memories.
There was sorrow.
And there was a hatred carved deep into his bones!
As expected, the new version was the fusion of virtuality and reality.
In his previous lives, the moment Earth’s coordinates were revealed, countless non-human races had rushed over like sharks smelling blood.
Humanity had been forced into a desperate situation, almost to the point of extinction.
But this time was different.
He was far, far stronger than in his previous lives.
That kind of tragedy—
He would never allow it to happen again.
Earth was home.
Those who dared trespass—
Would die!
He clenched the scroll tightly in his hand, so hard that his knuckles turned white.
After a while, he placed it back into his backpack.
Now was not the time!
He himself was ready, but the other players might not be.
Wait a little longer.
Wait until everything had been properly arranged.
After all, this concerned the survival of countless Earth players.
Once death came, they would no longer have the ability to resurrect freely!
The impact of the new version was far too great.
There could be no rush.
The gains from this battle were terrifyingly huge.
Divine Blood, Divine Soul, and Divinity Fragments had piled up into small mountains.
These were fuel for reincarnating through the Sacred Spring, capable of helping large numbers of players break through to legendary-grade.
Right now, it was precisely the time when players were undergoing large-scale reincarnation and advancement.

Ordinary players already had strong potential for long-term growth. Their class change quests were countless times easier than those of hidden classes. Combined with the favorable conditions Daniel had created for them, their leveling speed was soaring like mad.
These resources had arrived just in time.
After players broke through to legendary-grade, if there were not enough legendary-grade monsters, it would become very difficult for them to continue advancing.
This was also the reason Daniel was so eager to seize territory.
With the resources of the Divine Wind Realm, the players’ hunger for legendary-grade resources would be eased considerably.
The biggest gain was still Primal Spirit.

Unfortunately, the Godkin cherished their lives. Most of the warriors they had sent were from vassal races, and many of them were not innate races, so the amount of Primal Spirit gained was not particularly large.
But that was fine.
The deduction cooldown for Essence of Elemental Laws was thirty days, and only a short time had passed so far.
He could slowly accumulate more.
As for attacking the God Realm?
The conditions were not yet mature.
What remained was a pile of peak supreme-grade equipment and skill books.
At the current world level, the highest items that could be obtained were still below divine-grade.
Only after the new version opened would the upper limit be broken.
"These pieces of equipment and skill books are all useful."
Daniel calculated silently in his heart.
Things that he himself did not care for were absolute treasures in the eyes of other players.
They could be sold to the players perfectly.
Aside from that, the greatest harvest was gaining a firm foothold in the Divine Wind Realm.
After this battle, the Godkin should have learned their lesson. In the short term, they would not come seeking death again.
Thinking of this, Daniel instructed Conrad, "You can begin development. Occupy the entire world and organize its resources as quickly as possible."
"Understood, my lord."
Conrad looked at Daniel, then at Camille, and his confidence was clearly lacking.
Among the three powerhouses, his strength was the weakest.
The reverence in his heart involuntarily deepened.
Just then—
[Ding! You have received a new class change quest.]
[Prompt: A new quest has been added to your quest log. Please check the details.]
Daniel opened his quest log.
[Lord of Earth]
Forbidden-grade archer class change quest
Restriction: forbidden-grade archer
Quest Difficulty: Exalted-grade
Quest Objectives:
Control Earth’s World Origin and obtain the highest authority.
Defend Earth.
Quest Introduction:
Earth is a complete small world with its own World Origin. Whoever controls it will possess the highest authority over Earth. You must seize this authority.

Once Earth’s coordinates are made public, it will be like a piece of rich, fatty meat, attracting countless hungry wolves. You must defend it. You must not allow Earth to be destroyed by enemies, nor can you lose the highest authority.
Prompt:

Starfarers dream of finding a living world where they can settle down. To them, an unclaimed Earth is a treasure worth risking their lives to seize. Astral Corsairs will also not miss the opportunity to plunder Earth.

There are countless worlds and countless massive forces in the current star region, and every single one has ambitions of expansion. A world with publicly revealed coordinates is like a lamp in the darkness. It will draw them all in.
You must become powerful enough to protect Earth and your entire race from endless invasions.
Quest Duration: Long-term
Quest Reward: Starlight Rankings participation qualification ×1, forbidden-grade archer Class Awakening Scroll ×1.

chapters.title: Chapter 237 -237-Wolves on Every Side, the Assassin Luna_Fox
paragraphs: Daniel read through the class change quest several times from beginning to end.
This time, he actually felt a trace of pressure.
He had accepted so many absurd and incredibly difficult quests before, yet he had never known how to spell the word "pressure."
Only this time did his heart feel heavy.
Perhaps it was because this quest was tied to Earth.
Earth was his root, his homeland, the place he would risk his life to protect!
Moreover, the quest had rarely given him hints.
He had already seen Starfarers before. Conrad was a living example standing right in front of him.
Daniel understood better than anyone just how desperately those rootless wanderers drifting through the stars longed for a living world where they could settle down.
Once Earth’s coordinates were made public, to that group, it would be like a wolf that had starved for countless days suddenly smelling blood.
How vast was the star region?
He did not know.
But he knew that after the new version began, countless waves of Starfarer invasions would definitely arrive.
And there were also the Astral Corsairs.
Through Conrad’s description, he had gained some understanding of those people as well. They were desperadoes who specialized in plundering every resource they possibly could.
Any force capable of becoming Astral Corsairs had to have at least one divine-grade powerhouse holding the fort.
It was said that truly powerful pirate forces could even dominate an entire star system, forcing every living world within that system into misery and suffering.
How could they possibly let go of a piece of "fresh meat" like Earth?
If all of those were only small fry, then there were even more terrifying existences—
Those colossal powers within the star region!
These forces were not something the God Realm powers could compare to.
At best, the Godkin were local tyrants within this one star system. Compared to the great forces of the Starfield Tier, they were not even worthy of carrying their shoes.
The great powers of the star region were warlords who commanded massive armies.
It was said that the strongest force in the current star region was called Gold Mountain!
It ruled over one-third of the star systems in the entire star region, and under its command were over ten thousand great worlds like the Godkin’s.
Earth would be extremely attractive to them as well.
In the Endless Starfield, every territory already had an owner. It either belonged to one force or another.
If one wanted to develop, one had to expand desperately and compete to the death.
How many hungry wolves would a freshly born Earth with no ability to protect itself attract?
Daniel knew the answer without even needing to think.
He took a deep breath.
As long as divine-grade powerhouses could not descend, he could endure every difficulty.
In truth, the difficulty was not quite as terrifying as the class change quest introduction made it sound.
What he was more interested in was the reward for this quest.
A Starlight Rankings participation qualification?
What was that?
He was somewhat confused.
However, most of the things given by class change quests were absolute top-tier treasures. It should not be bad.
Since he could not figure it out, he could not be bothered to keep thinking about it.
Once he completed the quest, he would naturally find out.
God Realm.
The Lord of the Radiant Sanctum, the Lord of the Hall of Divine Grace, and the Lord of the God of Light Temple sat inside the Radiant Sanctum.
The three sages who had remained behind to guard the Godkin all wore rather unpleasant expressions at this moment.
When the scene of Faustus instantly killing the invading enemies in Aetheria was transmitted over, a blurry figure suddenly flashed through the mind of Brand, the Lord of the God of Light Temple.
That shadow slowly overlapped with Faustus’ face.
It was as if he had remembered something.
And yet, it was also as if he had failed to grasp anything at all.
"This human’s strength is actually this terrifying!"
Brand’s voice carried a faint tremble.
"Faustus is a mortal threat to my Godkin!"
Hiram, the Lord of the Hall of Divine Grace, gnashed his teeth in hatred.
The intelligence had been wrong.
Was the information sent by the Overseer false?
Damn that Faustus!
Wasn’t he supposed to be in the Divine Wind Realm?
"Haah..."
Ankarach, the Lord of the Radiant Sanctum, shook his head.
If they were talking about hatred, he hated Faustus more than anyone!
His youngest son, Kahn, had died at that man’s hands.
But he could not descend into a small world. No matter how much he hated him, he could only endure it.
Then the image shifted again...
In the Divine Wind Realm, Faustus punched Nubat into scraps with one blow!
Hiram shot up from his chair, furious like a crazed beast.
"Damn Faustus! Nubat—!"
At this moment, among the three divine-grade powerhouses present, another one now had a blood feud with him.
Ankarach’s face was as gloomy as the sky before a storm.
"Speak. How do we deal with him next?"
Hiram’s eyes were bloodshot.
"I want him dead! As long as he dies, I don’t care what price we have to pay!"
Brand remained silent for a while before suddenly letting out a cold laugh.
"My suggestion is... we contact Luna_Fox!"
The expressions of the other two sages froze.
Luna_Fox!
That was the strongest assassination organization in the entire star region. If they could persuade them to act, then killing one Faustus truly did not seem like it would be difficult!
Hiram’s eyes lit up, and he said without hesitation, "Whatever price is required, I can pay a portion of it!"
Ankarach nodded as well.
"The same goes for me!"
Brand nodded, the corner of his mouth curling into an icy arc.
"In that case, this matter is settled!"
"With a top assassin from Luna_Fox taking action, I’d like to see how he keeps jumping around!"
Canaan Star Region.
In a place extremely far from Aetheria, there was a misty, rain-like river of stars.
Hidden within that galaxy was the most terrifying assassination organization in the Canaan Star Region—
Luna_Fox!
Luna_Fox was the name of a great world.
It ruled over the myriad races of the local starry sky, and it was the most fearsome name in this stretch of stars.
At this moment, inside a certain secret realm of Luna_Fox—
"Roar—!"
A magical beast with golden pupils had every hair on its body standing upright as it cautiously stared at the young man before it.
The sage rank of this divine-grade magical beast had already spread out, yet there was only fear in its eyes!
And standing opposite it was merely a demi-sage.
"Divine-grade magical beasts are still ultimately inferior to true divine-grade powerhouses."
Yexis felt that oppressive pressure, yet his expression remained as relaxed as if he were taking a stroll.
Boom—!
His Divine Domain abruptly unfolded.
Hundreds of figures appeared in the void. Every single one possessed demi-sage strength, and together they formed a tightly arranged magic formation.
The aura leaking from it was actually not the slightest bit weaker than the magical beast’s sage rank.
"Roar, roar, roar!"
The magical beast roared furiously. Its enormous body charged over like a mountain.
But its body passed straight through Yexis, as if it had collided with a mass of air!
"The Law of Space."
The magical beast’s golden pupils suddenly contracted.
The young powerhouse before it had actually mastered the power of laws.
And it was even the Law of Space, the law most suited for concealment and assassination.
If space were imagined as a painting, and every scene within that painting was alive, then the Law of Space was like a painting hidden within that painting.
Unless one’s strength could pierce through layer upon layer of space, one would never be able to touch the person hiding within the painting inside the painting.
Bang!
Bang! Bang!
Yexis flashed out from the void. His long staff struck the magical beast like a torrential storm.
To the naked eye, it seemed as though he had only tapped it lightly.
But in reality, in that single instant, he had already struck tens of millions of times. The sounds simply had no time to travel out.
The divine-grade magical beast trembled all over from the pain.
Although the life level of a divine-grade being had long since become fundamentally different, such densely packed attacks still drove it mad with pain.
Every staff strike that landed felt like a needle stabbing into the gaps between its bones.
Yexis suddenly stopped and exhaled deeply.
"What a feeble lifeform."
The moment his words fell, muffled crackling sounds suddenly erupted from within the magical beast’s body.
Its bones snapped. Its flesh and blood turned to pulp. A terrifying aura exploded from inside it.
Rumble—!
The entire giant beast shattered into powder.
A trace of fatigue appeared on Yexis’ face.
He had used a secret art called Endless Force. In one brief instant, he had struck billions of times, and every strike had delivered a thread of force into the magical beast’s body.
Once enough force had accumulated, detonating it would blow the enemy apart from the inside out, leaving nothing behind.
The life level of divine-grade powerhouses was far too high. Ordinary attacks were not very useful against them.
Specialized methods were required to injure them.
Killing them was even harder.
Only a force on the level of Luna_Fox had that kind of confidence. Luna_Fox had collected vast numbers of secret arts specifically designed to counter divine-grade beings.
Secret arts capable of allowing a Divine Domain to clash head-on against a sage rank, such as Endless Force, were all treasured trump cards kept at the very bottom of the chest.
Only a great force with such deep foundations could bring out things like this.

sentences.text: Daniel read through the class change quest several times from beginning to end.
This time, he actually felt a trace of pressure.
He had accepted so many absurd and incredibly difficult quests before, yet he had never known how to spell the word "pressure."
Only this time did his heart feel heavy.
Perhaps it was because this quest was tied to Earth.
Earth was his root, his homeland, the place he would risk his life to protect!
Moreover, the quest had rarely given him hints.
He had already seen Starfarers before.
Conrad was a living example standing right in front of him.
Daniel understood better than anyone just how desperately those rootless wanderers drifting through the stars longed for a living world where they could settle down.
Once Earth’s coordinates were made public, to that group, it would be like a wolf that had starved for countless days suddenly smelling blood.
How vast was the star region?
He did not know.
But he knew that after the new version began, countless waves of Starfarer invasions would definitely arrive.
And there were also the Astral Corsairs.
Through Conrad’s description, he had gained some understanding of those people as well.
They were desperadoes who specialized in plundering every resource they possibly could.
Any force capable of becoming Astral Corsairs had to have at least one divine-grade powerhouse holding the fort.
It was said that truly powerful pirate forces could even dominate an entire star system, forcing every living world within that system into misery and suffering.
How could they possibly let go of a piece of "fresh meat" like Earth?
If all of those were only small fry, then there were even more terrifying existences—
Those colossal powers within the star region!
These forces were not something the God Realm powers could compare to.
At best, the Godkin were local tyrants within this one star system.
Compared to the great forces of the Starfield Tier, they were not even worthy of carrying their shoes.
The great powers of the star region were warlords who commanded massive armies.
It was said that the strongest force in the current star region was called Gold Mountain!
It ruled over one-third of the star systems in the entire star region, and under its command were over ten thousand great worlds like the Godkin’s.
Earth would be extremely attractive to them as well.
In the Endless Starfield, every territory already had an owner.
It either belonged to one force or another.
If one wanted to develop, one had to expand desperately and compete to the death.
How many hungry wolves would a freshly born Earth with no ability to protect itself attract?
Daniel knew the answer without even needing to think.
He took a deep breath.
As long as divine-grade powerhouses could not descend, he could endure every difficulty.
In truth, the difficulty was not quite as terrifying as the class change quest introduction made it sound.
What he was more interested in was the reward for this quest.
A Starlight Rankings participation qualification?
What was that?
He was somewhat confused.
However, most of the things given by class change quests were absolute top-tier treasures.
It should not be bad.
Since he could not figure it out, he could not be bothered to keep thinking about it.
Once he completed the quest, he would naturally find out.
God Realm.
The Lord of the Radiant Sanctum, the Lord of the Hall of Divine Grace, and the Lord of the God of Light Temple sat inside the Radiant Sanctum.
The three sages who had remained behind to guard the Godkin all wore rather unpleasant expressions at this moment.
When the scene of Faustus instantly killing the invading enemies in Aetheria was transmitted over, a blurry figure suddenly flashed through the mind of Brand, the Lord of the God of Light Temple.
That shadow slowly overlapped with Faustus’ face.
It was as if he had remembered something.
And yet, it was also as if he had failed to grasp anything at all.
"This human’s strength is actually this terrifying!"
Brand’s voice carried a faint tremble.
"Faustus is a mortal threat to my Godkin!"
Hiram, the Lord of the Hall of Divine Grace, gnashed his teeth in hatred.
The intelligence had been wrong.
Was the information sent by the Overseer false?
Damn that Faustus!
Wasn’t he supposed to be in the Divine Wind Realm?
"Haah..."
Ankarach, the Lord of the Radiant Sanctum, shook his head.
If they were talking about hatred, he hated Faustus more than anyone!
His youngest son, Kahn, had died at that man’s hands.
But he could not descend into a small world.
No matter how much he hated him, he could only endure it.
Then the image shifted again...
In the Divine Wind Realm, Faustus punched Nubat into scraps with one blow!
Hiram shot up from his chair, furious like a crazed beast.
"Damn Faustus!
Nubat—!"
At this moment, among the three divine-grade powerhouses present, another one now had a blood feud with him.
Ankarach’s face was as gloomy as the sky before a storm.
"Speak.
How do we deal with him next?"
Hiram’s eyes were bloodshot.
"I want him dead!
As long as he dies, I don’t care what price we have to pay!"
Brand remained silent for a while before suddenly letting out a cold laugh.
"My suggestion is... we contact Luna_Fox!"
The expressions of the other two sages froze.
Luna_Fox!
That was the strongest assassination organization in the entire star region.
If they could persuade them to act, then killing one Faustus truly did not seem like it would be difficult!
Hiram’s eyes lit up, and he said without hesitation, "Whatever price is required, I can pay a portion of it!"
Ankarach nodded as well.
"The same goes for me!"
Brand nodded, the corner of his mouth curling into an icy arc.
"In that case, this matter is settled!"
"With a top assassin from Luna_Fox taking action, I’d like to see how he keeps jumping around!"
Canaan Star Region.
In a place extremely far from Aetheria, there was a misty, rain-like river of stars.
Hidden within that galaxy was the most terrifying assassination organization in the Canaan Star Region—
Luna_Fox!
Luna_Fox was the name of a great world.
It ruled over the myriad races of the local starry sky, and it was the most fearsome name in this stretch of stars.

chapters.title: Chapter 238 -238-Hunting the Contemporary Starchosen
paragraphs: Whoosh—!
A tear opened in the void, and a man dressed in coarse linen robes stepped out.
His long hair fell loosely over his shoulders. Barefoot, he stepped upon the void as if walking across the floor of his own backyard.
"You have passed your trial," the linen-robed powerhouse said. "But Yexis, you are still only second place. There is still a gap between you and first."
"I understand, Instructor."
Yexis respectfully lowered his head.
"I will strive to catch up to him."
The linen-robed powerhouse nodded.
"That chair at the top of the gold medal ranking has been occupied by that person for a hundred years."
"In truth, you could choose to break through to divine-grade and enter the Heaven Ranking. The resources on the Heaven Ranking are far richer than what you have now."
"Instructor, I still want to wait a little longer."
Light flashed in Yexis’ eyes.
"I want to be like those seniors in history—using demi-sage rank strength to cross ranks and slay a low-grade divine-grade being."
Throughout Luna_Fox’s history, there had been plenty of monsters who killed divine-grade beings while still at demi-sage rank.
There had even been madmen at supreme-grade who dared to make a move against divine-grade beings!
Yexis wanted to polish his Divine Domain to complete perfection. Only when he reached that step would he be willing to take the next one.
Once he broke through, he would become a high-grade divine-grade powerhouse!
"It is always good to have a goal."
The linen-robed powerhouse raised an eyebrow, a hint of admiration in his tone.

"But if you want to reach that level, you need a guardian to help you condense an invincible momentum among those of the same realm. Your points are still not enough. As it happens, I have a mission here. Once you complete it, you should have enough to invite an Oracle-grade powerhouse to serve as your guardian."
"Instructor, thank you for your guidance."
Yexis straightened his back.
"May I ask what the mission is?"
"This mission is a little strange."
The linen-robed powerhouse frowned slightly.
"The target is a legendary-grade human, but the information provided by the employer says that this person is almost invincible below divine-grade."
Hmm?!
Almost invincible below divine-grade?
"There is actually such a powerhouse?"
Yexis was startled. Immediately afterward, a thick fighting spirit surged up inside him.
"Could it be... my target is the contemporary top-ranked prodigy?"
A strange smile appeared on the linen-robed powerhouse’s face.
"You actually guessed correctly."
"Faustus, a human powerhouse from Aetheria. He once reached the summit of Cloudcrest Peak and is the Starchosen of this generation. Your mission is to kill him."
"No problem!"
Yexis’ eyes lit up.
He had not accepted an assassination mission targeting a legendary-grade being in a very, very long time.
But since the opponent was the contemporary Starchosen, he was tempted!
"I will complete this mission perfectly!"
The linen-robed powerhouse nodded.

"At present, you are the only suitable candidate for this mission. Gil is currently condensing his invincible momentum. He has already challenged the demi-sage rank peers of an entire star river and is preparing to come here to challenge us next."
"On Luna_Fox’s side, only that fellow ranked first among the gold medals is presentable, so he is currently preparing for the battle and cannot accept this mission."
Yexis softly muttered the name. A surging fighting spirit appeared on his face.
Gil had already challenged an entire star river, and he still intended to travel across the entire star region.
Under the protection of a guardian, he would challenge demi-sage peers from countless star rivers and use that to condense his invincible momentum.
Once that momentum was complete, when he broke through to divine-grade, he would directly become a peak divine-grade powerhouse!
He wanted to step on the faces of every prodigy of his generation across the entire star region, using their defeats to pave his own path to the heavens.
"What a pity. I am not yet qualified to become his opponent."
Yexis sighed inwardly.
Luna_Fox would only send out its strongest to answer the challenge, and the strongest was naturally that fellow ranked first among the gold medals.
"Do not be discouraged."
The linen-robed powerhouse’s figure gradually faded, and his voice became ethereal.
"Many people are unknown below divine-grade, only to shock the world once they break through."
"If you can complete this mission, I will personally become your guardian."
"Thank you, Instructor. Rest assured, I will definitely complete the mission."
Yexis’ voice was filled with confidence.
Aetheria, Steel Plateau.
Thousands of players had gathered before a radiant, flowing gate.
By crossing this gate, one could enter a trial ground matched to one’s own strength. This was the Phantom Emporium.
As they waited, low conversations sounded among the crowd.
"It wasn’t this crowded here before. What happened today?"
A young warrior frowned as he looked around.

"You still haven’t heard? Guild Leader Faustus released an emergency world announcement—the game and reality are about to merge into one. From now on, there will no longer be a distinction between ’game’ and ’reality.’"
"If we don’t hurry up and improve our strength, what are you planning to use to block the non-human races once disaster descends?"
The mage beside him lowered his voice, his tone carrying a hint of urgency.

"Yeah. I didn’t expect those experts to actually be right this time. Reality and the game really are going to merge! Once the fusion happens and order is reshaped, the only thing that can help us stand firm will be the Strength in our hands."
Another archer slowly nodded.

"No wonder those lifestyle players who usually only care about mining and making medicine have been grinding monsters like mad these past few days. Even market supplies have gone up by thirty percent."

"This matter involves too much. One careless move could cause chaos throughout the world. In my opinion, we should wait for Guild Leader Faustus’ arrangements. Don’t overthink it. Just honestly sharpen your sword. That’s the right thing to do."
"No matter how things change, strength is supreme! That phrase will never be wrong anywhere."
As they were speaking, light flashed within the gate, and several figures walked out.
Satisfied smiles hung on their faces. Clearly, they had gained quite a lot.
"It’s our turn."
"Let’s go. Let the monsters behind the gate witness our power."
A party walked up to the gate.
Team leader Hals paid the entrance fee, and the system prompt immediately rang out.
"Based on the current average level of the player party, legendary-grade monsters will now be generated."
The party’s figures immediately disappeared into the curtain of light.
Aerial Realm.
Faustus had not poured the Sacred Spring of Life onto the World Tree.
The Aerial Realm was already a complete small world. If it rose by one more level, it would become a medium life world. That meant divine-grade powerhouses would be able to descend.
To the current him, that was not good news.
At this moment, a group of players was surrounding a magical beast and attacking it fiercely!
"Void Rend!"
A warrior roared and slammed forward, knocking the magical beast off balance before immediately sending it flying with one spear strike.
"Frost Prison!"
The mage in the rear seized the timing perfectly. Ice elements instantly froze the magical beast in midair.
Another earth-type spell had already condensed in his palm.
"Piercing Arrow!"
The archer loosened two fingers, and an arrow shot out with a sharp whistle, nailing the magical beast that was about to fall back into the air again.
"Bloodblade Assault!"
Blood light flashed around the assassin. His dagger stabbed into the magical beast’s body like a venomous snake.
He did not retreat. One slash followed another as he frantically poured out damage.
Whoosh—!
Seeing that the magical beast was about to smash into the ground, the assassin rolled away and darted far off, quietly waiting for the next opportunity.
The mage’s earth-type spell was ready at exactly the right moment.
"Earthsplit Fist!"
From the soft ground, a giant fist formed from earth elements suddenly shot up, blasting the magical beast into the air once more.
The assassin instantly turned back, and his dagger stabbed in again.
The magical beast dropped once more—
But this time, the assassin did not move away.
The warrior’s launch skill had already finished cooling down!
"Voidrend Slash!"
Boom—!
Roar, roar, roar!!
The magical beast was sent flying yet again.
After this chain of attacks, the magical beast could only hang helplessly in midair like prey being toyed with.
Before long, its massive body crashed to the ground, exploding into a field of dazzling loot.
"Beautifully done."
Hans looked at the rewards scattered across the ground and smiled as he patted his teammate on the shoulder.
"Our teamwork is getting smoother and smoother. Legendary-grade magical beasts are no longer enough to look at—I suggest we challenge supreme-grade ones next."
The mage grinned.
"Seconded."
The archer nodded.
"We’re all legendary-grade now, and our damage output is fairly decent. Trying a supreme-grade one should be fine."
"Wait a little longer."
Hans shook his head.
"Teamwork is one thing, but we still have too few powerful skills."
"Let’s build up our foundation a bit more. Each of us can go to the guild and exchange for a few decent skill books before challenging one. It won’t be too late then."
The teammates fell silent for a moment, then nodded one after another.
"That works too," the mage said. "I’ve got my eye on a legendary-grade skill book. It suits me perfectly, but I’m still a little short on points."
"I’ve got something I want too."
The assassin smiled.
"There are just too many good things in the guild. Guild Leader Faustus is truly amazing. He can even sell supreme-grade equipment like cabbages."
"Of course. Guild Leader Faustus is forever a god, hahahaha."
Hans laughed.
"A legendary figure like that—I’m following him to the end."
"Hahaha, count me in!"
The mage gave a sly smile.
"I’m the guild leader’s most devout follower, after all."
"Count me in too."
"And me!"

The mage gave a sly smile.
"I’m the guild leader’s most devout follower, after all."
"Count me in too."
"And me!"

chapters.title: Chapter 239 -239-World Fusion, Four Key Points
paragraphs: Divine Wind Realm.
At this moment, all players ranked within the top five thousand on the Stellar Level Rankings had gathered in one place.
In the eyes of ordinary players, these people were lofty experts who stood high above the masses. But right now, every single one of them stood obediently, not even daring to breathe too loudly.
Because the person standing before them was the legend among players!
Daniel!
Daniel lifted his eyelids slightly, his gaze sweeping across everyone’s faces.
His eyes were cold and clear. His voice was not loud, yet it was like icy spring water seeping through cracks in stone, coolly slipping into everyone’s ears.
"The human race must continue moving upward, so the fusion of the game world and the real world is something that cannot be stopped."

He said, "I do not want to see the world descend into chaos and order collapse when that time comes. If anyone dares stir up trouble and commit evil after the fusion, don’t blame me for turning ruthless."
Hiss—!
Everyone present drew in a sharp breath at the same time.
Cold sweat had already broken out on many people’s foreheads.
No one doubted Daniel’s strength, and there was even less need to mention his power and influence.
He was the strongest existence in this world.
Without exception.
His prestige among players had already reached the ceiling. Once he had been placed on that pedestal, he had never come down.
Everyone present was shrewd. They all understood what Daniel meant.
Most of them had never had such thoughts to begin with. But even if a tiny part of them had, they would now have to carefully weigh the consequences.
What would happen if they angered this lord?
"In short," Daniel said calmly, "what I want is an orderly and stable world."
"Whatever Aetheria is like, Earth must become the same."
"Guild Leader!"
A veteran player from the guild suddenly stood up, his gaze sweeping across the surrounding crowd like a blade.

"We all understand what you mean. I’ll put my words here right now: whoever dares rely on whatever foundation they once had on Earth and refuse to obey the rules you set down will be making an enemy of the entire guild!"
"Then let them test whether our blades are sharp or not!"
"Guild Leader, I swear to follow you to the death."
"Guild Leader, I support you too."
"大神 Daniel, don’t worry. We all support you."
Very quickly, wave after wave of players stood up and voiced their stance.
Those with other thoughts sat as if on a bed of nails, feeling uncomfortable all over. Awkward smiles hung on their faces, but in the end, they also stood up and echoed the others.
Daniel saw this scene clearly.
He understood better than anyone what kind of people players were.
A lawless world was something many ambitious players longed for.
The entire world would be reshuffled, and they would hold Strength capable of crushing billions of people in their hands. Who would not want to climb upward?
Who would not want to taste the flavor of power?
Daniel simply would not give them that chance.
"After the game and reality fuse,"
His gaze pressed down on the noisy crowd like two torches.
"I will not forcibly keep you in the guild. But you had better think it through. Once you leave, you can forget about ever coming back."

"All guild resources will be closed to those who leave. Also, if anyone relies on their Strength to act recklessly, even if they are a brother who has followed me for the longest time, I will make sure they die without even ashes left behind."
"You had better carve these words into your minds."
He waved his hand.
"Meeting dismissed."
After saying that, Daniel turned and left.
He had always been decisive in the way he handled matters.
He drew only one red line.
Whoever stepped across it would die!
He would absolutely not leave these people any room to repeatedly test his limits.
After Daniel left, the players finally began discussing in twos and threes.
"By the gods, that aura from the guild leader just now nearly scared my soul out of my body."
A player let out a long breath.
"It was even more terrifying than facing a supreme-grade boss alone."
"Who says it wasn’t?"
Another player lowered his voice, as if afraid something might hear him.
"I didn’t even dare breathe too hard. I was afraid the guild leader would misunderstand and think I was disloyal to him, hahahaha..."
"But may the Lord bear witness, my loyalty to the guild leader is tougher than silver-grade metal forged by dwarves."
"The guild leader’s words hit the nail on the head."
Someone smiled bitterly and shook his head.
"Those young brats who grew up under Earth’s old order have suddenly been given such enormous Strength overnight. Who can guarantee they won’t go mad?"
"Exactly. We ’players’ know what kind of people we are, don’t we?"
They themselves were players.
Daniel’s words had been meant for them.
And only they had the ability to turn Earth upside down.
"I’ve already made up my mind to follow the guild leader."
A player smiled honestly, but his eyes were filled with seriousness.
"If he points east, I will never go west. If he tells me to cut someone down, my sword will point at that person."
"Without the guild leader, where would this strength of mine have come from?"
"Looks like I’ll have to go back and give my brothers a proper warning."
Someone sighed helplessly.
"It’s time to restrain ourselves a little and stop being too conspicuous."
"Yeah. When Strength rises too quickly, people’s hearts become hard to control."
"At a critical moment like this, who would dare become the first bird to stick its head out?"
Someone muttered under his breath, as if warning himself.
"The guild leader will definitely kill a chicken to warn the monkeys. Whoever jumps out first will be that chicken. Trying to show off? That’s just courting death."
Daniel found a quiet place and took the Scroll of Version Upgrade out of his backpack.
[Ding! Confirm use of Scroll of Version Upgrade?]
"Confirm."
[Ding! Use successful!]
The next moment, a grand world announcement resounded throughout the thousands of large and small World Zones of Stellar!
[Ding! The brand-new version "Lord of Earth" is about to begin. The game world and the real world have begun fusing...]
[All players, please note: After world fusion, players will no longer need gaming devices to log in.]
[After fusion, the game system will continue to exist. Advancement beyond supreme-grade will require Mental State to improve one’s realm.]
[Prompt: After world fusion, all game systems will remain unchanged.]
[Key emphasis!!!]
[All real-world game regions will merge and fuse into one Earth world. The world’s area and landmasses will expand drastically!]
[Note: After world fusion, players who die on Earth will no longer be able to resurrect.]

[After the new version begins, the Gate of Reincarnation will open. The Gate of Reincarnation exists within every player’s system and can instantly appear at the bound resurrection point. Note: Currently, only Aetheria has resurrection points. Aside from Earth, deaths in all other planes will automatically result in appearance at a resurrection point.]
[Prompt: After world fusion, version update maintenance will begin. Estimated duration: five minutes. After maintenance ends, all players will appear on Earth by default.]
Daniel listened as system prompts popped up beside his ear one after another.
Overall, the changes were not too great.
There were four most obvious points.
First, gaming devices were no longer needed.
Every player’s system now had a Gate of Reincarnation. Through it, they could instantly return to their bound resurrection point.
Second, Earth had become special.
After the game fused with reality, all Earths where humans from different worlds lived would be forcibly fused together, forming a brand-new, enormous Earth!
Third point.
If one died on other planes, one could still resurrect.
Only death on Earth was true death.
There was definitely some secret hidden behind this.
Fourth, after reaching supreme-grade and above, players could no longer rely on killing monsters to gain experience and level up. From then on, they had to rely on themselves!
Even after reaching the required level, the Divine Domain would not generate on its own. Everything would depend on one’s own ability.
Mainly speaking, these were the four points that needed attention!

chapters.title: Chapter 240 -240-The Birth of Earth Origin
paragraphs: Just then, the system notification rang out once more.

[World Announcement: Player [Faustus] has unlocked a new version. The game and reality are about to merge. The system will enter update maintenance. Estimated duration: five minutes. All update notes will be sent to every player’s mailbox. Please log out as soon as possible.]
[Countdown begins: 59... 58... 57...]
Without saying another word, Daniel exited the game.
His vision blurred. When he opened his eyes again, he was already awake inside the game cabin.
Daniel climbed out of the cabin.
Then he discovered that the spatial ring on his hand had actually followed him back into reality.
He could also vaguely sense that there was a hidden pocket of space he could open at any moment, almost like a portable storage dimension.
That should be the backpack from the game.
The game interface was still floating in his field of vision, only now it had become semi-transparent.
Class, pets, equipment, skills, faction...
Everything that should have been there was still there. He could open whichever panel he wanted.
Overall, it was no different from how things had been in the game.
He wanted to test whether his combat power had fully merged over as well.
Daniel stretched out his hand and silently chanted in his heart.
"Arrow of Judgment!"
Buzz—!
The air trembled slightly.
A mass of holy light appeared out of thin air in his palm, so bright it was almost blinding.
Daniel sensed it carefully. The intensity of this power was roughly ninety percent of what it had been in the game!
Most likely, once the version update ended, he would be able to fully master this power!
At the same time, players all over the world logged out one after another, sensing the differences between themselves now and their in-game selves.
Two new pieces of information appeared in many people’s minds.
The first was an explanation of the changes brought by the fusion.
The second was a portal—the Gate of Reincarnation!
At this moment, the Gate of Reincarnation still displayed the maintenance timer. Only after these five minutes passed would they be able to connect to the system again.
In other words, every player’s strength, items, skills, pets...
Everything had merged over with them!
"This is way too convenient!"
A mage stared blankly at the little flame dancing in his palm, his grin stretching almost to his ears.
"From now on, I don’t even need to spend money on a lighter anymore. I can just rub out a little fireball."
"Watch this."
A man took a deep breath, bent down, and hooked one finger under the chassis of a heavy truck beside him.
With a gentle lift—
The entire truck was flipped up as if it were made of paper.
The man’s face lit up with excitement.
"I only used one finger..."
"What should I do..."
An archer narrowed his eyes, his gaze passing through the window and landing on the blazing sun in the sky. He licked his lips eagerly.
"My greatest wish in life has always been to see whether I can shoot that thing down."
"Hahaha... you brat, you’re seriously getting way too full of yourself!"
"Exactly. Even Lord Faustus might not be able to do something like that, and yet you actually dare to imagine it?"
The five minutes of maintenance passed in the blink of an eye.

[Ding—The Gate of Reincarnation has been opened! Players may pass through the Gate of Reincarnation and travel to their bound resurrection-point cities. Please note: Earth may now establish Starfield Portals to allow faster travel to various planes.]

[World Announcement: The current Earth Origin is condensing into form. Once the Origin has fully condensed, the coordinates of this star region will be made public to all worlds. Players—please defend your homeland.]
"Origin? What’s that?"
A player frowned, then suddenly looked up.
"Huh... why do I feel an incredibly powerful aura awakening in the north?"
"Earth Origin? Just from the name, it sounds like some priceless treasure."
Many players sensed that fluctuation as well, and their eyes began to shine.
"Where is it? Is that aura in the north?"
"What a terrifying pressure... It feels like it’s coming from the north. Is that the Origin?"
"Let’s go take a look!"
More and more players rushed in the direction of the aura.
Quite a few of them were legendary-grade players. They rode the wind through the air, as fast as shooting stars.
Others relied on magical equipment and likewise possessed the ability to fly, whistling across the sky.
All they could see was the radiance of the Origin. None of them could see the blood and fire hidden behind that light.
Once the coordinates were made public, what kind of disaster would they attract?
No one had even thought about it.
Perhaps this was simply the nature branded into players’ very bones: they would always see the benefits first, and never the blade.
Daniel had also sensed that the Origin was awakening.
His class-change mission was to take control of the Origin and repel all forces and powerful beings coveting Earth.
"Earth Origin... is mine!"
His figure abruptly vanished.
When he reappeared, he was already above a distant stretch of sea.
"The aura of the Origin... Let’s go take a look too."
"If someone can control the Origin, does that mean they’ll become the Lord of Earth?"
"Guild Leader Faustus will definitely go, right? Who could possibly snatch that thing from him?"
The system notification had spread the news of Earth Origin’s birth to every corner of the world.
The players all had different thoughts, but without exception, they began gathering toward the direction where that aura was surging.
"This should be the place."
Daniel looked down from above.
On the surface of the sea, a massive vortex was slowly rotating, like a sleeping eye gradually opening.
Deep within the vortex, a dazzling seven-colored light shimmered faintly.
"That’s right... that’s the Origin."
Boom—!
Without hesitation, he plunged into the vortex and sank into the deep sea.
At the same time, Immortal Singularity unfolded around him, forming a dry domain that kept the crushing seawater completely at bay.
He dove rapidly downward, drawing closer and closer to that cluster of radiance.
Only when he got near did he finally see it clearly—
The Origin was only the size of a fist. It was round, like a star that had been left behind on the seafloor.
Light flowed within it, as though endless life was being nurtured inside.
He took a deep breath and reached out his hand.
The instant his fingertip touched the Origin—
Boom!
A thunderous roar exploded in Daniel’s mind. The images before his eyes shattered violently, then quickly reassembled.
When he could see the world clearly again, it was as if he was no longer "himself."
He stood above the nine heavens, looking down upon the entire planet.
He was not seeing with his eyes.
It was more like...
The world itself had opened its eyes.
Mountains, rivers, forests, deserts—every inch of land appeared within his perception.

The flight paths of birds crossing the sky, the arcs of fish schools weaving through ocean currents, even the blooming of a wildflower somewhere on the earth and the bead of dew resting on a blade of grass—
He could see all of it with perfect clarity.
He saw countless players from Doom Guild rushing toward this place.
He saw the excited and confused players in the cities.
He saw ordinary people who still had no idea that the world was about to undergo a heaven-shaking transformation.
He even saw beyond Earth.

He saw the space station silently suspended in near-Earth orbit, mining vehicles slowly crawling across the surface of the Moon, a lonely rover traversing the barren plains of Mars, and the infinitely distant starry sky beyond.
Daniel felt something strange.
He had become the ruler of this planet.
His will was the will of this world.
"Move."
He silently commanded in his heart, sensing a towering mountain range in the distance and imagining it shifting one inch to the left.
Rumble, rumble—!
That mountain range let out a deep, muffled roar. The earth trembled, and the entire mountain was forcibly shifted by a centimeter.
"Rise."
With a turn of his thoughts, the vast sea suddenly churned violently, rolling up waves hundreds of meters high.

Sharks, jellyfish, octopuses, and giant whales were thrown into the air by the towering waves. Beneath the sunlight, they traced bright silver arcs through the sky before crashing thunderously back into the water.
"So this is what it feels like to become a Lord of Worlds..."
Daniel understood.

He even saw beyond Earth.

He saw the space station silently suspended in near-Earth orbit, mining vehicles slowly crawling across the surface of the Moon, a lonely rover traversing the barren plains of Mars, and the infinitely distant starry sky beyond.
Daniel felt something strange.
He had become the ruler of this planet.
His will was the will of this world.
"Move."
He silently commanded in his heart, sensing a towering mountain range in the distance and imagining it shifting one inch to the left.
Rumble, rumble—!
That mountain range let out a deep, muffled roar.
The earth trembled, and the entire mountain was forcibly shifted by a centimeter.
"Rise."
With a turn of his thoughts, the vast sea suddenly churned violently, rolling up waves hundreds of meters high.
Sharks, jellyfish, octopuses, and giant whales were thrown into the air by the towering waves.
Beneath the sunlight, they traced bright silver arcs through the sky before crashing thunderously back into the water.
"So this is what it feels like to become a Lord of Worlds..."
Daniel understood.

chapters.title: Chapter 241 -241-Coordinates Exposed, Defend the Homeland
paragraphs: This was the Strength that Earth Origin granted Daniel!
The Strength to change the entire world!
No wonder those who died on Earth could not be reborn—because Earth possessed an Origin.
Aerial Realm, the Divine Wind Realm, and those so-called complete small worlds did not.
Aetheria also had an Origin.
Only an Origin could create transcendents and advancement systems. Only an Origin could allow them to be reborn after death. That was the Strength to establish rules.
But Daniel had never learned how to use an Origin.
He had only just touched the threshold. Like a freshman who had just enrolled, he had to learn everything from the very beginning.
Just then—
[Ding! Do you wish to absorb and master the Origin? Upon success, you will merge with this world and become the ruler of the world, unlocking more world rules.]

[Warning! During the absorption process, you must not be disturbed. The process cannot be interrupted. Otherwise, you will suffer the Origin’s backlash. The consequences will be extremely severe—at best, you will be imprisoned inside the Origin forever, unable to escape; at worst, the Origin will collapse and the planet will be destroyed!]
Hiss—!
Daniel sucked in a cold breath, a chill running down his spine.
He could not be interrupted. He could not be disturbed...
And the consequences were unimaginably serious!
He did not dare delay for even a moment. He immediately contacted Camille through the puppet avatar stationed in Aetheria, then severed his connection with the Origin and flew out of the vortex.
Players were already swarming over from every direction.
"Guild Leader! You’re here!"
When they saw Daniel, they surrounded him one after another and greeted him.
"You came at just the right time."
Daniel gave the order in a deep voice.
"Doom Legion, hear my command—seal off an area of ten thousand miles. No one is allowed to take even a single step inside."
Seeing Daniel’s incomparably serious expression, everyone who heard him felt a chill crawl across their necks.
"As you command, Guild Leader!"
The top experts on the world level rankings accepted the order in unison and quickly scattered, surrounding this sea region as tightly as an iron barrel.
Fortunately, the Guild Leader had not ordered them to clear the area by force. Many players secretly breathed a sigh of relief.
A game was one thing. Reality was another.
In the game, good and evil were nothing more than symbols judged by the system. More importantly, people would not truly die. But in reality, no one was a cold-blooded butcher.
Merely stopping people was still something they could accept.
Daniel did not have especially high expectations of them either.

This group of players had not experienced the dark and bloody era of his previous lives. They still carried the inertia of law in their hearts. Their values were upright, and their moral sense was strong. That was perfectly normal.
But they obeyed orders.
The strongest among them were all under his command. As for the weaker ones, they probably could not make it here anyway.
He took a deep breath and once again dived into the depths of the Origin.
[Ding! Confirm absorption of Earth Origin? During the absorption process, you must not be interrupted or disturbed in any way...]
"Confirm."
This time, he did not hesitate in the slightest.
[Ding! You have begun absorbing the Origin. Earth’s coordinates are about to be made public to all worlds.]

[World Announcement: Player [Faustus] is absorbing "Earth Origin." Earth’s coordinates are about to be made public! All players, please take note—countless forces and powerful beings from the starry sky will inevitably come after hearing the news!]
[Warning: The countdown to the Defense War of Earth has begun!]
[Warning: The countdown to the Defense War of Earth has begun!]
[Warning: The countdown to the Defense War of Earth has begun!]
[Notification: Origin absorption in progress. Estimated completion time: seven days.]
[Notification: During the absorption period, "Faustus" cannot move and cannot perform any actions.]
In an instant, all players erupted into an uproar.
"The Guild Leader can’t move? Earth... Earth is in danger!"
"We have to keep a close watch on this place."
"Don’t be scared. We have strength in numbers. The sky won’t fall."
"I hope so."
Someone spoke in a low voice, uncertainty hidden in his tone.
"Earth... is our home, after all."
Divine Wind Realm.
Daniel’s puppet avatar was staying together with Camille.
Suddenly, Conrad hurried over.
"My lord, a world with publicly revealed coordinates has appeared on the star chart."
Conrad’s face was filled with astonishment.
"This kind of situation is extremely rare in the starry sky. Even newly born worlds would not directly expose their coordinates."
"My lord, this world is within our star system. Should we fight for it?"
Conrad’s eyes shone brightly.
That was a complete small world. Its resources would definitely not be lacking.
With Daniel and Camille’s strength, they were fully capable of taking it into their possession.
"This world is already in my grasp."
Daniel’s puppet avatar smiled faintly.
"You stay behind and guard Divine Wind Realm. Be on guard in case the Godkin send more powerful beings to invade. Camille and I will go."
"As you command, my lord."
Boom—!
Daniel’s puppet avatar and Camille descended upon Earth with overwhelming force.
"Master, is this the homeland you mentioned?"
Camille sensed this world and frowned slightly.
"Once its starry-sky coordinates are made public, I’m afraid this place will become a purgatory battlefield."
"As long as no divine-grade beings appear, there’s nothing to fear."
Daniel smiled.
"My main body is absorbing the Origin right now. We only need to hold out for seven days. With us here, no storm is worth fearing."
The two arrived at the land of the Origin.
Daniel gathered all the powerful beings present and gave his instructions.
"Go notify everyone. Have them all leave Earth and head to Aetheria. This place is about to become a battlefield."
"Guild Leader, let us stay and help you!"
"That’s right, Boss. We want to defend Earth, our homeland, together with you!"
"You may decide for yourselves."
Daniel said calmly.
"But let me say this first. If you are caught in the aftermath and die, then don’t come back to support me again."
"For now, however, you need to think of every possible way to notify everyone to leave. As long as the message is delivered, that will be enough."
"As you command. We’ll immediately find a way to notify everyone."
Very soon, the same message flooded the internet, radio stations, and short-video platforms of every country.
Everyone was to return to Aetheria through the Gate of Reincarnation.
Next, Earth would face endless invasion and war.
Ninety-nine percent of players chose to return to Aetheria and avoid the war.
But a very small number of people decided to stay behind and do their part to defend Earth, their homeland.
"With fine wine, we welcome our dearest friends. With sharp swords, we greet jackals and wolves!"
The players who stayed behind gripped their weapons tightly. Battle intent burned in their eyes, and their morale soared like a rainbow.
"Sovereignty is in our hands! How could we allow non-human races to manipulate us? Fight!"
"Glory to the human race! Defend our homeland! Fight to the last drop of blood!"
Ansel was a member of the White Bone Pirate Crew.
As a supreme-grade being, he counted as a grassroots backbone within the organization.
Not long ago, the captain had found him and said that he had discovered a plane with publicly revealed coordinates. He needed Ansel to investigate it.
Ansel was the most professional intelligence gatherer among them, so the task naturally fell to him.
Ansel knew very well that a plane with publicly revealed coordinates was both dangerous and tempting.
The true danger did not lie in the prey itself, but in the hunters.
That was a group so vast it was terrifying.
Starfarers yearned for territory. Pirates yearned for resources. Galactic powers yearned to expand their borders.

They were like wild dogs searching for food in the dark night. Upon smelling meat, their first reaction was not to pounce forward, but to prick up their ears, widen their eyes, and clearly see whether there were lions and tigers hidden in the darkness.
Ansel was the pirate crew’s eyes and ears.
At this moment, he had already arrived near Earth.
And he saw this fat, juicy piece of meat!
It was so peaceful and beautiful that he could not help but lose himself in it.

chapters.title: Chapter 242 -242-Powerful Enemies Arrive, Envoys of Two Races
paragraphs: However, Ansel quickly came back to his senses.
He had not forgotten that he had come here for serious business. He took a starry-sky disk out of his spatial ring.
This was one of the most common infiltration tools in the Endless Starfield. It could silently penetrate the barriers of a world.
Whoosh—!
In the next moment, Ansel slipped into Earth.
He was a top-tier scout, and he gathered every piece of valuable intelligence he could find: geography, resources, the strength of the natives, the characteristics of their civilization...
More importantly, he also had to search for his own kind—scouts sent by other forces.
According to the unwritten rules of the starry sky, scouts from major factions would all leave behind special markers.
It was just like tigers in the mountains using excrement to mark their territory. When other beasts smelled the scent, they would tactfully take a detour.
Ansel stayed on Earth for a full three days before leaving, bringing back extremely important intelligence.
Starfall Isle of the White Bone Pirate Crew.
Ansel presented the information he had gathered.

"What? The Blackwater Pirate Crew is here too! And there are also the Starfarer Mori Race, the Zhuihe Race, and one hundred and eighty other races? The sirenfolk, shadowkin, and Godkin of the local star system have also come to muddy the waters... Even the Council of Ten Thousand Races has arrived!"
The aura of a divine-grade powerhouse raged like a storm around the captain of the White Bone Pirate Crew.
Ansel knelt at the side, trembling from head to toe.
These were the various forces he had counted over the past three days. Even if the accuracy was not ninety-nine percent, it was at least ninety percent...
One could imagine that the actual number of forces involved would only be even greater.
It was easy to foresee what kind of terrifying situation this plane was about to face.
Wolves surrounded it on all sides.
Enemies lay in every direction.
"What a pity."
Ansel sighed inwardly.
"This plane probably can’t be protected. If they’re lucky, the powerful beings of this world might be able to take part of their race and flee, becoming Starfarers."
"If they’re unlucky, the entire world will be torn to shreds by the flames of war."
"Hmm... This is a little troublesome."
The pirate captain rubbed his brow.

Even with the strength of the White Bone Pirates, they had to be cautious in the face of such a situation. They had to calculate input and output with perfect precision, or else they would lose everything down to their underpants.
At the same time, scouts from various factions withdrew one after another, and intelligence reports were submitted in succession.
The major forces immediately realized that this fat piece of meat before them had already been covered in steel nails.
If anyone tried to swallow it whole, they would inevitably shatter every tooth in their mouth.
Among them, the Godkin were the most shocked.
"What? Traces of the Aetheria human race appeared there... It seems Faustus has also gotten involved."
"This matter is of great importance. We Godkin will observe for now."
"With that fellow Faustus there, anyone who wants to devour this plane will have to knock out their front teeth first."
"Let’s watch and wait for the time being. We have to be more cautious..."
Earth.
Two envoys had arrived before Daniel.
One had an alluring figure and an incomparably beautiful face. A soul-stirring charm flowed through her eyes.
She was the envoy of the sirenfolk.

Legend said that the sirenfolk lived in coral palaces deep beneath the sea. Their skin was as lustrous as pearls, their hair as soft and smooth as seaweed, and every movement they made carried the rhythm of the tides.
The other was shrouded from head to toe in pitch-black demonic energy. His face was hideous, and his keratinized skin was covered in strange runes.
That was the envoy of the shadowkin.
"The shadowkin only want control over this plane. We can allocate a habitat for your human race."
The shadowkin envoy spoke coldly, his tone filled with a condescending sense of charity.
"We sirenfolk are much more generous than they are."
The sirenfolk envoy smiled sweetly and glanced at the shadowkin beside her. Her voice was as soft as the sea breeze.
"We only request that a spatial portal be opened between the Siren Realm and this world, allowing both worlds to interact as equals and exchange what each side lacks."
"Hmph!"
The shadowkin envoy snorted coldly.
"Whoever believes you sirenfolk is an idiot."
"What you’re doing is cutting flesh with a dull knife. You simply want to devour this world bit by bit."
"Enough."
Daniel impatiently interrupted them, his gaze icy.
"Go back and tell the people behind you that I reject the conditions of both your races."
He sneered, his eyes as if he were looking at two ants who did not know whether they were alive or dead.
"You didn’t even bother asking around to find out what happened to the Godkin after they opposed me."
"And the two of you dare to come here and threaten me? Are you even worthy?"
"If you don’t leave now, you can forget about ever going back."
"Wait!"
The sirenfolk envoy hurriedly spoke, a trace of panic in her voice.
"We sirenfolk can also help you fight against the other enemies..."
"Get lost."
Daniel spat out only one word.
"Don’t make me say it a second time."
The faces of the two envoys turned alternately green and white. Hatred hid deep in their eyes, but in the end, they did not dare say another word. Gritting their teeth, they turned and left.
"Master, why didn’t you just kill them?"
Camille stood at the side and asked in confusion.
Daniel looked at the two sorry figures as they fled into the distance and said calmly, "Right now, the wolves are all restraining one another. None of them dares to make the first move."
"But none of them are willing to let go either. If we have to guard against them day and night, how could we possibly have that much energy?"
His eyes suddenly turned cold, and his voice became as chilling as poisoned steel.
"So I need to establish authority. Kill the chicken to warn the monkeys."
Camille understood at once.
The sirenfolk and the shadowkin were that chicken.
"Camille, are you afraid of death?"
Daniel suddenly asked with a smile.
"Afraid?"
Camille grinned, battle intent blazing in her eyes.
"I’m only afraid there won’t be enough enemies, or that they’ll be too weak to give me a satisfying slaughter!"
"Hmph! He actually dared to humiliate my race like that!"
The shadowkin envoy and the sirenfolk envoy flew out of Earth side by side, their resentment still raging along the way.
The shadowkin envoy gritted his teeth.
"Once I return and report this, I will definitely make that human fool pay!"
The sirenfolk envoy’s expression was no better. Those enchanting eyes were now filled with venomous hatred.
"We sirenfolk spoke to him politely and sincerely, yet he dared to treat us with such contempt!"
The sirenfolk envoy took a deep breath, her beautiful face twisting slightly.
The two powerful beings exchanged a glance, as though they had reached some kind of tacit agreement. After that, they each went their separate ways.
Their movements were immediately seen clearly by the scouts of the various major forces.
"The envoys of the sirenfolk and shadowkin... just left like that?"
"Look at their faces. They’re so livid you could probably squeeze juice out of them. They must have nearly crushed their teeth from grinding them, right?"
"Hahaha— The talks collapsed! They definitely collapsed!"
"Good! With so many eyes watching and everyone practically drooling themselves dry, the talks collapsed? Then let’s fight!"
Demon Realm.
After returning to the Demon Realm, the shadowkin envoy went straight to the person in charge of this matter.
"How did the negotiation go?"
The shadowkin powerhouse frowned.
"Why did you return so quickly? Did they accept, or did they refuse?"
"Reporting to you, my lord."
The shadowkin envoy lowered his head respectfully.
"The talks are over. Our demands were rejected outright by that human."
"Mm."
The shadowkin person in charge nodded, not taking it too seriously.
"That was within my expectations."
He had seen far too many things like this, and he had seen countless leaders as well. Some surrendered decisively, while others refused decisively. There was nothing strange about it.
"There is one more matter..."
The shadowkin envoy hesitated, a conflicted look appearing on his face.
"What is it?"
The shadowkin person in charge raised his brow.
"Dragging your feet and stammering like that is the style of those schemers among the Godkin. We shadowkin never beat around the bush. Speak plainly!"
"Reporting to you, my lord..."
The shadowkin envoy gritted his teeth, hatred surging in his eyes.
"It would have been one thing if that human merely refused. But he actually dared to openly humiliate us shadowkin!"
"How did he humiliate us?"
The shadowkin person in charge widened his eyes.
"That human Faustus’s exact words were—’What the hell are you shadowkin? You think you’re worthy of negotiating conditions with me?’"
The shadowkin envoy carefully glanced at the person in charge and quickly continued.
"He also said that even if he handed that plane over to the Godkin for free, he would never let us shadowkin benefit from it, and he told us to get as far away as possible!"
"What outrageous audacity!"
The shadowkin person in charge flew into a towering rage. Demonic energy around him erupted like a volcano, making even the air tremble.
"A mere human actually dares to be this arrogant! Hateful! Utterly hateful!"
"Pass down my military order—the Bloodriver Legion is to assemble immediately!"
"Exterminate the human race from top to bottom!"
"Not a single living being is to be left alive!"
