"We sirenfolk are much more generous than they are."
The sirenfolk envoy smiled sweetly and glanced at the shadowkin beside her.
Her voice was as soft as the sea breeze.
"We only request that a spatial portal be opened between the Siren Realm and this world, allowing both worlds to interact as equals and exchange what each side lacks."
"Hmph!"
The shadowkin envoy snorted coldly.
"Whoever believes you sirenfolk is an idiot."
"What you’re doing is cutting flesh with a dull knife.
You simply want to devour this world bit by bit."
"Enough."
Daniel impatiently interrupted them, his gaze icy.
"Go back and tell the people behind you that I reject the conditions of both your races."
He sneered, his eyes as if he were looking at two ants who did not know whether they were alive or dead.
"You didn’t even bother asking around to find out what happened to the Godkin after they opposed me."
"And the two of you dare to come here and threaten me?
Are you even worthy?"
"If you don’t leave now, you can forget about ever going back."
"Wait!"
The sirenfolk envoy hurriedly spoke, a trace of panic in her voice.
"We sirenfolk can also help you fight against the other enemies..."
"Get lost."
Daniel spat out only one word.
"Don’t make me say it a second time."
The faces of the two envoys turned alternately green and white.
Hatred hid deep in their eyes, but in the end, they did not dare say another word.
Gritting their teeth, they turned and left.
"Master, why didn’t you just kill them?"
Camille stood at the side and asked in confusion.
Daniel looked at the two sorry figures as they fled into the distance and said calmly, "Right now, the wolves are all restraining one another.
None of them dares to make the first move."
"But none of them are willing to let go either.
If we have to guard against them day and night, how could we possibly have that much energy?"
His eyes suddenly turned cold, and his voice became as chilling as poisoned steel.
"So I need to establish authority.
Kill the chicken to warn the monkeys."
Camille understood at once.
The sirenfolk and the shadowkin were that chicken.
"Camille, are you afraid of death?"
Daniel suddenly asked with a smile.
"Afraid?"
Camille grinned, battle intent blazing in her eyes.
"I’m only afraid there won’t be enough enemies, or that they’ll be too weak to give me a satisfying slaughter!"
"Hmph!
He actually dared to humiliate my race like that!"
The shadowkin envoy and the sirenfolk envoy flew out of Earth side by side, their resentment still raging along the way.
The shadowkin envoy gritted his teeth.
"Once I return and report this, I will definitely make that human fool pay!"
The sirenfolk envoy’s expression was no better.
Those enchanting eyes were now filled with venomous hatred.
"We sirenfolk spoke to him politely and sincerely, yet he dared to treat us with such contempt!"
The sirenfolk envoy took a deep breath, her beautiful face twisting slightly.
The two powerful beings exchanged a glance, as though they had reached some kind of tacit agreement.
After that, they each went their separate ways.
Their movements were immediately seen clearly by the scouts of the various major forces.
"The envoys of the sirenfolk and shadowkin... just left like that?"
"Look at their faces.
They’re so livid you could probably squeeze juice out of them.
They must have nearly crushed their teeth from grinding them, right?"
"Hahaha— The talks collapsed!
They definitely collapsed!"
"Good!
With so many eyes watching and everyone practically drooling themselves dry, the talks collapsed?
Then let’s fight!"
Demon Realm.
After returning to the Demon Realm, the shadowkin envoy went straight to the person in charge of this matter.
"How did the negotiation go?"
The shadowkin powerhouse frowned.
"Why did you return so quickly?
Did they accept, or did they refuse?"
"Reporting to you, my lord."
The shadowkin envoy lowered his head respectfully.
"The talks are over.
Our demands were rejected outright by that human."
"Mm."
The shadowkin person in charge nodded, not taking it too seriously.
"That was within my expectations."
He had seen far too many things like this, and he had seen countless leaders as well.
Some surrendered decisively, while others refused decisively.
There was nothing strange about it.
"There is one more matter..."
The shadowkin envoy hesitated, a conflicted look appearing on his face.
"What is it?"
The shadowkin person in charge raised his brow.
"Dragging your feet and stammering like that is the style of those schemers among the Godkin.
We shadowkin never beat around the bush.
Speak plainly!"
"Reporting to you, my lord..."
The shadowkin envoy gritted his teeth, hatred surging in his eyes.
"It would have been one thing if that human merely refused.
But he actually dared to openly humiliate us shadowkin!"
"How did he humiliate us?"
The shadowkin person in charge widened his eyes.
"That human Faustus’s exact words were—’What the hell are you shadowkin?
You think you’re worthy of negotiating conditions with me?’"
The shadowkin envoy carefully glanced at the person in charge and quickly continued.
"He also said that even if he handed that plane over to the Godkin for free, he would never let us shadowkin benefit from it, and he told us to get as far away as possible!"
"What outrageous audacity!"
The shadowkin person in charge flew into a towering rage.
Demonic energy around him erupted like a volcano, making even the air tremble.
"A mere human actually dares to be this arrogant!
Hateful!
Utterly hateful!"
"Pass down my military order—the Bloodriver Legion is to assemble immediately!"
"Exterminate the human race from top to bottom!"
"Not a single living being is to be left alive!"

chapters.title: Chapter 243 -243-The Wrath of Two Great Powers
paragraphs: Sirenfolk Realm.
The sirenfolk envoy passed through layers upon layers of coral palaces and returned to that boundless world of emerald waves, where she met the one in charge of her race.
"What?"
The sirenfolk administrator could hardly believe it.
"He rejected us that cleanly?"
"Did you make yourself clear? The conditions we sirenfolk offered are something no sane creature would ever refuse!"
His gaze was as sharp as a blade as he stared fixedly at the envoy.
"Did you truly convey our goodwill exactly as it was?"
The sirenfolk envoy trembled with grievance.
Goodwill?
That human had not even been willing to listen to one more word. He had not even let her finish speaking.
"My lord, I swear I explained everything clearly."
She lowered her head, her voice shaking.

"The moment I finished stating our terms, that human sneered. He cursed us sirenfolk as shameless and arrogant, saying we were unworthy and incapable, yet somehow dared to imitate the shadowkin and try to subdue him..."
"My lord, there were many even harsher words. I truly cannot bring myself to repeat them."
She raised her head, tears glimmering in her eyes.
"That human cursed me for a long time. He insulted the sirenfolk from top to bottom. Please, my lord, seek justice for me and restore the honor of the sirenfolk!"
"Bastard!"
The sirenfolk administrator smashed the coral pillar beside him with a single palm, laughing from sheer fury.
"He refuses the toast only to drink the penalty wine! It seems we sirenfolk have been too gentle these past years, so gentle that even an ant like him thinks we can no longer hold a blade..."
"Pass down my order. Deploy the entire Rainbow Coral Legion and crush those humans completely!"
"Especially that one called Faustus—I want him to die without a burial place!"
Boom—!
Space seemed to be violently twisted by an invisible giant hand.
Ripples spread out from the void, like the surface of a lake struck by a massive stone, layer upon layer expanding in every direction.
Whoosh—!
A Starfall Isle burst out from the distorted space. Dense demonic aura surged and billowed like black smoke, blotting out the sky.
Almost at the same moment, the space on the other side was torn open as well, and the sirenfolk’s Starfall Isle emerged almost simultaneously.
Two colossal entities hovered in the void, radiating a suffocating pressure.
The scene of the two races dispatching their legions was clearly witnessed by the informants of every major faction.
"Jack, did you see that?"
"That little human really has some skill."
A Divine-grade powerhouse from the Council of Races sat aboard a starship, tapping his fingers lightly against the armrest as he looked with great interest at the two distant Starfall Isles.
"To be able to draw both the sirenfolk and shadowkin legions over at the same time—he’s not simple."
Jack raised an eyebrow. His gaze swept over the fleets of the two races with visible dislike, his tone indifferent.
"In the Azure Feather Galaxy, our Council of Races is the strongest. We occupy ninety percent of the territory. The scraps that remain are divided among the Godkin, shadowkin, and sirenfolk."
"There are also some empty realms whose coordinates cannot be found!"
He paused, a trace of disgust appearing on his face.
"For all these years, those three races have taken turns fighting us for territory. The battles never end. Now I feel sick the moment I see their banners."
"Hey, what’s the rush? There are still plenty of days ahead. Fight long enough, and you’ll get used to it."
The Council of Races powerhouse smiled, then suddenly asked with curiosity,
"Speaking of which, why hasn’t our Council of Races sent an envoy to contact that human?"
"The higher-ups have arrangements."
Jack lowered his voice slightly.
"Apparently, the humans of this plane have some connection to the humans of the Chaos Universe."
"Chaos Humans?"
The powerhouse’s eyes lit up.
"You mean the Chaos Humans who rank second among the human forces in the Endless Starfield?"
"Who else?"
Jack glanced at him.
"After we obtained the public coordinates, the higher-ups discovered this connection."
"Right now, they’re communicating with the Chaos Humans. There should be results very soon."
"Now that is interesting."
A smile appeared at the corner of the powerhouse’s mouth as he leaned back in his chair.
"Looks like no one will be able to eat this piece of meat."
"The strength of the Chaos Humans is right there for all to see. Which faction in the Azure Feather Galaxy would dare act recklessly?"
"That depends on whether this group of humans can hold out until then."
Jack spoke calmly, his gaze cast into the distance, as though watching a play that was about to begin.
"Let’s watch."
The powerhouse nodded.
"These two races are merely the vanguard. When the time comes, those Starfarers will definitely rush in with red eyes too. What worries me most is—those Astral Corsairs."
"Those fools."
Jack sneered.
"The Astral Corsairs have no scruples."
His tone became grave.
"If they decide this bone is not worth gnawing on, they may simply use High Divine-grade Strength from outside the realm to blast the entire world apart. That would be troublesome!"
"For a High Divine-grade being, destroying a small world is no different from crushing an egg."
"They really are capable of doing something like that."
The powerhouse nodded in agreement.
At the same time, more than a hundred Starfarer tribes were suppressing their urge to act, crouching in the shadows like a pack of starving wolves licking their claws.
"The demon and monster races have made the first move. That saves us the effort of testing the waters."
"Let them try out the combat strength of this world’s humans first. No rush. Let’s watch."
"Once both sides are badly wounded, we’ll move in and pick up the ready-made gains."
Seven or eight pirate crews had also taken position. They hid within the shadows of the void like sharks lurking in deep water.
"The demon and monster races have begun. Hopefully they don’t shatter the plane."
"Don’t panic, don’t panic. Let’s watch first. In any case, we won’t lose anything."
"If we don’t strike, so be it. But once we do, we must tear off a piece of meat!"
Earth.
Daniel and Camille sensed the two majestic energy fluctuations beyond the realm at the same time.
Those fluctuations were far too powerful. Even from within the plane, it felt as though someone were beating a war drum in the heavens, making people’s hearts tremble with unease.
"They’re powerful elites."
Camille licked her lips, her eyes shining.
"Then powerful enemies are exactly who we fight."
Daniel’s puppet clone took a deep breath. The aura around him slowly spread out like a bow drawn to its limit.
"In this battle, we’ll make sure none of them return alive."
Buzz, buzz—!
The longsword in Camille’s hand began to tremble. The blade let out a low hum, as though responding to its master’s battle intent.
"Old friend, you can’t hold back anymore either?"
Camille lowered her head and looked at the sword in her hand. Then she grinned and laughed loudly, her voice filled with heroic spirit.
"Come—follow me, and let us taste the enemy’s blood!"
The aura outside the realm grew stronger and stronger.
One of the presences was especially distinct—so distinct that even the legendary-grade players on Earth could clearly feel that heavy pressure.
"The enemies from the non-human races are here?"
"They’re here! Let me see which blind fools have come to attack us!"
"Hiss... this pressure is way too terrifying!"
"Guild Leader Faustus, you can do it! The guild leader is forever invincible!"
"Lord Faustus... we’re counting on you."
Boom—!
Rumble—!
The world barrier was struck repeatedly and instantly cracked open.
Two Starfall Isles descended at the same time, one on the left and one on the right, in two different directions.
The baleful aura on the islands surged into the sky. The radiance of Holy Relics and Divine Domains intertwined and flashed, like two burning stars falling into the mortal world.
At this moment, the demon and monster races drew the attention of all.
"Master, I’ll go test them first!"
Camille’s expression was filled with excitement. She transformed into a stream of light and charged straight toward the shadowkin Starfall Isle.
Daniel’s figure also vanished in an instant. When he appeared again, he was already near the sirenfolk Starfall Isle.

chapters.title: Chapter 244 -244-Blood Dyes the Star River, A Terrifying Swordsman
paragraphs: Shadowkin Starfall Isle.
When the shadowkin powerhouses saw a streak of light tearing through the void toward them, they immediately went on guard.
"Blood River Formation—rise!"
Rumble—!

Thousands upon thousands of shadowkin warriors ignited their Immortal Singularities at the same time. Black flames linked together into a sea of fire. Divine Domains unfolded like a canopy across the heavens, and Holy Relics loomed like mountains.
Swish—!
The light revealed Camille’s figure.
One man.
One sword.
"Kill him!"

At the shadowkin powerhouse’s command, Holy Relics and Divine Domains erupted at the same time. Overwhelming Strength came crashing down, suppressing everything beneath it. Space shattered under the terrible pressure, revealing pitch-black spatial rifts.
If an ordinary demi-sage were faced with such might, they would likely have been scared out of their wits, their soul scattered on the spot.
Clang—!
Heavenlight was drawn from its sheath.
A clear sword cry rang through the sky.
"Blood dyes the star river..."
A flush of red rose over Camille’s face. His sword radiance transformed into a towering pillar of light and collided fiercely with the shadowkin Divine Domains and Holy Relics.
Rumble, rumble—!
The sword light split open the Divine Domains and sent the Holy Relics flying.
Wherever the blade passed, it was like a knife cutting through tofu. Layer after layer of the shadowkin formation’s defenses were easily torn apart.
With one sword strike, countless souls perished.
"Peak demi-sage rank!"
A shadowkin powerhouse cried out in shock. The horror on his face quickly twisted into hatred.
"That swordsman is too arrogant! Let’s attack together!"
He signaled desperately to several demi-sage colleagues beside him, his voice filled with killing intent.

Several shadowkin demi-sages attacked at once, each unleashing their own methods. Their Divine Domains overlapped, and Holy Relics flew out together, closing in from all directions to suppress Camille on the spot.
"Break!"
Light flowed over the sword in Camille’s hand. Countless sword beams exploded outward and gathered into a vast sea of swords.
The sea of swords surged like a ten-thousand-meter wave pouring down from the heavens, instantly swallowing those peak demi-sage rank shadowkin powerhouses.
"Ah—! What divine art is this..."
"What terrifying swordsmanship! Man and sword as one, sword and god as one—such astonishing talent!"
"How does he dare take the sword as his god... How is that possible..."
Within the sea of swords, screams rose one after another. The shadowkin demi-sage ranks wailed and fell amid the sword light.
They were all demi-sages. Some among them were even peak demi-sage rank powerhouses.
Yet the difference between one demi-sage and another could still be as vast as heaven and earth.
Several of them had joined forces, but they were all crushed by a single sword strike!
With that one sword, Camille had slain several powerhouses of the same rank.
"Come, you shadowkin trash—"
Camille threw his head back and roared, his voice shaking the land in all directions.
His figure transformed into a streak of light and charged straight into the heart of the shadowkin Starfall Isle.
"Damn it, that swordsman is here! Run!"
"No, he’s too fast... We don’t have time."
"It’s over... We’re finished..."
Sword light erupted inside the Starfall Isle, then vanished, then erupted again.
Terrifying sword radiance ravaged the island, tearing the sturdy star isle into pieces until it was shattered and scattered everywhere.
Countless corpses fell from the sky like raindrops, smashing into the ground and sending up clouds of dust.
Swish—!
Camille sheathed his sword and flew out from the shattered star isle, hovering in the void.
He was drenched in blood from head to toe, yet not a single wound marked his body.
His cold gaze swept across the horizon, as if it could pierce through the world barrier and stab straight into the watching eyes beyond the realm.
"Heh—shadowkin. So that’s all you amount to."
"That swordsman... is far from simple."
The Divine-grade powerhouse from the Council of Races glanced at Jack beside him, his tone carrying a hint of admiration.
"His Divine Domain seems somewhat unusual."
Jack raised an eyebrow, a trace of pity appearing in his eyes.
"When his Divine Domain evolved toward the sage rank, he fused himself with his sword. He went astray."
"There is no fixed path to Divine-grade."
The Council of Races powerhouse did not seem to care.
"What nonsense about proper paths and crooked paths? Those are just rules invented by you academy types."
"You don’t understand what I mean."
Jack sneered.
"There is no fixed path to Divine-grade—that part is correct."

"But that swordsman’s mistake is that he had already gone off course while still at the Divine Domain stage. He hasn’t even reached Divine-grade yet, but his road has already forked in the wrong direction."
"Oh? I don’t think that’s necessarily true."
"Then let’s wait and see. Of course, that assumes he survives..."
"With that swordsman there, no matter how many powerhouses go in, they’ll just be throwing their lives away."
Among the Starfarer camp, someone growled bitterly.
"If we pay a certain price, there will always be a way to kill him..."
Someone beside him retorted unconvinced.
"And what if we pay a terrible price, only to make wedding clothes for someone else in the end?"
That powerhouse sneered, his gaze drifting toward the pirates.
"For example—those hyenas who specialize in picking up scraps?"
"Sigh..."
The Starfarers all sighed at once.
This beautiful blue planet truly was a rose covered in thorns.
"The native residents of this world are actually this strong!"
A powerhouse from the Whitebone Pirates watched the scene of the shadowkin legion’s destruction, his scalp going numb.
So many shadowkin powerhouses had been cut down by a single sword from that man. That also meant that even if they personally took the field, they would not gain the slightest advantage.
"Steady. Stay steady."
A powerhouse from the Blackwater Pirates waved his hands repeatedly, his voice extremely low.
"Let’s see what happens on the sirenfolk side."
The gazes of all the pirates turned in unison toward the other Starfall Isle.
Sirenfolk Starfall Isle.
The atmosphere here was so strange that it nearly made it impossible to breathe.
The sirenfolk powerhouses wore peculiar expressions as they stared fixedly at the figure slowly walking toward the Starfall Isle.
The newcomer was alone, yet he treated the countless sirenfolk powerhouses as if they were nothing. He walked as casually as if he were strolling through his own back garden.
Calm, unhurried, and completely at ease.
"Face the enemy—!"
A sirenfolk powerhouse shouted sharply.
Boom—!
The sirenfolk warriors instantly entered battle mode. Divine Domains spread open, Holy Relics bloomed with light, and terrifying energy surged wildly through the grand formation.
Daniel did not stop walking.
His face remained as calm as a still lake as he continued forward.
The sirenfolk powerhouse felt an unprecedented sense of humiliation.
He had lived for so many years, yet he had never seen a creature this arrogant.
"Butcher him—!"
He could no longer hold back and let out a furious roar.
The legion warriors behind him cast their Divine Domains over Daniel. Holy Relics came crashing down with earth-shattering Strength.
"Let’s see you keep acting arrogant. Die!"
The sirenfolk powerhouse cursed viciously in his heart.
However, Daniel walked out from within the Divine Domains, completely unharmed!
Not even the corner of his clothes was wrinkled.
"This... How is this possible?"
The sirenfolk powerhouse felt as though he were dreaming.
The dual crushing force of Divine Domains and Holy Relics had not even scratched this person’s skin?
He was clearly only legendary-grade!
"Con... Continue attacking!"
The sirenfolk powerhouse’s voice had already begun to tremble.
Beneath the Divine Domains, the threads of causality around Daniel kept pulsing.
It was not only the Divine Domains. Even the Holy Relics could not touch him.
He seemed to have become an insulator against all harm. Every attack missed by an imperceptible hair’s breadth, yet none of them could ever truly land on him.
At that moment, the thought passing through Daniel’s mind was...
Instantly killing them would indeed let people know that I’m strong.
But they wouldn’t know exactly how strong I am.
To intimidate these starving wolves, I have to make them fear me down to their bones.
Should I be a little more arrogant?
What he did not know was that, within a deeper layer of space, a pair of eyes was staring fixedly at him, the pupils suddenly contracting.
"Fate... Law of Causality..."
Yexis’s heart pounded wildly.
His mission target was far more terrifying than he had imagined!
That was the power of law.
Law!
An existence that stood above all elemental Strength!
"Wait!"
"...Has he already discovered me?"

sentences.text: Shadowkin Starfall Isle.
When the shadowkin powerhouses saw a streak of light tearing through the void toward them, they immediately went on guard.
"Blood River Formation—rise!"
Rumble—!
Thousands upon thousands of shadowkin warriors ignited their Immortal Singularities at the same time.
Black flames linked together into a sea of fire.
Divine Domains unfolded like a canopy across the heavens, and Holy Relics loomed like mountains.
Swish—!
The light revealed Camille’s figure.
One man.
One sword.
"Kill him!"
At the shadowkin powerhouse’s command, Holy Relics and Divine Domains erupted at the same time.
Overwhelming Strength came crashing down, suppressing everything beneath it.
Space shattered under the terrible pressure, revealing pitch-black spatial rifts.
If an ordinary demi-sage were faced with such might, they would likely have been scared out of their wits, their soul scattered on the spot.
Clang—!
Heavenlight was drawn from its sheath.
A clear sword cry rang through the sky.
"Blood dyes the star river..."
A flush of red rose over Camille’s face.
His sword radiance transformed into a towering pillar of light and collided fiercely with the shadowkin Divine Domains and Holy Relics.
Rumble, rumble—!
The sword light split open the Divine Domains and sent the Holy Relics flying.
Wherever the blade passed, it was like a knife cutting through tofu.
Layer after layer of the shadowkin formation’s defenses were easily torn apart.
With one sword strike, countless souls perished.
"Peak demi-sage rank!"
A shadowkin powerhouse cried out in shock.
The horror on his face quickly twisted into hatred.
"That swordsman is too arrogant!
Let’s attack together!"
He signaled desperately to several demi-sage colleagues beside him, his voice filled with killing intent.
Several shadowkin demi-sages attacked at once, each unleashing their own methods.
Their Divine Domains overlapped, and Holy Relics flew out together, closing in from all directions to suppress Camille on the spot.
"Break!"
Light flowed over the sword in Camille’s hand.
Countless sword beams exploded outward and gathered into a vast sea of swords.
The sea of swords surged like a ten-thousand-meter wave pouring down from the heavens, instantly swallowing those peak demi-sage rank shadowkin powerhouses.
"Ah—!
What divine art is this..."
"What terrifying swordsmanship!
Man and sword as one, sword and god as one—such astonishing talent!"
"How does he dare take the sword as his god...
How is that possible..."
Within the sea of swords, screams rose one after another.
The shadowkin demi-sage ranks wailed and fell amid the sword light.
They were all demi-sages.
Some among them were even peak demi-sage rank powerhouses.
Yet the difference between one demi-sage and another could still be as vast as heaven and earth.
Several of them had joined forces, but they were all crushed by a single sword strike!
With that one sword, Camille had slain several powerhouses of the same rank.
"Come, you shadowkin trash—"
Camille threw his head back and roared, his voice shaking the land in all directions.
His figure transformed into a streak of light and charged straight into the heart of the shadowkin Starfall Isle.
"Damn it, that swordsman is here!
Run!"
"No, he’s too fast...
We don’t have time."
"It’s over...
We’re finished..."
Sword light erupted inside the Starfall Isle, then vanished, then erupted again.
Terrifying sword radiance ravaged the island, tearing the sturdy star isle into pieces until it was shattered and scattered everywhere.
Countless corpses fell from the sky like raindrops, smashing into the ground and sending up clouds of dust.
Swish—!
Camille sheathed his sword and flew out from the shattered star isle, hovering in the void.
He was drenched in blood from head to toe, yet not a single wound marked his body.
His cold gaze swept across the horizon, as if it could pierce through the world barrier and stab straight into the watching eyes beyond the realm.
"Heh—shadowkin.
So that’s all you amount to."
"That swordsman... is far from simple."
The Divine-grade powerhouse from the Council of Races glanced at Jack beside him, his tone carrying a hint of admiration.
"His Divine Domain seems somewhat unusual."
Jack raised an eyebrow, a trace of pity appearing in his eyes.
"When his Divine Domain evolved toward the sage rank, he fused himself with his sword.
He went astray."
"There is no fixed path to Divine-grade."
The Council of Races powerhouse did not seem to care.
"What nonsense about proper paths and crooked paths?
Those are just rules invented by you academy types."
"You don’t understand what I mean."
Jack sneered.
"There is no fixed path to Divine-grade—that part is correct."
"But that swordsman’s mistake is that he had already gone off course while still at the Divine Domain stage.
He hasn’t even reached Divine-grade yet, but his road has already forked in the wrong direction."
"Oh?
I don’t think that’s necessarily true."
"Then let’s wait and see.
Of course, that assumes he survives..."
"With that swordsman there, no matter how many powerhouses go in, they’ll just be throwing their lives away."
Among the Starfarer camp, someone growled bitterly.
"If we pay a certain price, there will always be a way to kill him..."
Someone beside him retorted unconvinced.
"And what if we pay a terrible price, only to make wedding clothes for someone else in the end?"
That powerhouse sneered, his gaze drifting toward the pirates.
"For example—those hyenas who specialize in picking up scraps?"
"Sigh..."
The Starfarers all sighed at once.
This beautiful blue planet truly was a rose covered in thorns.
"The native residents of this world are actually this strong!"
A powerhouse from the Whitebone Pirates watched the scene of the shadowkin legion’s destruction, his scalp going numb.
So many shadowkin powerhouses had been cut down by a single sword from that man.
That also meant that even if they personally took the field, they would not gain the slightest advantage.
"Steady.
Stay steady."
A powerhouse from the Blackwater Pirates waved his hands repeatedly, his voice extremely low.
"Let’s see what happens on the sirenfolk side."
The gazes of all the pirates turned in unison toward the other Starfall Isle.
Sirenfolk Starfall Isle.
The atmosphere here was so strange that it nearly made it impossible to breathe.
The sirenfolk powerhouses wore peculiar expressions as they stared fixedly at the figure slowly walking toward the Starfall Isle.
The newcomer was alone, yet he treated the countless sirenfolk powerhouses as if they were nothing.
He walked as casually as if he were strolling through his own back garden.
Calm, unhurried, and completely at ease.
"Face the enemy—!"
A sirenfolk powerhouse shouted sharply.
Boom—!
The sirenfolk warriors instantly entered battle mode.
Divine Domains spread open, Holy Relics bloomed with light, and terrifying energy surged wildly through the grand formation.
Daniel did not stop walking.
His face remained as calm as a still lake as he continued forward.
The sirenfolk powerhouse felt an unprecedented sense of humiliation.
He had lived for so many years, yet he had never seen a creature this arrogant.
"Butcher him—!"
He could no longer hold back and let out a furious roar.
The legion warriors behind him cast their Divine Domains over Daniel.
Holy Relics came crashing down with earth-shattering Strength.
"Let’s see you keep acting arrogant.
Die!"
The sirenfolk powerhouse cursed viciously in his heart.
However, Daniel walked out from within the Divine Domains, completely unharmed!
Not even the corner of his clothes was wrinkled.
"This...
How is this possible?"
The sirenfolk powerhouse felt as though he were dreaming.
The dual crushing force of Divine Domains and Holy Relics had not even scratched this person’s skin?
He was clearly only legendary-grade!
"Con...
Continue attacking!"
The sirenfolk powerhouse’s voice had already begun to tremble.
Beneath the Divine Domains, the threads of causality around Daniel kept pulsing.
It was not only the Divine Domains.
Even the Holy Relics could not touch him.
He seemed to have become an insulator against all harm.
Every attack missed by an imperceptible hair’s breadth, yet none of them could ever truly land on him.
At that moment, the thought passing through Daniel’s mind was...
Instantly killing them would indeed let people know that I’m strong.
But they wouldn’t know exactly how strong I am.
To intimidate these starving wolves, I have to make them fear me down to their bones.
Should I be a little more arrogant?
What he did not know was that, within a deeper layer of space, a pair of eyes was staring fixedly at him, the pupils suddenly contracting.
"Fate...
Law of Causality..."
Yexis’s heart pounded wildly.
His mission target was far more terrifying than he had imagined!
That was the power of law.
Law!
An existence that stood above all elemental Strength!
"Wait!"
"...Has he already discovered me?"

chapters.title: Chapter 245 -245-Luna_Fox Assassin—Certain Death?
paragraphs: Yexis’s heart went half cold.
Powerhouses who mastered the Law of Causality were the hardest to assassinate. The moment you so much as formed a thought, they could follow the threads of causality and sense your existence.
In direct combat, they could even alter the result.
Even more terrifying existences could change the cause itself, making their opponent die without a complete corpse before they had even attacked.
As for those top-tier Oracle-grade beings... they could even follow the causal threads and erase their target directly from the river of time!
"This mission... was taken too hastily."
Yexis gritted his teeth. For a moment, he actually felt somewhat lost.
Facing such an opponent, he could not think of any way to win!
He continued observing Daniel.
At this moment, Daniel had already stepped onto the sirenfolk Starfall Isle.
What!
The sirenfolk powerhouses were collectively petrified.
"He actually broke in?"
The jaws of the sirenfolk warriors nearly dropped to the ground.
How were they supposed to fight this battle?
If they truly made a move, their own base would be destroyed first.
"I’m here to send you on your way."
Daniel swept a cold glance over the sirenfolk warriors before him. His voice was not loud, yet it pierced into every warrior’s ears like an icicle.
Buzz, buzz—!
A mass of dazzling light surfaced from his body, growing brighter and brighter, more and more blazing, like a scorching sun rising from the surface of the sea.
Epic-grade forbidden spell—Arrow of Judgment!
The light was blinding, scorching like the midday sun.
That vast energy, almost insane in its intensity, directly tore apart the spatial barrier.
The surrounding space was like glass struck by a heavy hammer. Cracks spread like a spiderweb, then exploded with a deafening blast.
The entire Starfall Isle was sliced into countless fragments.
Space collapsed. The weaker warriors were sucked into the turbulent currents of the chaotic void and instantly turned to ash.
Those who were slightly stronger were also torn apart by spatial rifts, their divine sources shredded as they died on the spot.
Even demi-sages had their Divine Domains destroyed and their bodies obliterated amid the endless spatial ruptures.
Countless damage numbers jumped wildly.
"-3 billion!"
"-3 billion!"
"-3 billion!"
Until not a single living soul remained.
System notifications surged in like a tsunami.
[Ding! Obtained Primal Spirit ×10,000...]
[Ding! Obtained Primal Spirit ×10,000...]
[Ding! Obtained Primal Spirit ×10,000...]
The sirenfolk Starfall Isle had been annihilated!
"Hiss... Too strong!"
"This Strength... How terrifying!"
Yexis could not stop trembling. Even he himself could no longer tell whether it was excitement or fear.
In short, he had been deeply stimulated.
Although he had mastered a low-grade spatial law, that man’s Strength was enough to pierce through multiple layers of space and pose a fatal threat to him.
"In that case, I’m afraid I only have one chance left."
Yexis took a deep breath and forcefully suppressed the shock in his heart.
"The power of my Divine Domain is enough to rival an ordinary sage rank, while my opponent has not yet condensed his own Divine Domain. From that perspective, I still have a sliver of hope!"
"I cannot miss this chance—!"
His figure flashed, and he swiftly slipped into the deeper layers of space near Daniel.
Spatial law was known for concealment. He moved through the gaps of space, silent and traceless.
In the blink of an eye, he had already drawn close.
Boom—!
Yexis suddenly charged out of space, his Divine Domain unfolding with a thunderous roar.
Bang!
Space could not withstand that terrifying pressure. It shattered instantly like crushed crystal.
This scene abruptly appeared before the eyes of all the powerhouses beyond the realm, drawing a wave of shocked cries.
"It’s a Luna_Fox assassin!"
"Hiss—who spent such a huge price to hire someone from Luna_Fox?"
"That human powerhouse... is probably finished."
Yexis’s Divine Domain enveloped Daniel completely.
Crushing Strength descended like mountains and seas overturning.
Hmph!
Daniel sensed that terrifying force, far beyond his understanding, locking onto him. Yet a cold sneer appeared at the corner of his mouth.
Crusader’s Physique, convert MP into HP!
[Ding: Conversion successful. Current HP: 956.42 trillion!]
Boom!
Rumble, rumble!
Frenzied attacks powerful enough to blast a world into fragments crashed onto Daniel’s body wave after wave.
Yet he did not move an inch.
He was completely unharmed.
"What kind of joke is this—!"
Yexis was horrified to the extreme. He swung the flail in his hand with all his strength, unleashing his strongest strike.
Tens of millions of staff shadows poured down in an instant. Because the speed was too fast, the naked eye could only see a single strike.
That one strike was also tens of millions of strikes. With secret arts reinforcing it, it was enough to kill even a low Divine-grade powerhouse.
And Daniel was merely legendary-grade.
Boom!
"This is impossible!"
Yexis was shocked to discover that his weapon could not hit Daniel at all.
Every strike missed by just the tiniest bit.
He reacted instantly.
That was the power of law.
It seemed as though the attack had missed by only a hair’s breadth, but in reality, it was separated by ten thousand miles.
"Fate Law of Causality!"
Yexis hated him so much that his teeth itched.
Encountering a powerhouse who knew the Fate Law of Causality was utterly disgusting!
This assignment was practically a trap!
He had to leave immediately.
His figure faded, escaping into deeper space as he tried to flee.
"You think... you can leave?"
Daniel released the attribute conversion, the corner of his mouth curving into an icy arc.
Swish—!
"This sword—can split the void!"
A sword light exploded out of nowhere, cutting through layer after layer of space like a heavy streak of ink drawn across white paper.
Wherever it passed, space was split into two halves.
Clang!
"It’s that swordsman..."
Yexis was forced out of space and swung his flail to block.
He had already been locked onto by a cold gaze.
Camille’s eyes were frosty, his killing intent biting.
"Before you made your move, you should have considered the price!"
Daniel stepped forward and instantly appeared beside Yexis.
His fist was wrapped in destructive power where ice and fire intertwined. The surrounding space faintly trembled, letting out groans as though it could no longer bear the burden.
If he did not dodge, he would die!
Yexis’s mind shook violently. He wanted to escape into space, only to discover that the space around him had fallen into dead silence.
Most of his Strength had somehow vanished, and his legs felt as though they had been filled with lead!
Epic-grade forbidden spell—Veil of Eternal Night!
Hunting Domain!
Boom—!
Daniel’s fist smashed down with a thunderous crash.
The outcome held no suspense.
Bang!
Yexis was blasted apart by a single punch, turning into dust that filled the sky.
Yexis, the top-tier assassin of the Luna_Fox organization, had fallen!

chapters.title: Chapter 246 -246-The One Who Bears the Burden for His Race
paragraphs: Daniel listened to the system notifications ringing beside his ears and immediately took out the two secret arts to examine them.
[Endless Divine Power (Divine-grade)]
Restriction: supreme-grade

Description: A secret art created by an Oracle-grade member of the Luna_Fox organization. It can inflict damage far beyond the user’s current realm. After being enhanced, the strength of this secret art has increased tremendously.
With the host’s current strength, it can heavily injure Divine-grade powerhouses.
Daniel’s eyes lit up.
A secret art capable of heavily injuring Divine-grade powerhouses... This was simply a treasure!
He remembered back when he was in the God Realm. His damage had been severely weakened when it landed on Divine-grade powerhouses, almost like level suppression in a game.
If he learned this secret art, would he be able to directly kill Divine-grade beings?
A bold thought flashed through his mind.
"Unfortunately, it has a threshold. I have to step into supreme-grade before I can study it."
He smiled.
At present, he was only eighty levels away from supreme-grade. It would not be long.
He put the secret art away into his personal space.
[Holy Condensation (Divine-grade)]
Restriction: supreme-grade

Description: A secret art created by an Oracle-grade member of Luna_Fox. It allows a supreme-grade powerhouse’s Divine Domain to rival the sage rank of a low Divine-grade powerhouse. After being enhanced, the strength of this secret art has increased tremendously.
Daniel’s heart stirred slightly.
There was actually such a heaven-defying secret art in this world, one that could allow a Divine Domain to rival sage rank?

He remembered how that assassin had used his Divine Domain to suppress him the moment he appeared. At the time, Daniel had found it strange. Why did it feel like the man’s Divine Domain was almost comparable to sage rank?
So it had been the effect of this secret art!
"If I can master this secret art, I won’t have to worry about the sage rank of Divine-grade enemies in the future."
He took a deep breath, his eyes flashing with sharp light.
"With my own Strength, I should be able to contend with a sage."
Without a doubt, both of these secret arts were heaven-defying existences.
It could be said that the greatest gains from this battle were precisely these two secret arts.
"This Endless Starfield truly contains everything imaginable. Nothing is too strange to exist here."
Daniel put the secret arts away, his heart filled with anticipation for his promotion to supreme-grade.
Camille’s sword strike had swept away the shadowkin legion like a storm.
Daniel, meanwhile, had crushed the sirenfolk army into dust with casual ease.
The players watching from afar felt indescribable shock surging in their hearts.
They were awed by Camille’s wild and unrestrained swordsmanship, and toward Daniel, they developed an almost devout faith.
"No matter what desperate situation fate throws at us, Guild Leader Faustus has never disappointed us."
An old player spoke in a low voice, his tone firm.

"That’s right. He is like a towering tree, blocking all the storms for us. It is true that he has absorbed most of the sunlight and rain from the sky, but it is also precisely because of the order he personally established that we have been able to grow so vigorously and walk far ahead of everyone else."
"As expected of the hero I admire most. He is unstoppable. The scene before us is the best proof—he made everyone withdraw from the battlefield and shouldered the survival of the entire world alone."
"The guild leader is moving forward while carrying the fate of the entire race on his back. He is also moving forward while bearing the full weight of this era."
"I really don’t know when we’ll finally grow strong enough to fight shoulder to shoulder with him..."
"That’s exactly what I mean... I’ve truly had enough of my own weakness and incompetence."
"I swear in the name of the gods, I never want to just stand far away again and watch helplessly as the guild leader charges toward death alone."
Another young warrior clenched his fists. His gaze was fixed on Camille’s figure, and his voice was hoarse.
"Did you see that swordsman? That sword of his was practically like splitting open an entire river of stars. When will we ever possess Strength like that?"
The mage beside him shook his head and gave a bitter smile.
"Stop dreaming for now. Just being able to stand firmly beside the guild leader already requires us to give everything we have."
"But I don’t want to be the one protected forever."
The warrior spoke in a low voice.
"One day, I will stand beside the guild leader too, instead of merely looking up at his back."
No one spoke again.
Beyond the realm, the gazes of the Divine-grade powerhouses had also remained fixed on those two figures.
"I originally thought that swordsman was already a once-in-an-era genius. I never imagined that this human powerhouse would be even more unfathomable."
"That move he used to annihilate the sirenfolk was so effortless that it almost looked ostentatious, almost arrogant."
The Divine-grade powerhouse from the Council of Races sighed softly, his tone filled with shock.
Jack smiled faintly.
"He deliberately did that for us to see."

"With his true strength, destroying the sirenfolk is no harder than crushing a few insects. He is telling every faction lying in wait beyond the realm—whoever dares to make a move had better first weigh whether they have enough ability."
"With that swordsman in this world, and this human powerhouse holding the line as well..."
The Council of Races powerhouse shook his head.
"The other factions probably won’t have much of a chance."
"What I fear is that some factions will use unscrupulous methods to force them to act."
Jack’s gaze swept quietly toward the directions where the Starfarers and pirates were hiding.
"This battle... simply can’t be fought."
A Divine-grade powerhouse among the Astral Corsairs gave a bitter smile, his voice full of helplessness.
"Among our subordinates, we cannot pick out a single demi-sage capable of contending with either of those two."
The pirates calculated secretly and discovered that whether it was that swordsman or the human leader, both of them stood more than one level above the strongest demi-sage in their own camp.
"At present, there is only one method—we use some means to force them out of that small world."
"Otherwise, below Divine-grade, they are invincible!"
Extreme thoughts began turning in the pirates’ minds.
"Let’s first see what the Starfarers do. They’re more anxious than we are."
"As long as Divine-grade doesn’t appear, they’re practically invincible."
The Starfarers were already starting to think of retreating.
"Then force them out! Once they come into this open starry sky, our Divine-grade powerhouses will only need one hand to crush them into powder!"
Ruthless light flashed in the Starfarers’ eyes.
"But methods like that... aren’t those what those pirates usually use?"

"What time do you think this is? How many years have we wandered through this Endless Starfield? We don’t have a single inch of land beneath our feet that belongs to us. Sooner or later, we’ll die in this cold void."
"Exactly. This small world that voluntarily made its coordinates public is our only path to survival!"
"How about... we first send someone to negotiate with them?"
"Negotiate? If negotiations could solve the problem, why would the sirenfolk and shadowkin have mobilized their armies and met them with blades?"

"Then there’s no more need to talk. Act immediately! Unite those one hundred-plus Starfarer races and work together to set up that Starfall Arcane Array. Force the two powerhouses hiding in that world to come out."
One powerhouse drew the long saber at his waist, a trace of madness in his eyes.
"If they refuse to come out—then we will erase this planet from the Star Chart completely!"

[Endless Divine Power (Divine-grade)]
Restriction: supreme-grade
Description: A secret art created by an Oracle-grade member of the Luna_Fox organization.
It can inflict damage far beyond the user’s current realm.
After being enhanced, the strength of this secret art has increased tremendously.
With the host’s current strength, it can heavily injure Divine-grade powerhouses.
Daniel’s eyes lit up.
A secret art capable of heavily injuring Divine-grade powerhouses...
This was simply a treasure!
He remembered back when he was in the God Realm.
His damage had been severely weakened when it landed on Divine-grade powerhouses, almost like level suppression in a game.
If he learned this secret art, would he be able to directly kill Divine-grade beings?
A bold thought flashed through his mind.
"Unfortunately, it has a threshold.
I have to step into supreme-grade before I can study it."
He smiled.
At present, he was only eighty levels away from supreme-grade.
It would not be long.
He put the secret art away into his personal space.
[Holy Condensation (Divine-grade)]

It allows a supreme-grade powerhouse’s Divine Domain to rival the sage rank of a low Divine-grade powerhouse.
After being enhanced, the strength of this secret art has increased tremendously.
Daniel’s heart stirred slightly.
There was actually such a heaven-defying secret art in this world, one that could allow a Divine Domain to rival sage rank?
He remembered how that assassin had used his Divine Domain to suppress him the moment he appeared.
At the time, Daniel had found it strange.

So it had been the effect of this secret art!

It could be said that the greatest gains from this battle were precisely these two secret arts.
"This Endless Starfield truly contains everything imaginable.

chapters.title: Chapter 247 -247-Using All of Earth as the Stake
paragraphs: The Starfarers swiftly united.

More than a hundred races and countless powerhouses ignited their Immortal Singularities. Under the guidance of several Divine-grade powerhouses, their energy gathered into a raging torrent, soon erupting with a terrifying aura that far surpassed that of an ordinary Divine-grade.
This abnormal movement startled every faction closely watching this place.
"These lunatics really are going all in."
The pirates cursed with laughter, yet their eyes flashed with excitement.
"That’s fine. Once they’re done fighting, we’ll see if there are any bargains to pick up."
"These hypocritical desperadoes really dare to do anything for the sake of a world."
The pirates folded their arms and watched coldly from the side.
"The two powerhouses inside that world have no choice but to show themselves now."
Jack smiled.
"If they hide inside the world, they can only watch helplessly as the world is destroyed. If they come out, they’ll have to face the suppression of Divine-grade powerhouses."
"That’s right... This choice is far too difficult."
The Council of Races powerhouse shook his head and sighed.
"This is the cruelty of the Endless Starfield. Strength is everything."
Swish—!
Daniel’s brows suddenly furrowed.
"The threads of causality..."
The threads of causality had suddenly surfaced of their own accord without warning.
This was the second time!
The last time had also been when he was facing an enormous crisis.
"What kind of danger is approaching?"
He stared at those pulsing threads of causality and opened each highlighted thread one by one.
Buzz—!
His consciousness sank into them...
Whoosh—!
When he withdrew from the threads of causality, his face was as dark as the sky before a storm.
"Master, what happened?"
Seeing his expression change so suddenly, Camille quickly asked.
"This is no small matter."
Killing intent surged in Daniel’s eyes as he slowly said,
"Those Starfarers beyond the realm have set up a Starfall Arcane Array."
"They want to use this world as a hostage to force us out. If we go out, we’ll be suppressed by Divine-grade powerhouses. If we don’t, they’ll blast this world into fragments."
"What a ruthless, vicious scheme."
"Master... then we..."
Camille opened his mouth, but he did not know what to say.
Daniel barely hesitated.
At a moment of life and death, a choice had to be made immediately.
Recklessness might lead to death.
But hesitation would certainly lead to death!
"I’ll go out. You stay here and guard this place."
He clenched his fists tightly, his voice as heavy as iron.
"They dare threaten me? Then let’s see whose skull is harder!"
"Master... may you return victorious."
Camille did not try to stop him. There was not even the slightest surprise in his expression.
Once, he had made the same choice.
He had sacrificed himself and guarded his people alone for nearly ten thousand years.
His enemies had changed from the blades of other races to the long passage of time, then from time to the human heart, and finally from the human heart to his own people.
Camille had never regretted it.
If he were given another chance to choose, he would still walk the same path—even if the ending had already been doomed from the beginning.
Daniel was the same.
"That human leader who carried the greatsword on his back turned and returned to a battlefield of certain death for the sake of his race."
"The sages of Aetheria drew their blades across their own throats to win their people a place to live."
"In previous eras, countless human powerhouses threw themselves forward one after another to protect their people."
"I am merely... making the same choice."
Daniel raised his foot and stepped forward.
His figure instantly vanished from where he stood.
"Humans cannot remain ignorant beings who are merely sheltered. They must know who is shielding them from the wind and rain..."
Camille murmured softly, then suddenly waved his hand.
Swish, swish, swish—!
Countless sword lights flew from his hand and transformed into massive swords, hovering before every player.
The backs of the swords were as smooth as mirrors, reflecting the scene beyond the realm.
The players were startled at first. Then they saw the image clearly.
They saw that familiar figure—Daniel!
"That’s... Guild Leader Faustus! Why did he go out?"
"What’s going on? Has the guild leader already decided defense is beneath him and chosen to attack first?"
"No... why do I feel like the guild leader was forced out by something?"
"Yeah, even I can sense a suffocating, terrifying aura. That is definitely not Strength that belongs to this world."
"Don’t tell me... the guild leader went there to..."
"Shut up! Close that cursed mouth of yours!"
"Lord Faustus is invincible! Even if the end of the world descends and the God of Death swings his scythe himself, he won’t be able to take Faustus’s life!"
"Look! The guild leader is charging in!"
"Charge! My hero—let those petty villains see what a true god really is!"
Beyond the realm.
The moment Daniel’s figure appeared, countless pairs of eyes locked onto him all at once, like starving wolves catching the scent of blood.
"Once, I saw a very similar scene."
Jack calmly looked at that young figure, but his fingers trembled slightly in a way almost impossible to notice.
That tiny movement was seen by the Council of Races powerhouse beside him.
In Jack’s vision, Daniel’s figure gradually overlapped with a certain back from his memories.
Only, back then, that figure had faced Astral Corsairs.
At this moment, Daniel was facing Starfarers, pirates, and the entrenched factions from every side.
That year, that figure had already been at the peak of demi-sage rank.
Daniel, however, was only legendary-grade.
"Jack..."
The Council of Races powerhouse hesitated, wanting to speak but stopping himself.
He remembered very clearly the first time he had met Jack.
At that time, a pirate group had used the survival of an entire plane as leverage. Jack had gritted his teeth and walked out of the world barrier, preparing to go to a battle where death was certain.
Back then, Jack had still been at the peak of demi-sage rank.
Many years had passed. The demi-sage rank from back then was now a Divine-grade powerhouse, and that pirate group had been uprooted by his own hands.
But that feeling of being forced into a desperate corner, where even breathing felt painful, had probably already grown into his bones. It could never be carved out in this lifetime.
"He’s out! This fellow finally came out!"
The pirates grinned viciously, their eyes filled with excitement.
"Although only one came out, once this human leader dies, that sword wielder will have to crawl out sooner or later too."
They had seen far too many scenes like this and had never miscalculated before.
"Hurry up and die. Hurry up and die. Once both of them are dead, we can loot to our hearts’ content."
The pirates suppressed the hearts that were nearly leaping out of their throats, their mouths dry with anticipation.
"Only him?"
The Starfarer Divine-grade powerhouse frowned, then quickly relaxed.
"Then we’ll lure them out and kill them one by one. We’re not afraid of him coming out. We’re only afraid he’ll hide in his shell like a cowardly turtle."
The Divine-grade powerhouses of the other wandering factions cracked their knuckles, their eyes filled with eagerness.
"Hmph, legendary-grade? An ant-like thing."
One Divine-grade powerhouse suddenly erupted with an overwhelming aura. His sage rank unfolded with a thunderous roar, and he was about to smash Daniel into meat paste on the spot.
Daniel felt the terrifying Strength of the sage rank pressing toward him from every direction.
He did not hesitate at all.
He summoned ninety-nine clones at once, cast teleportation, and charged madly toward the area where the Starfarers were clustered together.
Rumble—!
The sage rank descended.
That Strength, powerful enough to crush everything, swallowed Daniel whole.
On Earth, countless players stared fixedly at everything through the images projected on the backs of the swords.
They could not feel that pressure, but just by watching, they knew how terrifying that sage rank was.
"Guild leader..."
The hearts of the guild players clenched into tight knots.
"Lord Faustus, nothing will happen to you!"
Some players were so nervous that they bit their lips bloody. Their fingernails dug into their palms, and they did not even notice when beads of blood seeped out.
"Daniel..."
A female player’s eyes had already turned red.
Suddenly, within the sage rank, Faustus’s figure shattered with a boom into a pile of motes of light!
That invincible guild leader...
Had died!

chapters.title: Chapter 248 -248-For Humanity, Ten Thousand Deaths Without Regret
paragraphs: "Guild Leader—!!!"
In that instant, the towering idol that stood high in the hearts of countless players collapsed with a thunderous crash.
Cries and roars exploded across Earth.
"Impossible..."
"How could Guild Leader die just like that?"
Tears blurred their vision.
Their mouths hung open, their faces still frozen in stunned disbelief.
Faustus was dead?
No...
How could he die?
If he died, what would happen to humanity?
"What kind of joke is this!"
Someone roared like a madman, his voice cracking completely.
"It’s an illusion! Right, we’re playing a game! This game is fake... Wuwu... Boss!!!"
He could barely speak coherently anymore.
But at that moment, Daniel’s figure appeared in the image once again.
The hearts of countless players, which had already burned into ash, seemed to be lit by a spark and came alive again.
"Look! The guild leader isn’t dead!"
"I knew it! Lord Faustus is a god of war! He’s our guardian deity! How could he possibly die?"
Someone wiped away tears while repeating those words over and over again.
"Guild Leader... you have to hold on!"
"What nonsense! Guild Leader will definitely kill them all!"
Beyond the realm.
Daniel did not stop for even a single step. He continued charging fiercely toward the Starfarer formation.
"Hm? He didn’t die? What’s going on?"
That Divine-grade powerhouse showed confusion on his face.
"This human... can revive?"
"Damn it! Are all of you just standing around watching the show? Attack together and kill him!"
A powerhouse shouted at the top of his lungs.
The moment his words fell, several Divine-grade powerhouses unfolded their sage ranks at the same time and joined forces against Daniel.
Daniel still charged forward.
The path ahead meant death the moment he stepped onto it, but only that path could give him a way to survive.
It was both a dead end and his only hope.
"This is humanity’s only chance..."
His figure was suppressed once again.
This time, all the Divine-grade powerhouses attacked together, crushing both his main body and his clones!
But before they could breathe a sigh of relief—
Swish—!
Daniel appeared again.
The instant he revived, he summoned his clones once more and continued charging forward with his head down.
"Come then... let’s die together, you bastards!"
Boom—!
He plunged headfirst into the clustered Starfarer ships.
"Walk toward death with me!"
Rumble—!
Daniel’s self-destruction was terrifyingly powerful. Even a large section of the starry sky collapsed from the blast.
Countless Starfarers were crushed into fragments by that destructive Strength.
But in the blink of an eye, Daniel’s figure revived and regenerated from another direction!
Sage rank crashed down again.
Daniel died.
Then exploded!
Boom, boom, boom—!
Every time Daniel revived, he self-destructed once.
The vast and mighty Starfarer formation suffered devastating casualties under his rounds of relentless self-destruction.
On Earth, the players could no longer speak.
They simply watched that incomparably stubborn figure charge into certain death again and again, be suppressed again and again, and be smashed to pieces again and again.
Then he revived and charged in once more.
"The guild leader... is using his own life to buy us a chance to survive!"
The joy of Daniel not dying had yet to fully spread before grief surged up from the depths of their hearts.
"Boss Faustus... the eternal god."
This time, no one held even the slightest dissatisfaction toward Daniel anymore.
Even the schemers lurking in the dark collectively stopped their plots after seeing this scene.
Those who carry firewood for the people must not be allowed to freeze to death in the snowstorm!
To put it bluntly, stabbing someone like that in the back was not something a human deserved to do!
In the image, Daniel self-destructed again.
Again and again.
Madly.
Endlessly.
In the image, flames connected into a sea, and even the starry sky trembled.
"It hurts so much to watch... Are the enemies so powerful that Boss Faustus can only resist them this way?"
Someone wiped away tears, his voice choked.
"Damn it... I’m actually crying."
A burly man with a rough build was now crying like a child.
Beyond the realm.
"He’s a ruthless one."
Jack’s emotions were equally complicated.
He was not shocked by Daniel’s strength, though Daniel was indeed powerful.
What truly made his heart tremble was that man’s ferocity—the ferocity to trade life for life and perish together with the enemy.
"Sigh..."
The Council of Races powerhouse also sighed softly.
By now, the Divine-grade powerhouses had already gone mad with slaughter.
Nearly two-thirds of the Starfarers had died.
Even if they truly seized this living world in the end, their races would basically be crippled.
"Kill him! Kill that ant!"
Despair surged up in the hearts of the Divine-grade powerhouses.
Despair for their races!
And all of this had been caused by that ant!
"Die, you damned bastard!"
Daniel was like a tireless machine—revive, self-destruct; revive again, self-destruct again.
He had no choice.
Because on his shoulders rested all of Earth, all of humanity.
"If you kill all of our people, don’t even think of preserving your plane!"
A Divine-grade powerhouse roared hoarsely.
"Are you trying to drag everyone down with you?"
Daniel’s rhythm of self-destruction suddenly stopped.
"Are you... retreating or not?"
His voice was like wind scraping out of an ice pit. There was no expression on his face at all, so cold it made one’s heart turn numb.
"If you insist on mutual destruction, then I’ll accompany you to the very end."
"Then let’s die together!"
Some Divine-grade powerhouses had already lost nearly all of their clansmen. One of them shouted at the top of his lungs,
"Come on! Let’s all be destroyed together!"
"I’ll drag you down with me!"
That Divine-grade powerhouse laughed miserably. The Immortal Singularity throughout his body ignited with a thunderous roar. Even his sage rank began burning fiercely.
He was burning his own life, burning his own soul, forcibly raising his Strength.
"All of you, die!"
He hurled all of his Strength toward Earth.
"Break—!"
But at that very instant...
In the chaotic void, a ring of ripples suddenly spread outward.
The flames on that insane Divine-grade powerhouse’s body went out instantly, as though someone had poured a bucket of ice water over his head.
All the Starfarer Divine-grade powerhouses within that ring of spatial ripples melted silently like snowmen beneath the blazing sun.
Sages had fallen!
Not a single sage from the more than one hundred Starfarer races remained.
They had no power to resist at all. In the blink of an eye, they died within that ring of ripples.
Jack and the Council of Races powerhouse stood up in shock at the same time.
"Oracle-grade."
The Council of Races powerhouse slowly spat out those three words.
"An Oracle-grade has actually descended in person... This..."
Jack’s voice carried a trace of trembling.
Daniel seemed to sense something and abruptly turned his head toward a certain direction.
Every Divine-grade powerhouse who had attacked him—
At this moment, not a single one remained.
All dead!
An existence capable of instantly killing Divine-grade powerhouses so effortlessly...
He stared fixedly at that patch of void without blinking.
Space seemed to be torn open by the gentlest force imaginable—smooth and silent.
Two figures walked out from within, neither hurried nor slow.

In that instant, the towering idol that stood high in the hearts of countless players collapsed with a thunderous crash.
Cries and roars exploded across Earth.
"Impossible..."
"How could Guild Leader die just like that?"

Faustus was dead?
No...

If he died, what would happen to humanity?

Right, we’re playing a game!

chapters.title: Chapter 249 -249-Golden Mountain’s Compulsory Invitation
paragraphs: The sacred auras surrounding the two great powerhouses had been restrained to the absolute limit. Their presence was no different from that of ordinary mortal beings.
One of them wore a black robe, and embroidered upon his chest was a dazzling Golden Mountain. His expression was calm as he glanced at Justin beside him.
Justin felt as though a rabbit had been stuffed into his chest, jumping wildly up and down. He carefully stole a look at that Tier-6 Oracle-grade existence, then gave an awkward smile and spoke.
"I have never been able to stand those who bully others by relying on their power. Just now, I lost control for a moment and acted a little too heavily."
When he said this, his expression was so natural that it was almost as if he were commenting on the weather.
Whether that Tier-6 Oracle-grade believed him or not was hard to say.
In any case, Justin himself almost believed it.
"No matter. They were merely a swarm of ants."
The Tier-6 Oracle-grade smiled and blinked, his gaze casually sweeping over the directions where the Astral Corsairs and the Council of Races were located.
Boom—!
Jack felt his mind buzz violently, turning completely blank.

It had only been a careless glance from that Oracle-grade powerhouse, yet Jack felt as though he had returned to the time when he had still been a mortal and had been locked onto by a legendary-grade powerhouse. Every hair on his body stood on end, and a chill ran down his spine.
"Go! Hurry up and go!"
Jack’s voice trembled as he desperately urged the powerhouses of the Council of Races to leave at once.
"No kidding. If we don’t run now, it’ll be too late..."
The powerhouse from the Council of Races gave a bitter smile.
"The one who came is actually a major figure from Golden Mountain."
"Just what kind of identity does that human brat have? How could he draw out an existence like this?"
In a fluster, he controlled the astral vessel and pushed it to maximum power, vanishing into the void.
On the Astral Corsairs’ side, several Divine-grade powerhouses simultaneously felt a chill rush from their tailbones straight to the crowns of their heads.
Only one thought remained in their minds.
Run!
Run as far away as possible!
"Something’s wrong with this place! Retreat, now!"
"It’s Golden Mountain! Two Oracle-grade existences actually came!"
"That human brat is far too bizarre... What the hell did we provoke?"
The Astral Corsairs, who were normally savage, arrogant, and unruly, no longer had even the slightest intention of plundering anything.
They did not dare to entertain so much as a single greedy thought. All they wished for now was to leave this patch of void alive.
With just one casual glance, that Oracle-grade existence had frightened this group of desperadoes into scattering in all directions.
Daniel looked at the two powerhouses without the slightest attempt to hide his scrutiny.
In his memories, only the ancient existence he had encountered when the World War had been forcefully initiated—the one capable of roaming the Time River—possessed the power to casually erase a Sage.
"These two... just what realm have they reached?"
He could not see through them.
The two powerhouses did not mind Daniel’s brazen gaze.

The Golden Mountain powerhouse’s eyes were filled with curiosity and investigation. Deep within his pupils, radiance flowed and shifted, as though he were activating some secret technique in an attempt to see through Daniel’s background.
As for Justin, his surface remained as calm as still water, yet his heart was surging with indescribable emotions.
"Justin, you came looking for him for something too, didn’t you?"
"How about... you go first?"
The Oracle-grade Angel turned his head, his tone carrying a hint of casualness.
"I would not dare overstep."
Justin lowered his posture to the extreme and spoke with utmost respect.
"Lord Angel, you have important matters to attend to. My small affair is nothing compared to yours. Naturally, you should go first."
Angel smiled. The light in his eyes slowly faded away, but inwardly, he was secretly shocked.
This little human fellow could not be seen through even by him.
How interesting!
Then Angel thought of Justin’s earlier secret intervention, and understanding immediately dawned in his heart.
This kid Justin definitely knew something about this human. Otherwise, he would never have killed those Divine-grade powerhouses for no reason just to sell him a favor.
"Faustus."
A warm smile appeared on Angel’s face.
When it came to things he could not see through, he always liked to leave himself plenty of room to maneuver. Therefore, his attitude was unexpectedly amiable.
"I am Angel, an envoy of Golden Mountain."
Golden Mountain?
That Golden Mountain, the strongest faction in the Canaan Starfield?
Daniel remembered seeing a brief introduction to it during a certain class change quest.
The starry sky of the myriad races was made up of galaxies. Above galaxies were star rivers. Above star rivers were starfields. And Golden Mountain was the most colossal behemoth in this starfield.
Golden Mountain...
It was terrifying!
"Greetings, Your Excellency."
Daniel gave a slight nod, neither servile nor arrogant.
"May I ask what instructions Your Excellency has come to give?"
"Do you know of the Starlight Rankings?"
In Angel’s hand, an invitation forged from some unknown material appeared out of thin air.
"I don’t know much."
Daniel glanced at the invitation and had already guessed something in his heart.
"It is a competition held by Golden Mountain once every so often, between powerhouses below the Divine-grade, correct?"
"More or less."
Angel smiled and shook his head.
"In the past, it was indeed hosted by Golden Mountain within its own domain. But this time, things are different."
His expression gradually turned solemn, and his voice also sank.

"This time, forces from other starfields have joined hands with Golden Mountain to co-host the first-ever cosmic Starlight Rankings Tournament! Every ranked powerhouse in the Canaan Starfield must participate."
Daniel’s eyes narrowed slightly.
Must participate!
Those two words carried an unquestionable sense of compulsion. They were also enough to show just how much importance Golden Mountain attached to this tournament.
Most likely, the matters hidden behind this tournament involved far more than a mere struggle between several starfields.
"I... am on the Starlight Rankings as well?"
Daniel raised his brows in slight surprise.
"Haha..."
The solemnity on Angel’s face instantly faded as he shook his head with a laugh.
"You still don’t know how famous you are now, do you?"
"You are the Starchosen of this generation who reached the summit of Cloudcrest Peak. Not only are you on the rankings, your position is not low either."
"Is that so?"
Daniel blinked, his interest now piqued.
"You are ranked twenty-seventh."
Angel explained, "Golden Mountain happens to be taking the top thirty this time, and you are on the list."
As he spoke, he handed over the invitation.
The invitation had seemed as light as a sheet of paper in Angel’s hand, but once it reached Daniel’s hand, it became so heavy that it nearly pressed his arm down.
"Rise."
Daniel used ninety percent of his strength before he barely managed to hold it steady.
His understanding of Angel’s strength deepened once again.
A trace of appreciation flashed through Angel’s eyes.
"I still need to deliver invitations to the other young powerhouses on the rankings, so I will not linger here any longer."
He looked at Daniel with expectation in his eyes.
"With this invitation in your possession, once the time comes, it will teleport you to the location designated by Golden Mountain."
"Prepare well. I shall take my leave first."
"Thank you for your guidance, Your Excellency."
Daniel nodded, thinking to himself that this had saved him quite a bit of trouble.
"Farewell, Your Excellency."
"Justin..."
Angel turned to look at Justin and gave a slight nod.
"Respectfully sending off Lord Angel."
Justin bowed respectfully.
Angel’s figure rapidly faded, then dispersed into the void like smoke.
Daniel looked at Justin curiously.
Strange...
Why did he feel as though something on this powerhouse’s body was connected to him somehow?
Golden Mountain had come looking for him because of the Starlight Rankings.
Then what had this powerhouse named Justin come looking for him for?
Seeing Angel leave, Justin’s heart suddenly relaxed.
But the moment he realized he had to face Daniel alone, he became somewhat at a loss again.
